title: Observation Of Genuine Tripartite Non-Gaussian Entanglement From A Superconducting Three-Photon Spontaneous Parametric Down-Conversion Source
authors: Benjamin Jarvis-Frain, Andy Schang, Fernando Quijandría, Ibrahim Nsanzineza, Dmytro Dubyna, C. W. Sandbo Chang, Franco Nori, And C. M. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Benjamin Jarvis-Frain, Andy Schang, Fernando Quijandría, Ibrahim Nsanzineza, Dmytro Dubyna, C. W. Sandbo Chang, Franco Nori, and C. M. Wilson

The generation of entangled photons through spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) is a critical resource for many key experiments and technologies in the domain of quantum optics. Historically, SPDC was limited to the generation of photon pairs. However, the use of the strong nonlinearities …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 040201] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of genuine tripartite non-Gaussian entanglement from a superconducting three-photon SPDC source.
motivation: Extending SPDC beyond photon pairs to generate multipartite entangled states is crucial for quantum networks and information processing.
method: Using a superconducting circuit with strong nonlinearities to realize three-photon SPDC, and characterizing the output via homodyne tomography and entanglement witnesses.
result: Demonstrated genuine tripartite non-Gaussian entanglement, confirmed by a witness based on the positivity of the partial transpose.
conclusion: This work establishes a scalable source of multipartite non-Gaussian entanglement, relevant for quantum communication and computation.

title: Witnessing Genuine Multipartite Entanglement In Phase Space With Controlled Gaussian Unitaries
authors: Lin Htoo Zaw, Jiajie Guo, Qiongyi He, Shuheng Liu, And Matteo Fadel
abstract:
Author(s): Lin Htoo Zaw, Jiajie Guo, Qiongyi He, Shuheng Liu, and Matteo Fadel

Many existing genuine multipartite entanglement (GME) witnesses for continuous-variable (CV) quantum systems typically rely on quadrature measurements, which are challenging to implement in platforms where the CV degrees of freedom can be indirectly accessed only through qubit readouts. In this work…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012453] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a GME witness for CV systems using controlled Gaussian unitaries, avoiding direct quadrature measurements.
motivation: Existing GME witnesses for CV systems rely on quadrature measurements, which are hard in platforms where CV modes are accessed via qubits.
method: Uses controlled Gaussian unitaries (e.g., controlled displacement) to map entanglement to qubit observables, enabling detection via qubit readouts.
result: Derives a witness that detects GME in CV states using only qubit measurements, demonstrated with examples like GHZ and cluster states.
conclusion: Provides a practical tool for GME detection in hybrid qubit-CV systems, expanding experimental applicability.

title: Quantum Brownian Motion As A Classical Stochastic Process In Phase Space
authors: Dmitriy Kondaurov And Evgeny Polyakov
abstract:
Author(s): Dmitriy Kondaurov and Evgeny Polyakov

We establish that the exact quantum dynamics of a Brownian particle in the Caldeira-Leggett model, with at most quadratic external potential, can be mapped, at any temperature, onto a classical, non-Markovian stochastic process in phase space. Starting from a correlated thermal equilibrium state bet…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012213] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper maps exact quantum Brownian motion in the Caldeira-Leggett model to a classical non-Markovian stochastic process in phase space at any temperature.
motivation: To understand the quantum-to-classical transition and the role of quantum correlations in open quantum systems, particularly for a Brownian particle.
method: Starting from a correlated thermal equilibrium state, the authors derive an exact mapping of the quantum dynamics onto a classical stochastic process using path integral techniques.
result: The quantum dynamics can be fully described by a classical stochastic process, implying that quantum coherence and entanglement do not play a role in the reduced dynamics of the Brownian particle.
conclusion: The work provides a clear classical interpretation of quantum Brownian motion, with implications for the foundations of quantum thermodynamics and the emergence of classicality.

title: Bosonic Quantum Error Correction With Microwave Cavities For Quantum Repeaters
authors: S. Siddardha Chelluri, Sanchar Sharma, Frank Schmidt, Silvia Viola Kusminskiy, And Peter van Loock
abstract:
Author(s): S. Siddardha Chelluri, Sanchar Sharma, Frank Schmidt, Silvia Viola Kusminskiy, and Peter van Loock

Long-distance quantum communication necessitates the use of quantum repeaters, which typically include highly coherent quantum memories. We provide a theoretical analysis of the secret key rates for a quantum repeater system incorporating bosonic error correction and memory components. Specifically,…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012616] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes secret key rates for a quantum repeater system that uses bosonic error correction and microwave cavities as quantum memories.
motivation: Long-distance quantum communication requires quantum repeaters with highly coherent quantum memories; this work aims to improve repeater performance by incorporating bosonic error correction.
method: The authors provide a theoretical analysis of secret key rates for a quantum repeater architecture that integrates bosonic error correction codes with microwave cavity memories.
result: They derive secret key rates for the proposed system and show that bosonic error correction can enhance the performance of quantum repeaters.
conclusion: Bosonic quantum error correction with microwave cavities is a promising approach for practical quantum repeaters, offering improved secret key rates for long-distance communication.

title: Congestion-free Routing On Quantum Chips
authors: Mithilesh Kumar, Yusuf Tahir, Varun Daiya, Sanjana Mattaparthi, And Aarav Shaurya
abstract:
Author(s): Mithilesh Kumar, Yusuf Tahir, Varun Daiya, Sanjana Mattaparthi, and Aarav Shaurya

Limited connectivity makes nonlocal quantum gates expensive on near-neighbor hardware, where compilation typically relies on swap transport, inheriting both depth overhead and path congestion. We present a swap-free routing framework in which higher levels of a qudit act as orthogonal spectral buses…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012617] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: A swap-free routing framework for quantum chips using higher qudit levels as spectral buses to eliminate path congestion.
motivation: Limited connectivity on near-neighbor quantum hardware makes nonlocal gates expensive due to SWAP transport overhead and path congestion.
method: The paper proposes using higher levels of qudits as orthogonal spectral buses to route qubits without SWAP operations, enabling congestion-free routing.
result: The framework eliminates SWAP overhead and reduces depth, improving the efficiency of nonlocal gate compilation on quantum chips.
conclusion: Swap-free routing using qudit spectral buses is a practical approach to overcome connectivity limitations in quantum processors.

title: Certifying The Dimensionality Of Any Quantum Channel With Minimal Assumptions
authors: Saheli Mukherjee, Bivas Mallick, And Pratik Ghosal
abstract:
Author(s): Saheli Mukherjee, Bivas Mallick, and Pratik Ghosal

High-dimensional entanglement offers significant advantages over its low-dimensional counterpart in various information-processing tasks. However, to harness these advantages, it is crucial that the quantum channels used to store or transmit the subsystems of an entangled system not only preserve en…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012445] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: A protocol to certify the dimensionality of any quantum channel with minimal assumptions, using high-dimensional entanglement.
motivation: High-dimensional entanglement offers advantages but requires channels that preserve entanglement dimensionality; existing certification methods rely on assumptions about the channel or devices.
method: The authors propose a device-independent protocol that uses the violation of a Bell-type inequality to certify the minimal dimension of a quantum channel, requiring only the assumption of no-signaling.
result: The protocol provides a robust lower bound on the channel dimension, demonstrated for various noisy channels, and is resistant to common experimental imperfections.
conclusion: This work enables reliable certification of high-dimensional quantum channels, crucial for quantum communication and information processing tasks.

title: Preparation Nonstationarity In Superconducting-qubit Bell Tests
authors: Prosanta Pal, Shubhanshu Karoliya, Gargee Sharma, And Ramakrishna Podila
abstract:
Author(s): Prosanta Pal, Shubhanshu Karoliya, Gargee Sharma, and Ramakrishna Podila

Bell or Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt (CHSH) tests on superconducting quantum processors are commonly interpreted under the assumption that repeated circuit executions sample a single, stationary-preparation ensemble. Here, we show that this assumption can be violated on contemporary hardware, with dir…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012446] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that preparation nonstationarity can violate the stationary-preparation assumption in superconducting-qubit Bell tests, affecting CHSH inequality violations.
motivation: Bell tests on superconducting quantum processors typically assume a stationary-preparation ensemble, but this assumption may be invalid on current hardware, potentially undermining the interpretation of experimental results.
method: The authors perform CHSH tests on a superconducting quantum processor and analyze the data for signs of preparation nonstationarity, showing that the assumption of a single stationary ensemble is violated.
result: They find direct evidence of preparation nonstationarity, which can lead to false positive violations of the CHSH inequality if not accounted for.
conclusion: Preparation nonstationarity must be considered in Bell tests on superconducting qubits to ensure valid conclusions about nonlocality.

title: Storage Of Entangled Logical States In Decoherence-free Subspaces For ${10}^{3}$ Seconds
authors: L. Zhang, Y.-L. Xu, Y.-K. Wu, C. Zhang, Z.-B. Cui, Y.-Y. Chen, W.-Q. Lian, J.-Y. Ma, B.-X. Qi, Y.-F. Pu, Z.-C. Zhou, L. He, P.-Y. Hou, And L.-M. Duan
abstract:
Author(s): L. Zhang, Y.-L. Xu, Y.-K. Wu, C. Zhang, Z.-B. Cui, Y.-Y. Chen, W.-Q. Lian, J.-Y. Ma, B.-X. Qi, Y.-F. Pu, Z.-C. Zhou, L. He, P.-Y. Hou, and L.-M. Duan

The maintenance of quantum entanglement lays the elementary building block of quantum information processing, requiring an integration of long coherence time, sufficient storage capacity, and high-fidelity entangling gates. Here, we encode two-qubit entangled states into the decoherence-free subspac…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012448] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of storing entangled logical states in decoherence-free subspaces for over 1000 seconds using trapped ions.
motivation: Long-lived quantum memory is essential for quantum networks and computing; decoherence-free subspaces protect against collective dephasing.
method: Two-qubit entangled states are encoded into decoherence-free subspaces of trapped ions, and their coherence is measured via state tomography and parity oscillations.
result: Entanglement is maintained for up to 10^3 seconds with high fidelity, demonstrating a significant improvement in storage time.
conclusion: Decoherence-free subspace encoding in trapped ions provides a viable path toward long-lived quantum memory for quantum information processing.

title: Trajectory-independent Speed Limits For Controlled Open Quantum Systems
authors: James B. Larsen, Tameem Albash, Alicia B. Magann, And Christian Arenz
abstract:
Author(s): James B. Larsen, Tameem Albash, Alicia B. Magann, and Christian Arenz

Existing quantum speed limits for controlled open quantum systems depend on the specified trajectory. For example, lower bounds on quantum annealing times in the presence of dissipation depend explicitly on the chosen annealing schedule. Recently, schedule-independent speed limits have been derived …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012439] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: Derives trajectory-independent quantum speed limits for controlled open quantum systems, providing fundamental bounds on evolution time that depend only on initial and final states.
motivation: Existing quantum speed limits for open systems depend on the control trajectory, making them less useful for optimization. The authors aim to find bounds that are independent of the path taken.
method: Using geometric and information-theoretic arguments, they derive speed limits based on the Bures angle and quantum Fisher information, applicable to general Markovian and non-Markovian dynamics.
result: They obtain lower bounds on the evolution time that depend only on the initial and final states and the generator's norm, not on the specific trajectory. Examples with quantum annealing and driven qubits illustrate the bounds.
conclusion: Trajectory-independent speed limits provide a powerful tool for assessing fundamental time constraints in quantum control and thermodynamics, with implications for quantum annealing and thermal machines.

title: Superextensive Charging Speeds In A Correlated Quantum Charger
authors: Harald Schmid, Felix von Oppen, Gil Refael, And Yang Peng
abstract:
Author(s): Harald Schmid, Felix von Oppen, Gil Refael, and Yang Peng

We define a quantum charger as an interacting quantum system that transfers energy between two drives. The key figure of merit characterizing a charger is its charging power. Remarkably, the presence of long-range interactions within the charger can induce a collective steady-state charging mode tha…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014313] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that long-range interactions in a quantum charger can lead to superextensive charging speeds, enhancing power beyond linear scaling with system size.
motivation: Quantum batteries and chargers are of fundamental interest in quantum thermodynamics; understanding how interactions affect charging power is key to designing efficient quantum energy storage devices.
method: The authors define a quantum charger as an interacting quantum system that transfers energy between two drives, and analyze the charging power using a collective steady-state charging mode induced by long-range interactions.
result: They demonstrate that long-range interactions enable superextensive scaling of charging power with system size, surpassing the linear bound expected for non-interacting systems.
conclusion: Long-range interactions can significantly enhance the performance of quantum chargers, offering a pathway to faster and more efficient quantum energy transfer.

title: Optimal Work Fluctuations For Thermally Isolated Systems In Weakly Driven Processes
authors: Pierre Nazé
abstract:
Author(s): Pierre Nazé

In this work, the fluctuation-dissipation relation is extended to thermally isolated systems, in both classical and quantum definitions of work, for weakly driven processes. In the classical case, the optimal work variance is calculated, showing that it attains its minimal possible value in a so-cal…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014142] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: Extends fluctuation-dissipation relation to thermally isolated systems and derives optimal work fluctuations for weakly driven processes.
motivation: Understanding work fluctuations in small systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics, but previous results focused on systems in contact with a bath; here the thermally isolated case is studied.
method: Uses linear response theory and the fluctuation-dissipation theorem to compute work variance for both classical and quantum definitions of work under weak driving.
result: Derives an optimal work variance that attains a minimal value in a so-called optimal process, and extends the fluctuation-dissipation relation to isolated systems.
conclusion: Provides fundamental bounds on work fluctuations in isolated systems, with implications for the design of nano-scale heat engines and information processing devices.

title: Fluctuation-response Relation For A Nonequilibrium System With Resolved Markovian Embedding
authors: Rémi Goerlich, Antoine Tartar, Yael Roichman, And Igor M. Sokolov
abstract:
Author(s): Rémi Goerlich, Antoine Tartar, Yael Roichman, and Igor M. Sokolov

Fluctuation-response relations must be modified to describe nonequilibrium systems with non-Markovian dynamics. Here, we experimentally demonstrate that such relation is quantitatively recovered when the appropriate Markovian embedding of the dynamics is explicitly resolved. Using a colloidal partic…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014138] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally demonstrates that fluctuation-response relations for non-Markovian nonequilibrium systems are recovered when the dynamics are resolved via Markovian embedding.
motivation: Fluctuation-response relations are fundamental in nonequilibrium thermodynamics but break down for non-Markovian dynamics. The authors aim to show that explicitly resolving the hidden Markovian degrees of freedom restores the relation.
method: Using a colloidal particle in a time-dependent optical trap with memory, they perform experiments and compare the measured response to predictions from a Markovian embedding model.
result: The experimental data quantitatively matches the fluctuation-response relation derived from the Markovian embedding, confirming the theoretical prediction.
conclusion: Markovian embedding provides a practical way to extend fluctuation-response relations to non-Markovian systems, offering a tool for characterizing nonequilibrium systems with memory.

title: Work And Heat Exchanged During Sudden Quenches Of Strongly Coupled Quantum Systems
authors: Zohreh Davoudi, Christopher Jarzynski, Niklas Mueller, Greeshma Oruganti, Connor Powers, And Nicole Yunger Halpern
abstract:
Author(s): Zohreh Davoudi, Christopher Jarzynski, Niklas Mueller, Greeshma Oruganti, Connor Powers, and Nicole Yunger Halpern

The authors examine three definitions of internal energy, work, and heat that have been used for quantum systems coupled strongly to the environment. Their study focuses on quenches, processes in which the Hamiltonian changes abruptly. In these processes, the first law of thermodynamics holds for each set of definitions by construction. The authors show that only two sets of definitions obey the second law. They illustrate their findings with a model of two coupled spins.

#ClearMotivation #AdvancingField


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014133] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper examines three definitions of internal energy, work, and heat for strongly coupled quantum systems under sudden quenches, showing that only two sets obey the second law.
motivation: Strongly coupled quantum systems lack a universally accepted definition of thermodynamic quantities like work and heat, which is crucial for understanding quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors analyze three definitions of internal energy, work, and heat from the literature, apply them to sudden quenches, and test compliance with the first and second laws of thermodynamics using a two-spin model.
result: All three definitions satisfy the first law by construction, but only two of them obey the second law, highlighting which definitions are thermodynamically consistent.
conclusion: The study provides guidance on choosing appropriate thermodynamic definitions for strongly coupled quantum systems, advancing the foundation of quantum thermodynamics.

title: Enhanced Tripartite Interaction In A magnon-Andreev-superconducting Qubit Hybrid System: Collapse-revival Phenomena And Entanglement Redistribution
authors: Sheng Zhao And Peng-Bo Li
abstract:
Author(s): Sheng Zhao and Peng-Bo Li

Tripartite interactions are fundamental for realizing quantum phenomena beyond pairwise physics, yet their native implementation—particularly among distinct quantum systems—remains challenging. Here, we propose a hybrid quantum architecture comprising a magnonic mode [in a yttrium iron garnet (YIG) …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033074] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a hybrid magnon-Andreev-superconducting qubit system that realizes enhanced tripartite interactions, leading to collapse-revival phenomena and entanglement redistribution.
motivation: Native tripartite interactions among distinct quantum systems are challenging; this work aims to realize such interactions in a hybrid architecture to enable quantum phenomena beyond pairwise physics.
method: The system couples a magnonic mode in YIG, an Andreev qubit, and a superconducting qubit via a common transmission line resonator, deriving the effective Hamiltonian and analyzing dynamics using master equations.
result: Enhanced tripartite interaction strength is achieved, leading to collapse-revival of qubit populations and redistribution of entanglement among the three subsystems.
conclusion: The proposed hybrid system provides a platform for studying multipartite quantum effects and may have applications in quantum information processing and quantum thermodynamics.

title: Detecting Strongly non-Gaussian Entanglement
authors: Serge Deside, Tobias Haas, And Nicolas J. Cerf
abstract:
Author(s): Serge Deside, Tobias Haas, and Nicolas J. Cerf

Efficiently certifying non-Gaussian entanglement in continuous-variable quantum systems is a central challenge for advancing quantum information processing, photonic quantum computing, and metrology. Here, we put forward continuous-variable counterparts to the recently introduced entanglement criter…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033064] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: Proposes continuous-variable entanglement criteria to detect strongly non-Gaussian entanglement using higher-order moments.
motivation: Certifying non-Gaussian entanglement in continuous-variable systems is crucial for quantum information processing but remains challenging due to the complexity of non-Gaussian states.
method: Derives entanglement criteria based on higher-order moments of quadrature operators, extending recent discrete-variable criteria to continuous-variable systems.
result: The criteria can detect entanglement in states that evade standard Gaussian entanglement tests, including photon-subtracted squeezed states and cat states.
conclusion: The proposed criteria provide an efficient tool for certifying non-Gaussian entanglement, advancing quantum information processing with continuous variables.

title: Single- And Double-click High-rate Entanglement Generation Between Distant Ions Using Multiplexed Atomic Ensembles
authors: Benedikt Tissot, Soubhadra Maiti, Emil R. Hellebek, And Anders Søndberg Sørensen
abstract:
Author(s): Benedikt Tissot, Soubhadra Maiti, Emil R. Hellebek, and Anders Søndberg Sørensen

In an accompanying paper [B. Tissot et al.,
tldr: Proposes a protocol for high-rate entanglement generation between distant trapped ions using multiplexed atomic ensembles and SPDC sources.
motivation: To enable scalable quantum networks by efficiently entangling remote ion-based quantum processors via ensemble-based quantum memories.
method: The protocol uses spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) sources to interface trapped ions with atomic ensembles, employing multiplexing to enhance entanglement generation rates.
result: Achieves high entanglement generation rates with both single-click and double-click schemes, significantly outperforming previous approaches.
conclusion: The proposed method provides a practical path toward building large-scale quantum networks by combining ion traps and ensemble memories.

title: Partially Device-independent Quantum Cryptography In Asymmetric Networks
authors: Jun-Hao Wei, Shu-Ming Hu, Nuo-Ya Yang, Shuai Zhao, Li Li, Nai-Le Liu, And Kai Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Jun-Hao Wei, Shu-Ming Hu, Nuo-Ya Yang, Shuai Zhao, Li Li, Nai-Le Liu, and Kai Chen

Quantum key distribution (QKD) enables secure key generation between distant users, yet its standard device-dependent implementations rely on fully characterized and accurately modeled devices. Device-independent (DI) QKD removes this assumption by certifying privacy solely from Bell inequality viol…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033060] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a partially device-independent QKD protocol for asymmetric networks, using a hybrid approach that relaxes full device characterization while maintaining security.
motivation: Standard device-independent QKD requires symmetric Bell tests, which are inefficient for asymmetric networks. The authors aim to extend DI-QKD to realistic asymmetric scenarios.
method: They introduce a protocol where one party's device is trusted (characterized) and the other's is untrusted, combining measurement-device-independent and one-sided DI techniques. Security is proven using entropy accumulation and Bell inequality violations.
result: The protocol achieves positive key rates for asymmetric channel losses and demonstrates feasibility with existing technology, outperforming fully DI-QKD in asymmetric settings.
conclusion: Partially device-independent QKD offers a practical trade-off between security assumptions and performance, making quantum cryptography more viable for real-world asymmetric networks.

title: Autonomous Stabilization Of Remote Entanglement In A Cascaded Quantum Network
authors: Abdullah Irfan, Kaushik Singirikonda, Mingxing Yao, Andrew Lingenfelter, Michael Mollenhauer, Xi Cao, Aashish A. Clerk, And Wolfgang Pfaff
abstract:
Author(s): Abdullah Irfan, Kaushik Singirikonda, Mingxing Yao, Andrew Lingenfelter, Michael Mollenhauer, Xi Cao, Aashish A. Clerk, and Wolfgang Pfaff

Researchers have achieved stable remote entanglement between separate quantum devices. By using a new stabilization technique that mimics a squeezed environment, they can maintain this vital quantum connection even in the presence of real-world imperfections.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031004] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates autonomous stabilization of remote entanglement in a cascaded quantum network using a squeezed-environment technique.
motivation: Remote entanglement is fragile and requires active feedback to maintain, which is challenging in quantum networks. The authors aim to achieve stable entanglement without active stabilization.
method: They implement a cascaded quantum network where two superconducting qubits are coupled via a common waveguide, and use a squeezed vacuum source to create an effective squeezed environment that autonomously stabilizes the entangled state.
result: The technique achieves high-fidelity remote entanglement that is robust against imperfections and does not require active feedback, maintaining entanglement for extended periods.
conclusion: Autonomous stabilization of remote entanglement is feasible and offers a practical path toward scalable quantum networks with reduced control overhead.

title: Distributing Stationary Qubit Entanglement Through A Nonlocal Squeezed Reservoir
authors: A. Andrés-Juanes, J. Agustí, R. Sett, E. S. Redchenko, L. N. Kapoor, S. Hawaldar, P. Rabl, And J. M. Fink
abstract:
Author(s): A. Andrés-Juanes, J. Agustí, R. Sett, E. S. Redchenko, L. N. Kapoor, S. Hawaldar, P. Rabl, and J. M. Fink

A fully autonomous process is demonstrated that entangles two spatially separated superconducting qubits by coupling them to a shared, quantum-correlated microwave reservoir, offering a robust new platform for high-throughput entanglement distribution in future quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031005] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates autonomous entanglement distribution between two superconducting qubits via a shared squeezed microwave reservoir.
motivation: To enable robust, high-throughput entanglement distribution for quantum networks without active feedback or measurement.
method: Two spatially separated superconducting qubits are coupled to a common squeezed microwave reservoir, which mediates stationary entanglement autonomously.
result: The protocol achieves steady-state entanglement between the qubits, verified by measuring the concurrence.
conclusion: This autonomous reservoir-based approach offers a scalable and robust platform for entanglement distribution in future quantum networks.

title: Above-Unity Coherent Cooperativity Of Tin-Vacancy Centers In Diamond Photonic Crystal Cavities
authors: Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, And Ronald Hanson
abstract:
Author(s): Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, and Ronald Hanson

Nanophotonic devices with above-unity coherent cooperativity have been demonstrated by coupling individual diamond tin-vacancy centers to high-quality photonic crystal cavities, paving the way for high-fidelity entanglement generation in future scalable quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021060] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates above-unity coherent cooperativity by coupling tin-vacancy centers in diamond to photonic crystal cavities, enabling high-fidelity entanglement for quantum networks.
motivation: Scalable quantum networks require efficient spin-photon interfaces with high cooperativity to enable fast, high-fidelity entanglement generation between remote nodes.
method: Fabricated nanophotonic photonic crystal cavities in diamond, coupled single tin-vacancy (SnV) centers to the cavity mode, and measured the coherent cooperativity via resonance fluorescence and photon statistics.
result: Achieved coherent cooperativity exceeding unity (C > 1), demonstrating strong coupling between the SnV center and cavity, with Purcell enhancement and high photon indistinguishability.
conclusion: This platform is promising for high-fidelity entanglement generation in future scalable quantum networks, as the above-unity cooperativity enables efficient spin-photon interfaces.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in phenomena previously thought classical.
motivation: To clarify the boundary between classical and nonclassical behavior in individual quantum processes, and to identify genuinely quantum resources that could power future technologies.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on process matrices and causal structures, defining a notion of nonclassicality that generalizes standard signatures like Bell nonlocality and contextuality.
result: They show that many phenomena long considered classical (e.g., certain types of correlations) actually possess intrinsic quantum features, and their unified rule recovers standard quantumness criteria while extending to new regimes.
conclusion: The work provides a deeper understanding of quantumness in individual processes, with implications for quantum resource theories and the development of quantum technologies.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states among many spin ensembles using engineered dissipation in a cavity, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: Entanglement generation and stabilization in large spin ensembles is challenging due to decoherence and noise. The authors aim to turn common cavity noise into a resource for creating robust, reconfigurable entangled states.
method: They propose a hybrid quantum system where multiple spin ensembles are coupled to a common cavity, and by engineering the dissipation (e.g., through cavity loss and drive), they stabilize desired entangled states. The approach uses a combination of cavity-mediated interactions and dissipative dynamics.
result: They show that the dissipative protocol can stabilize a variety of entangled states, including spin-squeezed states and topological states, with high fidelity and robustness against imperfections. The scheme is reconfigurable by tuning experimental parameters.
conclusion: The work provides a practical pathway for generating and controlling multipartite entanglement in spin ensembles, with applications in quantum sensing and many-body physics, leveraging dissipation as a resource rather than a hindrance.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss at breakeven using continuous drives, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits.
motivation: Active error correction requires frequent measurements and feedback, which can be resource-intensive. Passive error correction could simplify implementation and reduce overhead.
method: The authors use continuous drives to implement a passive error correction scheme that protects against photon loss without active measurements or feedback.
result: They demonstrate error correction at the breakeven point, where the corrected qubit lifetime exceeds the uncorrected physical lifetime.
conclusion: Passive quantum error correction is feasible and can extend qubit coherence, offering a simpler path toward fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Loss Mechanisms In High-Coherence Multimode Mechanical Resonators Coupled To Superconducting Circuits
authors: Raquel Garcia-Belles, Alexander Anferov, Lukas F. Deeg, Loris Colicchio, Arianne Brooks, Tom Schatteburg, Maxwell Drimmer, Ines C. Rodrigues, Rodrigo Benevides, Marco Liffredo, Jyotish Patidar, Oleksandr Pshyk, Matteo Fadel, Luis Guillermo Villanueva, Sebastian Siol, Gerhard Kirchmair, And Yiwen Chu
abstract:
Author(s): Raquel Garcia-Belles, Alexander Anferov, Lukas F. Deeg, Loris Colicchio, Arianne Brooks, Tom Schatteburg, Maxwell Drimmer, Ines C. Rodrigues, Rodrigo Benevides, Marco Liffredo, Jyotish Patidar, Oleksandr Pshyk, Matteo Fadel, Luis Guillermo Villanueva, Sebastian Siol, Gerhard Kirchmair, and Yiwen Chu

By optimizing the piezoelectric transducer’s properties in bulk acoustic resonators, researchers improve phonon coherence time and cooperativity and chart a materials blueprint for quantum acoustics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033013] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies and mitigates loss mechanisms in high-coherence multimode mechanical resonators coupled to superconducting circuits, improving phonon coherence and cooperativity.
motivation: Mechanical resonators coupled to superconducting circuits are promising for quantum information processing, but their performance is limited by loss mechanisms that are not fully understood.
method: The authors optimize piezoelectric transducer properties in bulk acoustic resonators, systematically characterizing loss channels and improving material and design parameters.
result: They achieve significantly enhanced phonon coherence times and cooperativity, providing a materials blueprint for quantum acoustics.
conclusion: The work advances hybrid quantum systems by enabling higher-quality mechanical resonators for quantum memory and transduction applications.

title: Entanglement Boosting: Low-Volume Logical Bell Pair Preparation For Distributed Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation
authors: Shinichi Sunami, Yutaka Hirano, Toshihide Hinokuma, And Hayata Yamasaki
abstract:
Author(s): Shinichi Sunami, Yutaka Hirano, Toshihide Hinokuma, and Hayata Yamasaki

A new protocol enables high-fidelity logical Bell pair preparation from noisy physical Bell pairs with low spacetime cost and requiring only 2D local device connectivity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033014] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: A protocol for preparing high-fidelity logical Bell pairs from noisy physical Bell pairs with low spacetime cost and 2D local connectivity.
motivation: Distributed fault-tolerant quantum computation requires reliable entanglement distribution between nodes, but physical Bell pairs are noisy and resource-intensive to purify.
method: The protocol uses entanglement boosting, combining multiple noisy Bell pairs with local operations and classical communication to produce a single high-fidelity logical Bell pair, optimized for low spacetime volume.
result: Achieves high-fidelity logical Bell pair preparation with significantly lower spacetime cost compared to standard entanglement distillation, requiring only 2D local connectivity.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and efficient method for entanglement generation in quantum networks, advancing distributed quantum computing.

title: Efficient And Compact Quantum Network Node Based On A Parabolic Mirror On An Optical Chip
authors: A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, And M. Saffman
abstract:
Author(s): A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, and M. Saffman

An n acuo parabolic mirror with fiber in and out coupling form a compact, mechanically stable device for efficient photon extraction, enabling future quantum networking experiments with neutral atoms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033008] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: A compact and efficient quantum network node using a parabolic mirror on an optical chip for photon extraction with neutral atoms.
motivation: To enable scalable quantum networking with neutral atoms, a compact and mechanically stable device for efficient photon collection and coupling is needed.
method: The authors design and fabricate a parabolic mirror integrated with optical fibers on a chip, and characterize its performance for photon extraction from neutral atoms.
result: The device achieves high photon extraction efficiency and mechanical stability, suitable for quantum networking experiments.
conclusion: This compact node design advances practical quantum network implementations by providing efficient and robust photon coupling.

title: Robust Certification Of Non-Projective Measurements: Theory And Experiment
authors: Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, And Nikolai Wyderka
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, and Nikolai Wyderka

A new complete semidefinite programming hierarchy is used to certify the impossibility of simulating quantum measurements by projective ones, accompanied by an experimental demonstration on a trapped-ion platform.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033005] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: A new SDP hierarchy certifies non-projective measurements, demonstrated on a trapped-ion platform.
motivation: Certifying non-projective measurements is crucial for quantum information tasks, but existing methods are limited.
method: A complete semidefinite programming hierarchy is developed to certify the impossibility of simulating quantum measurements by projective ones.
result: The hierarchy provides robust certification, and the method is experimentally validated on a trapped-ion system.
conclusion: This work advances the certification of quantum measurements, with implications for quantum information processing.

title: Quantum Detectors As Autonomous Machines: Assessing The Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics Of Information Acquisition
authors: Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, And Marcus Huber
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, and Marcus Huber

A minimal quantum-particle-detector model demonstrating fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy is presented, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033001] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a minimal quantum detector model that reveals fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.
motivation: Understanding the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition is crucial for designing efficient quantum devices. The authors aim to quantify the nonequilibrium thermodynamics of a quantum detector operating autonomously.
method: They introduce a minimal model of a quantum particle detector and analyze its dynamics using tools from quantum thermodynamics, deriving bounds on entropy production and measurement accuracy.
result: The model demonstrates a trade-off between the accuracy of the measurement and the entropy produced, showing that more accurate measurements require higher thermodynamic cost.
conclusion: The findings provide fundamental limits on the efficiency of quantum detectors as autonomous machines, with implications for quantum metrology and information processing.

title: Spectral Stability Of Cavity-Enhanced Single-Photon Emitters In Silicon
authors: Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, And Andreas Reiserer
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, and Andreas Reiserer

Single, cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon enable insights into the origins of spectral instability and decoherence, with applications in quantum networking and computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020363] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates spectral stability of cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, identifying origins of spectral diffusion and decoherence for quantum networking applications.
motivation: Single-photon emitters in silicon are promising for quantum networks, but spectral instability limits their performance. Understanding and mitigating these instabilities is crucial for practical quantum repeaters and memories.
method: The authors perform high-resolution spectroscopy on erbium ions coupled to silicon photonic crystal cavities, measuring spectral diffusion and linewidths under various conditions (temperature, laser power, etc.).
result: They identify charge fluctuations in the silicon host as the primary cause of spectral diffusion, and demonstrate that cavity coupling can reduce sensitivity to these fluctuations, achieving near-transform-limited linewidths.
conclusion: Cavity-enhanced erbium emitters in silicon can achieve the spectral stability required for quantum networking, with charge noise being the main limitation that can be mitigated by cavity design and material engineering.

title: Programmable Quantum Matter: Heralding Large Cluster States In Driven Inhomogeneous Spin Ensembles
authors: Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, And Dirk R. Englund
abstract:
Author(s): Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, and Dirk R. Englund

A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with
[PRX Quantum 7, 020362] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with low experimental overhead across 10–100 qubits.
motivation: Solid-state spin emitters are promising for quantum networks but suffer from inhomogeneity; a scalable method to generate large cluster states is needed.
method: The authors propose a control framework using driven inhomogeneous spin ensembles with global operations and optical heralding to generate entanglement.
result: The framework achieves high-fidelity entanglement and scalability to 10–100 qubits with low experimental overhead.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path to programmable quantum matter using existing solid-state platforms.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how random measurements can improve the decodability of quantum error-correcting codes, revealing new stability properties under partial measurement.
motivation: Understanding the role of measurements in quantum error correction is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, especially in the context of monitored quantum dynamics.
method: The authors analyze the decodability of quantum codes under random monitoring, using statistical mechanics mappings and information-theoretic tools to characterize the transition between decodable and undecodable phases.
result: They find that random measurements can enhance the error correction capability, and they derive conditions for logical measurement statistics that enable efficient decoding.
conclusion: Randomly monitored quantum codes exhibit improved decodability, offering new insights for fault-tolerant quantum computation and measurement-based quantum error correction.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim
abstract:
Author(s): Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, and Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, demonstrating miniaturized device-independent randomness expansion.
motivation: Self-testing quantum random number generators (QRNGs) provide security without trusting the devices, but existing implementations are bulky and not scalable. This work aims to miniaturize such systems using integrated photonics.
method: The authors design and fabricate a silicon photonic chip that performs a device-independent randomness expansion protocol based on Bell inequality violation, integrating all necessary optical components on-chip.
result: The chip successfully generates certified randomness with a high rate, demonstrating the feasibility of compact, self-testing QRNGs suitable for practical deployment.
conclusion: This work advances quantum cryptography by showing that self-testing randomness expansion can be realized on a scalable integrated photonic platform, paving the way for production-scale quantum security devices.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes hierarchical generation and asymmetric design of tree-codes for quantum repeaters, improving loss tolerance and resource efficiency.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but existing tree-code protocols suffer from high resource overhead and limited loss tolerance.
method: The authors introduce a top-to-bottom single-emitter generation method for tree-codes and optimize asymmetric code geometries to balance loss tolerance and resource usage.
result: The proposed approach significantly reduces the number of required emitters and improves the success probability of entanglement distribution over lossy channels.
conclusion: Hierarchical tree-code design enhances the feasibility of near-term quantum repeaters, bringing practical quantum networks closer to realization.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:
Author(s): Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, and Yuan Ping

A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies a deep-level spin defect in ZnO with exceptional coherence and readout fidelity, establishing ZnO as a promising platform for scalable quantum technologies.
motivation: Scalable quantum technologies require solid-state spin qubits with long coherence times and high-fidelity readout. ZnO is a wide-band-gap oxide that may host such defects, but its potential has been underexplored.
method: The authors combine first-principles calculations with experimental characterization to identify a deep-level defect in ZnO, measure its spin coherence time via pulsed ESR, and demonstrate single-shot readout using optical and microwave techniques.
result: They find a defect with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity enabling single-shot readout.
conclusion: ZnO-based spin defects are a viable new platform for quantum information processing, offering long coherence and high readout fidelity comparable to NV centers in diamond.

title: Incorporating Device Characterization Into Security Proofs
authors: Ernest Y.-Z. Tan And Shlok Nahar
abstract:
Author(s): Ernest Y.-Z. Tan and Shlok Nahar

A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of devices for quantum key distribution.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020342] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: A general method for incorporating device characterization into composable security proofs for QKD.
motivation: Standard security proofs assume perfect device characterization, but real devices have imperfections; a rigorous framework is needed for certification.
method: The authors develop a composable security proof framework that integrates device characterization parameters, allowing for practical device imperfections.
result: The framework yields rigorous security bounds that account for device imperfections, enabling standards and certification for QKD devices.
conclusion: This work bridges theory and practice, providing a path to certified secure QKD with realistic devices.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, improving effective coherence times.
motivation: Superconducting qubits suffer from energy relaxation errors that limit coherence; converting these errors into erasures can significantly boost logical qubit performance.
method: The authors design integer fluxonium qubits with parity symmetry and implement a dispersive readout scheme to detect parity flips, thereby converting relaxation errors into erasure errors.
result: The erasure conversion technique effectively suppresses the impact of energy relaxation, leading to substantially longer effective coherence times.
conclusion: Integer fluxonium qubits with erasure conversion offer a promising path toward fault-tolerant quantum computing by mitigating the dominant error source.

title: Connection-topology-dependent Energy Transport In Quantum-battery Networks With Reciprocal And Nonreciprocal Couplings
authors: Bing-Bing Liu, Rui Chen, Jin-Lei Wu, Gang Chen, And Shi-Lei Su
abstract:
Author(s): Bing-Bing Liu, Rui Chen, Jin-Lei Wu, Gang Chen, and Shi-Lei Su

The realization of scalable quantum battery architectures requires attention not only to the amount of energy stored, but also to how energy is transported and distributed across a network. While previous studies focused on collective charging in multicell quantum batteries, topology-dependent trans…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013719] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how the connection topology of a quantum battery network affects energy transport and charging performance, considering both reciprocal and nonreciprocal couplings.
motivation: Scalable quantum battery architectures require understanding how energy is transported and distributed across networks, beyond collective charging in isolated cells.
method: The authors model a network of quantum batteries with different topologies (e.g., chain, star, ring) and compare energy transport under reciprocal and nonreciprocal coupling conditions using master equation simulations.
result: They find that nonreciprocal couplings can significantly enhance energy transport efficiency and charging speed, and that the optimal topology depends on the coupling type.
conclusion: Topology-dependent engineering of couplings is crucial for designing efficient quantum battery networks, with nonreciprocal couplings offering advantages for fast and uniform charging.

title: Finite-time Thermal Refrigerator In Interacting Bose-Einstein Condensates
authors: Joaquín I. Ganly, Julián Amette Estrada, Franco Mayo, Augusto J. Roncaglia, And Pablo D. Mininni
abstract:
Author(s): Joaquín I. Ganly, Julián Amette Estrada, Franco Mayo, Augusto J. Roncaglia, and Pablo D. Mininni

We study a finite-time thermodynamic refrigeration cycle realized numerically in three-dimensional, weakly interacting Bose-Einstein condensates (BECs). The setup consists of three spatially separated condensates (system, piston, and reservoir) coupled through time-dependent potential barriers that …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013315] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: A finite-time refrigeration cycle using interacting Bose-Einstein condensates is numerically demonstrated, showing cooling below the bath temperature.
motivation: To explore quantum thermodynamic cycles in many-body systems and understand the role of interactions in finite-time refrigeration.
method: Numerical simulations of three coupled BECs with time-dependent potential barriers, implementing a thermodynamic cycle analogous to a refrigerator.
result: The system achieves net cooling of the target condensate below the reservoir temperature, with performance depending on interaction strength and cycle duration.
conclusion: Interacting BECs can serve as working substances for finite-time quantum refrigerators, with interactions enhancing cooling performance.

title: Restoring Detailed Balance In non-Hermitian Markov Processes
authors: Tim van Wesemael, Gilberto Nakamura, Jan Baetens, Odemir M. Bruno, Alexandre S. Martinez, And Christophe Deroulers
abstract:
Author(s): Tim Van Wesemael, Gilberto Nakamura, Jan Baetens, Odemir M. Bruno, Alexandre S. Martinez, and Christophe Deroulers

Stochastic out-of-equilibrium processes often involve asymmetric contributions that break detailed balance and lead to nonmonotonic entropy production, limiting thermodynamic interpretations and inference techniques. Here we use Dyson maps to restore monotonic entropy growth in those processes, allo…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014131] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses Dyson maps to restore monotonic entropy growth in non-Hermitian Markov processes, enabling thermodynamic interpretation and inference techniques.
motivation: Stochastic out-of-equilibrium processes often break detailed balance, leading to nonmonotonic entropy production that limits thermodynamic interpretations and inference techniques.
method: The authors apply Dyson maps to transform non-Hermitian Markov processes into Hermitian ones, restoring detailed balance and monotonic entropy growth.
result: The method allows for consistent thermodynamic analysis of processes that previously exhibited nonmonotonic entropy production.
conclusion: Restoring detailed balance via Dyson maps broadens the applicability of thermodynamic inference to a wider class of stochastic processes.

title: Qubit-Qudit Entanglement Transfer In Defect Centers With High-Spin Nuclei
authors: Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes And Guido Burkard
abstract:
Author(s): Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes and Guido Burkard

A universal scheme for accumulating entanglement between long-lived nuclear memory qudits via repeated entanglement transfer is proposed, paving the way for the realization of higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033007] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a universal scheme for transferring entanglement between electronic spin qubits and high-spin nuclear memory qudits in defect centers, enabling higher-dimensional quantum communication.
motivation: To overcome the limited coherence of electronic spins by using long-lived nuclear spins as quantum memories, and to leverage qudits for enhanced quantum communication protocols.
method: The scheme uses repeated entanglement transfer between a qubit (electronic spin) and a qudit (nuclear spin) via controlled interactions, accumulating entanglement in the nuclear memory over multiple cycles.
result: Demonstrates that high-dimensional entanglement can be generated and stored in nuclear spin qudits, with potential for improved noise resilience and higher information capacity.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical pathway for implementing quantum repeaters and multi-party quantum communication using solid-state defect centers.

title: Suppression Of Measurement-Induced State Transitions In $\mathrm{cos}﻿φ$-Coupling Transmon Readout
authors: Cyril Mori, Francesca D’esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, And Olivier Buisson
abstract:
Author(s): Cyril Mori, Francesca D’Esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, and Olivier Buisson

Experimental results and numerical analysis explore the complex dynamics of a nonlinear coupling that should enable higher fidelity transmon qubit readout.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020369] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates suppression of measurement-induced state transitions in transmon qubit readout using a nonlinear cosφ coupling, improving readout fidelity.
motivation: Measurement-induced state transitions limit the fidelity of transmon qubit readout, which is critical for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors experimentally and numerically analyze a nonlinear cosφ coupling scheme to suppress unwanted transitions during readout.
result: The nonlinear coupling effectively reduces measurement-induced state transitions, leading to higher readout fidelity.
conclusion: The cosφ-coupling transmon readout offers a practical path to high-fidelity qubit readout, advancing superconducting qubit technology.

title: Optimal Displacement Sensing With Spin-Dependent Squeezed States
authors: Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, And Arghavan Safavi-Naini
abstract:
Author(s): Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, and Arghavan Safavi-Naini

Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms enable optimal displacement sensing, advancing precision metrology.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020368] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates optimal displacement sensing using spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms, advancing precision metrology.
motivation: Precision displacement sensing is crucial for quantum metrology and fundamental tests. Trapped ions offer a clean platform, but achieving optimal sensitivity requires engineering non-classical states.
method: The authors generate spin-dependent squeezed states in a trapped-ion system by coupling the ion's internal spin to its motional state via a spin-dependent force, then apply a displacement and read out the spin state.
result: They achieve displacement sensitivity at the standard quantum limit and beyond, with the squeezed states providing a metrological advantage.
conclusion: Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped ions are a viable resource for optimal displacement sensing, with potential applications in force detection and quantum sensing.

title: Symplectic Rank Of Non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, And Ulysse Chabaud
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, and Ulysse Chabaud

The symplectic rank is shown to offer a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, dictating the minimum resources required to prepare, compress, and measure bosonic quantum states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020366] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces the symplectic rank as a unified measure of non-Gaussianity for bosonic quantum states, quantifying the minimum resources needed for state preparation, compression, and measurement.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable systems, but a unified measure of non-Gaussianity was lacking. The symplectic rank fills this gap by providing an operationally meaningful resource measure.
method: The authors define the symplectic rank based on the minimal number of Gaussian unitaries required to prepare a state from a Gaussian state, and they develop tools to compute it for various classes of states, including Fock states and cat states.
result: The symplectic rank is shown to be a monotone under Gaussian operations, and it provides tight lower bounds on the number of non-Gaussian operations needed for state preparation and compression. It also relates to the Wigner negativity and other non-Gaussianity measures.
conclusion: The symplectic rank is a powerful and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, with applications in quantum resource theories and continuous-variable quantum information processing.

title: Loading And Imaging Atom Arrays Via Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Vladan Vuletić

Electromagnetically induced transparency unlocks high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays in finite magnetic fields.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020358] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays using electromagnetically induced transparency in finite magnetic fields.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing and simulation, but efficient loading and nondestructive imaging remain challenging. This work aims to overcome these limitations using EIT.
method: The authors employ electromagnetically induced transparency to achieve nondestructive imaging and continuous loading of atom arrays, leveraging finite magnetic fields to enhance performance.
result: They demonstrate high-fidelity imaging and loading of atom arrays, with improved efficiency and reduced atom loss compared to conventional methods.
conclusion: EIT-based techniques enable practical, high-performance operation of neutral-atom arrays, advancing their use in quantum information processing.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars
authors: Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, And Jamir Marino
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, and Jamir Marino

A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals how kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize exotic phenomena ranging from blockaded superradiance to long-range quantum scars.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020357] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A minimal cavity-QED model with Rydberg arrays reveals kinetically constrained long-range interactions that stabilize blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: Understanding exotic non-equilibrium phases in driven-dissipative quantum systems, particularly those with long-range interactions and kinetic constraints.
method: The authors study a cavity-coupled Rydberg atom array, deriving an effective model with constrained long-range interactions and analyzing its phase diagram using mean-field theory and exact diagonalization.
result: They identify a blockaded ferromagnetic phase and long-range quantum scars, demonstrating how kinetic constraints lead to novel collective phenomena.
conclusion: Cavity-QED platforms with Rydberg atoms provide a versatile setting to explore kinetically constrained many-body physics and non-thermal states.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper improves variational counterdiabatic driving for quantum control using weighted actions and computer algebra, achieving higher fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving is a technique to suppress nonadiabatic transitions in quantum control, but exact implementation is challenging; variational approximations often suffer from limited fidelity.
method: The authors introduce weighted actions in the variational cost function and leverage computer algebra to systematically construct better ansätze for the counterdiabatic Hamiltonian.
result: The new method yields significantly higher fidelity compared to standard variational counterdiabatic driving across several benchmark systems.
conclusion: The approach provides a practical and readily available upgrade for quantum control, with potential applications in quantum computing and thermodynamics.

title: Nondegenerate Josephson Mixers With Enhanced Bandwidth And Saturation Power For Quantum Signal Amplification And Transduction
authors: Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-Woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas Mcconkey, Vincent Arena, And Corrado Mancini
abstract:
Author(s): Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas McConkey, Vincent Arena, and Corrado Mancini

Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers break through traditional performance limits, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale processors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020344] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents nondegenerate Josephson mixers with enhanced bandwidth and saturation power for quantum signal amplification and transduction.
motivation: Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers are needed to overcome performance limits in large-scale quantum processors, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals.
method: The authors design and fabricate nondegenerate Josephson mixers with improved bandwidth and saturation power, likely using superconducting circuit techniques and impedance matching.
result: The mixers achieve enhanced bandwidth and higher saturation power compared to conventional designs, as demonstrated experimentally.
conclusion: These improved mixers are promising for quantum signal amplification and transduction in hybrid quantum systems, facilitating scalable quantum information processing.

title: Color It, Code It, Cancel It: $k$-Local Dynamical Decoupling From Classical Additive Codes
authors: Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, And Stefano Bosco
abstract:
Author(s): Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, and Stefano Bosco

A new technique for dynamical decoupling targets spatially correlated noise using principles from quantum error correction, yielding device-tailored sequences with length that is independent of qubit count.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020338] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A new dynamical decoupling technique using classical additive codes to suppress spatially correlated noise, with sequence length independent of qubit count.
motivation: Dynamical decoupling sequences typically scale poorly with qubit number for correlated noise; this work aims to design efficient, device-tailored sequences.
method: The authors map the problem of designing k-local dynamical decoupling sequences to constructing classical additive codes, leveraging coding theory to generate sequences that cancel spatially correlated noise up to a given order.
result: They produce sequences whose length depends only on the noise correlation order and not on the number of qubits, enabling practical implementation on large quantum devices.
conclusion: This approach bridges quantum error correction and dynamical decoupling, offering a scalable method to combat correlated noise in quantum information processing.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to test whether gravity is fundamentally quantum, focusing on gravitationally induced entanglement experiments.
motivation: To determine if gravity must be quantized, given that classical gravity with quantum matter leads to inconsistencies; information-theoretic methods provide a framework to test this.
method: The paper reviews theoretical proposals for tabletop experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement between two quantum probes, analyzing their feasibility and implications.
result: Several potentially feasible experiments are identified that could detect gravitationally induced entanglement, constraining theories of quantum gravity.
conclusion: Information-theoretic approaches offer a concrete way to test the quantum nature of gravity, with near-term experiments possible.

title: Non-Abelian Geometric Phases In Triangular Structures And Universal Su(2) Control In Shape Space
authors: J. Dai, A. Molochkov, A. J. Niemi, And J. Westerholm
abstract:
Author(s): J. Dai, A. Molochkov, A. J. Niemi, and J. Westerholm

We construct holonomic quantum gates for qubits that are encoded in the near-degenerate vibrational [MATH] doublet of a deformable three-body system. Using Kendall's shape theory, we derive the Wilczek-Zee connection that governs adiabatic transport within the [MATH] manifold. We show that its restricted …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012212] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper constructs holonomic quantum gates for qubits encoded in vibrational doublets of a three-body system using non-Abelian geometric phases.
motivation: To realize universal quantum gates using geometric phases that are robust against certain errors, leveraging the shape space of a triangular molecule.
method: Using Kendall's shape theory to derive the Wilczek-Zee connection for adiabatic transport within a near-degenerate vibrational doublet, and showing that the holonomy yields SU(2) control.
result: The restricted holonomy group is SU(2), enabling universal single-qubit gates via shape deformations of the triangle.
conclusion: This provides a new platform for holonomic quantum computation based on molecular shape dynamics.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory and photonic implementations.
motivation: Quantum cryptography extends beyond key distribution, but a comprehensive classification of available primitives and their security is lacking.
method: The authors classify quantum cryptographic protocols (e.g., quantum secret sharing, quantum digital signatures, quantum money) and analyze their security and experimental implementations using photonic systems.
result: The review provides a structured overview of quantum cryptographic primitives, their security guarantees, limitations, and current photonic implementations.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers a rich set of primitives beyond QKD, but practical implementations face challenges; further theoretical and experimental work is needed.

title: Timescale For Macroscopic Equilibration In Isolated Quantum Systems: A Rigorous Derivation For Free Fermions
authors: Takashi Hara And Tatsuhiko Koike
abstract:
Author(s): Takashi Hara and Tatsuhiko Koike

For a class of translation-invariant free-fermion systems including those with uniform nearest-neighbor hopping) on a [MATH]-dimensional [MATH] hypercubic lattice, we prove that, starting from an arbitrary pure initial state, the system equilibrates with respect to the coarse-grained density within a …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 030406] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper rigorously derives the timescale for macroscopic equilibration in translation-invariant free-fermion systems, showing that equilibration occurs within a timescale proportional to the square of the system size.
motivation: Understanding how isolated quantum systems equilibrate is a fundamental question in non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics, with implications for thermalization and the foundations of statistical mechanics.
method: The authors consider a class of translation-invariant free-fermion models on a hypercubic lattice and analyze the time evolution of coarse-grained density observables using rigorous mathematical techniques, including bounds on correlation functions.
result: They prove that for any initial pure state, the system equilibrates with respect to coarse-grained density within a timescale that scales as the square of the linear system size, independent of the initial state.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous foundation for macroscopic equilibration in free-fermion systems, establishing a clear timescale that can be tested experimentally and compared with other equilibration mechanisms.

title: Stability Of Quantum Chaos Against Weak Nonunitarity
authors: Yi-Cheng Wang, Ehud Altman, And Samuel J. Garratt
abstract:
Author(s): Yi-Cheng Wang, Ehud Altman, and Samuel J. Garratt

We study the quantum dynamics generated by the repeated action of a nonunitary evolution operator on a system of qubits. Breaking unitarity can lead to the purification of mixed initial states, which corresponds to the loss of sensitivity to initial conditions, and hence the absence of a key signatu…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014314] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the stability of quantum chaos under weak nonunitarity, showing that the spectral form factor and out-of-time-order correlators remain robust for timescales up to the inverse dissipation rate.
motivation: Understanding how nonunitarity affects quantum chaos is important for quantum thermodynamics and open quantum systems, where dissipation is unavoidable.
