result: It demonstrates how operating near a quantum phase transition can yield Heisenberg-limited scaling in parameter estimation, surpassing standard quantum limits.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing offers a robust framework for next-generation sensors, though practical challenges like decoherence and control remain.

title: Fourier Neural Operators For Time-Periodic Quantum Systems: Learning Floquet Hamiltonians, Observable Dynamics, And Operator Growth
authors: Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, And Christopher Earls
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, and Christopher Earls

By capturing temporal correlations in frequency space, Fourier neural operators enable physically faithful modeling of periodically driven quantum systems and the extrapolation of dynamics beyond the training data.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020340] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: Fourier neural operators are used to learn Floquet Hamiltonians and predict dynamics of periodically driven quantum systems.
motivation: Modeling time-periodic quantum systems is computationally challenging; neural operators offer a data-driven approach to capture temporal correlations.
method: Fourier neural operators are applied to learn the Floquet Hamiltonian and observable dynamics from training data, leveraging spectral methods for efficiency.
result: The method accurately extrapolates dynamics beyond the training time window and captures operator growth in Floquet systems.
conclusion: Fourier neural operators provide a physically faithful and efficient tool for studying periodically driven quantum systems.

title: Zero-noise Extrapolation Via Cyclic Permutations Of Quantum Circuit Layouts
authors: Zahar Sayapin, Daniil Rabinovich, Nikita Korolev, And Kirill Lakhmanskiy
abstract:
Author(s): Zahar Sayapin, Daniil Rabinovich, Nikita Korolev, and Kirill Lakhmanskiy

Increasing the utility of currently available noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices requires developing efficient methods to mitigate hardware errors. In this work we propose a novel cyclic layout permutations based zero noise extrapolation (CLP-ZNE) protocol for such a task. The method le…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012620] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a zero-noise extrapolation method using cyclic permutations of quantum circuit layouts to mitigate errors on NISQ devices.
motivation: NISQ devices suffer from hardware errors; efficient error mitigation methods are needed to improve utility.
method: The protocol applies cyclic permutations to the circuit layout and performs zero-noise extrapolation on the permuted circuits.
result: The method demonstrates improved error mitigation compared to standard ZNE in numerical simulations.
conclusion: CLP-ZNE is a practical error mitigation technique for NISQ devices, but its contribution is incremental and not a core information-theoretic result.

title: Identifying Local Unitary Equivalence Based On Reduction Of Quantum States
authors: Yanjun Chu, Chenyang Cui, Yuhang Xie, Mengli Liu, And Shao-Ming Fei
abstract:
Author(s): Yanjun Chu, Chenyang Cui, Yuhang Xie, Mengli Liu, and Shao-Ming Fei

Local unitary equivalence is central to entanglement quantification and classification. Identifying the local unitary equivalence remains a formidable challenge. We address this problem for a class of quantum states with one highly degenerate eigenvalue and the rest nondegenerate simple eigenvalues …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012451] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to determine local unitary equivalence for quantum states with one highly degenerate eigenvalue using reduction of quantum states.
motivation: Local unitary equivalence is crucial for entanglement quantification and classification, but identifying it remains challenging, especially for mixed states.
method: The authors derive necessary and sufficient conditions for local unitary equivalence by reducing the problem to comparing reduced density matrices of the states.
result: They provide a practical criterion that simplifies the verification of local unitary equivalence for a specific class of quantum states.
conclusion: The method offers a useful tool for entanglement classification but is limited to states with a particular spectral structure.

title: Entanglement Dynamics Of Delocalized Interacting Particles
authors: M. F. V. Oliveira, F. A. B. F. de Moura, M. L. Lyra, And G. M. A. Almeida
abstract:
Author(s): M. F. V. Oliveira, F. A. B. F. de Moura, M. L. Lyra, and G. M. A. Almeida

Quantum entanglement in systems of identical particles is often obscured by the interplay between exchange-induced correlations and the operational framework used to define entanglement. To study the role of exchange statistics, we propose a scheme using two distinguishable particles where an exchan…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012452] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies entanglement dynamics in a system of two distinguishable particles with exchange symmetry, focusing on how exchange statistics affect entanglement.
motivation: To understand the role of exchange statistics in entanglement of identical particles, which is often obscured by the interplay between exchange-induced correlations and the operational framework.
method: The authors propose a scheme using two distinguishable particles where an exchange interaction is introduced, and study the entanglement dynamics using concurrence.
result: They find that the entanglement dynamics depend on the initial state and the strength of the exchange interaction, with some states showing enhanced entanglement due to exchange.
conclusion: Exchange statistics can significantly influence entanglement dynamics, and the proposed scheme provides a way to study these effects in a controlled manner.

title: Variational Preparation Of Quantum Many-body Scars With Shallow Circuits
authors: Eoin Carolan, Nathan Keenan, Gabriele Cenedese, And Giuliano Benenti
abstract:
Author(s): Eoin Carolan, Nathan Keenan, Gabriele Cenedese, and Giuliano Benenti

We present and benchmark a type of variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) which we denote [MATH]-VQE. It is designed to target midspectrum eigenstates and prepare quantum many-body scar states. The approach leverages the fact that noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices are limited in their ability to …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012613] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) variant to prepare quantum many-body scar states using shallow circuits.
motivation: Quantum many-body scars are non-thermal eigenstates that evade thermalization, and their preparation is challenging for near-term quantum devices.
method: The authors introduce a modified VQE (called M-VQE) that targets mid-spectrum eigenstates by incorporating a penalty term to avoid low-energy states, and benchmark it on small systems.
result: The method successfully prepares scar states with high fidelity using shallow circuits, demonstrating feasibility on noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical way to study quantum many-body scars on current quantum hardware, though the contribution is incremental and the scope is limited to small systems.

title: Boundary Time Crystals Beyond Mean-field Theory: A Stroboscopic Rotating-wave Approximation
authors: Zeping Liu, Yaotian Li, Zhaoyu Fei, And Xiaoguang Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Zeping Liu, Yaotian Li, Zhaoyu Fei, and Xiaoguang Wang

Boundary time crystals are a class of exotic dissipative quantum phases that spontaneously break continuous time-translation symmetry in the thermodynamic limit of open quantum systems. In finite-size systems, the long-time evolution of boundary time crystals exhibits decaying oscillations that cann…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012211] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies boundary time crystals in open quantum systems using a stroboscopic rotating-wave approximation beyond mean-field theory.
motivation: Boundary time crystals are exotic dissipative quantum phases that break continuous time-translation symmetry, but their finite-size behavior and beyond-mean-field effects are not well understood.
method: The authors develop a stroboscopic rotating-wave approximation to analyze the dissipative dynamics of boundary time crystals, going beyond the mean-field approximation.
result: They find that the long-time evolution exhibits decaying oscillations that can be captured by their approximation, and they characterize the phase transition and finite-size scaling.
conclusion: The work provides a more accurate theoretical description of boundary time crystals, relevant for understanding non-equilibrium quantum phases in open systems.

title: Programmable Dissipation For Controlling Nonunitary Floquet Dynamics
authors: Guang-Chen He, Xiao-Meng Zhang, Zhao-Xian Chen, Ze-Guo Chen, And Ming-Hui Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Guang-Chen He, Xiao-Meng Zhang, Zhao-Xian Chen, Ze-Guo Chen, and Ming-Hui Lu

Programmable dissipation provides a practical route to steer nonunitary dynamics in periodically driven systems. Here we realize Floquet engineering of state-selective loss modulation in a reconfigurable electroacoustic two-level platform and demonstrate in situ control of the driven dynamics. We sh…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024313] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates programmable dissipation to control nonunitary Floquet dynamics in an electroacoustic platform.
motivation: To achieve in situ control of driven dynamics in periodically driven systems, which is relevant for quantum thermodynamics and open quantum systems.
method: Floquet engineering of state-selective loss modulation in a reconfigurable electroacoustic two-level platform.
result: Demonstrated in situ control of nonunitary dynamics, showing programmable dissipation.
conclusion: Programmable dissipation is a practical route to steer nonunitary dynamics, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics.

title: Spacetime Duality Between Sequential And Measurement-feedback Circuits
authors: Tsung-Cheng Lu, Sarang Gopalakrishnan, And Yizhi You
abstract:
Author(s): Tsung-Cheng Lu, Sarang Gopalakrishnan, and Yizhi You

Two prevalent approaches for preparing long-range entangled quantum states are (i) linear-depth sequential unitary (SU) circuits, which apply local unitary gates sequentially, and (ii) constant-depth measurement-feedback (MF) circuits, which employ midcircuit measurements and conditional feedback ba…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045123] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes a spacetime duality between sequential unitary circuits and measurement-feedback circuits for preparing long-range entangled states.
motivation: To understand the relationship between two seemingly different approaches for generating long-range entanglement: sequential unitary circuits and measurement-feedback circuits.
method: The authors prove a duality mapping that shows any linear-depth sequential unitary circuit can be simulated by a constant-depth measurement-feedback circuit, and vice versa, using a spacetime perspective.
result: They demonstrate that the two circuit families are equivalent in terms of the states they can prepare, with a trade-off between circuit depth and the use of measurements and feedback.
conclusion: The duality provides a unified framework for designing entanglement preparation protocols and highlights the role of measurements as a resource in quantum circuits.

title: Discrete Time Crystal Order In Spin Chains Enabled By Floquet Flat Bands
authors: Mahbub Rahaman And Analabha Roy
abstract:
Author(s): Mahbub Rahaman and Analabha Roy

We propose a novel protocol to realize discrete time-crystal (DTC) order in clean, periodically driven spin-[MATH] chains. In each drive cycle, a global spin flip is followed by a two-tone flat-band segment. This flat-band segment engineers a fully degenerate Floquet quasienergy spectrum, suppresses …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034311] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a protocol to realize discrete time-crystal order in clean, periodically driven spin chains using Floquet flat bands.
motivation: Discrete time crystals are a novel non-equilibrium phase of matter, and realizing them in clean systems without disorder is a significant challenge.
method: The protocol uses a global spin flip followed by a two-tone flat-band segment in each drive cycle, engineering a fully degenerate Floquet quasienergy spectrum.
result: The flat-band segment suppresses heating and stabilizes the DTC order, as demonstrated through numerical simulations.
conclusion: The proposed protocol provides a clean and robust way to realize DTC order, potentially observable in current experimental platforms.

title: Phase Transition From Localization To Chaos In A Classical Many-body System
authors: Yusuf Kasim, Pavel Orlov, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Yusuf Kasim, Pavel Orlov, and Tomaž Prosen

We report a dynamical phase transition in the information spreading within a classical 2D deterministic interacting many-body system. Specifically, the transition is observed in a recently introduced momentum-conserving parity check cellular automaton (MCPCA) on the square lattice [Kasim and Prosen,…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014140] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports a dynamical phase transition from localization to chaos in information spreading within a classical many-body system.
motivation: Understanding the transition from localized to chaotic behavior in many-body systems is fundamental to statistical mechanics and information thermodynamics.
method: The authors study a momentum-conserving parity check cellular automaton (MCPCA) on a square lattice, analyzing information spreading dynamics.
result: They observe a clear dynamical phase transition in the information propagation, characterized by a change from localized to chaotic spreading.
conclusion: The work provides insights into classical many-body chaos and information dynamics, relevant to the foundations of thermodynamics.

title: Exploring Fixed Points And Eigenstates Of Quantum Systems With Reinforcement Learning
authors: María Laura Olivera-Atencio, Jesús Casado-Pascual, And Denis Lacroix
abstract:
Author(s): María Laura Olivera-Atencio, Jesús Casado-Pascual, and Denis Lacroix

We introduce a reinforcement-learning algorithm designed to identify the fixed points of a given quantum operation. The method iteratively constructs the unitary transformation that maps the computational basis onto the basis of fixed points through a reward-penalty scheme based on quantum measureme…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033087] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: A reinforcement learning algorithm is introduced to find fixed points of quantum operations by constructing unitary transformations via measurement-based reward-penalty.
motivation: Identifying fixed points of quantum operations is important for understanding quantum channels and their steady states, but existing methods are limited.
method: The algorithm iteratively builds a unitary that maps the computational basis to the fixed-point basis, using quantum measurements to provide rewards or penalties.
result: The method successfully identifies fixed points for several example quantum operations, demonstrating its effectiveness.
conclusion: Reinforcement learning offers a practical approach to finding fixed points of quantum operations, with potential applications in quantum information and simulation.

title: Nonreciprocal Multiphoton Bundle Emission In A Spinning Resonator
authors: Xue Gao, Jun Xu, And Xiangming Hu
abstract:
Author(s): Xue Gao, Jun Xu, and Xiangming Hu

We propose a scheme to realize nonreciprocal multiphoton bundle emission in a spinning resonator. The system consists of a rotating two-mode cavity directly coupled to a two-level atom, enabling efficient excitation of the desired multiphoton bundle states. These photon bundles originate from leapfr…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033090] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a scheme for nonreciprocal multiphoton bundle emission using a spinning resonator coupled to a two-level atom.
motivation: To realize nonreciprocal multiphoton emission, which is important for quantum information processing and chiral quantum optics.
method: A rotating two-mode cavity is directly coupled to a two-level atom, enabling leapfrog multiphoton processes that produce photon bundles.
result: The system achieves nonreciprocal emission of multiphoton bundles with controlled directionality and photon statistics.
conclusion: The scheme provides a platform for generating nonreciprocal multiphoton states, with potential applications in quantum networks and photonic quantum computing.

title: Validating The Calibrated Creation Of Heralded Single Photons
authors: Daniel Borrero Landazabal And Kaisa Laiho
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Borrero Landazabal and Kaisa Laiho

For attributing a free-propagating heralded single quantum, several light characteristics such as the number of the emitted modes, mean photon number, and photon-number parity are needed. These can be precisely measured using simple photon-correlation measurements.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032013] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a method to characterize heralded single-photon sources using simple photon-correlation measurements to determine mode number, mean photon number, and photon-number parity.
motivation: Reliable characterization of heralded single-photon sources is essential for quantum communication and networking applications, but existing methods often require complex setups.
method: The authors use photon-correlation measurements, specifically second-order correlation functions and click statistics, to extract the number of modes, mean photon number, and parity of the heralded state.
result: They demonstrate that these parameters can be precisely measured with simple experimental configurations, validating the calibration of heralded single-photon sources.
conclusion: The proposed method provides a practical tool for characterizing heralded single-photon sources, which is important for quantum network applications such as quantum repeaters and QKD.

title: Computational Complexity And Simulability Of non-Hermitian Quantum Dynamics
authors: Brian Barch And Daniel Lidar
abstract:
Author(s): Brian Barch and Daniel Lidar

Non-Hermitian (NH) quantum systems demonstrate striking differences from their Hermitian counterparts, leading to claims of NH advantage in areas ranging from metrology to entanglement generation. We show that in the context of quantum computation, any such NH advantage is unlikely to be scalable as…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033083] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that non-Hermitian quantum dynamics do not provide a scalable advantage for quantum computation due to complexity-theoretic limitations.
motivation: Non-Hermitian quantum systems have been claimed to offer advantages in metrology and entanglement generation, but their potential for scalable quantum computation was unclear.
method: The authors analyze the computational complexity of simulating non-Hermitian dynamics and prove that any such advantage is unlikely to be scalable, using complexity theory and simulation arguments.
result: They demonstrate that non-Hermitian quantum dynamics are not more powerful than standard Hermitian quantum computation in terms of computational complexity, and that simulating them is at least as hard as simulating Hermitian systems.
conclusion: Non-Hermitian advantage is not scalable for quantum computation, and the results align with known complexity classes for quantum computing.

title: General Model And Modulation Strategies For Sagnac-based Encoders
authors: Federico Berra, Matías Rubén Bolaños, Alberto de Toni, Kannan Vijayadharan, Costantino Agnesi, Marco Avesani, Andrea Stanco, Paolo Villoresi, And Giuseppe Vallone
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Berra, Matías Rubén Bolaños, Alberto De Toni, Kannan Vijayadharan, Costantino Agnesi, Marco Avesani, Andrea Stanco, Paolo Villoresi, and Giuseppe Vallone

In recent decades, there has been an increasing demand for faster modulation schemes. Electro-optic modulators are essential components in modern photonic systems, enabling high-speed control of light for applications ranging from telecommunications to quantum communication. Conventional inline and …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033069] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a general model and modulation strategies for Sagnac-based encoders used in quantum communication.
motivation: Faster modulation schemes are needed for quantum communication, and Sagnac-based encoders offer advantages but lack a unified theoretical framework.
method: The authors develop a general model for Sagnac-based encoders and analyze various modulation strategies, including phase and intensity modulation.
result: They identify optimal modulation strategies that maximize encoding speed and fidelity, and validate their model with experimental data.
conclusion: The proposed model and strategies can improve the performance of Sagnac-based encoders in quantum key distribution and other quantum communication systems.

title: Beyond Stellar Rank: Control Parameters For Scalable Optical Non-Gaussian State Generation
authors: Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, And Akira Furusawa
abstract:
Author(s): Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, and Akira Furusawa

Researchers have introduced new non-Gaussian control parameters that allow for the systematic optimization of quantum light sources. This breakthrough can increase the success rate of generating essential quantum states by orders of magnitude.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021034] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces new non-Gaussian control parameters for optimizing optical quantum state generation, significantly increasing success rates.
motivation: Scalable generation of non-Gaussian quantum states is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods suffer from low success rates.
method: The authors propose control parameters beyond the stellar rank to systematically optimize the generation of non-Gaussian states in optical systems.
result: The new parameters enable orders-of-magnitude improvement in the success rate of generating essential quantum states.
conclusion: This work provides a practical framework for scalable optical non-Gaussian state generation, advancing quantum optics and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Universality In The Anticoncentration Of Noisy Quantum Circuits At Finite Depths
authors: Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo de Nardis, And Andrea de Luca
abstract:
Author(s): Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo De Nardis, and Andrea De Luca

A universal description of noisy random circuits reveals depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent anticoncentration.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020365] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a universal description of anticoncentration in noisy random quantum circuits, identifying depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent behavior.
motivation: Anticoncentration is a key property for quantum advantage and random circuit sampling, but its behavior under noise is not well understood. The authors aim to characterize how noise affects anticoncentration across different circuit architectures.
method: The authors study random quantum circuits with local noise using analytical techniques from statistical physics and random matrix theory, deriving universal scaling laws for the anticoncentration measure as a function of circuit depth and noise rate.
result: They find three depth-dependent regimes: a noise-free regime, a universal regime where anticoncentration decays exponentially with depth, and a saturation regime. The results are independent of the specific circuit architecture.
conclusion: Noisy random circuits exhibit universal anticoncentration behavior, which has implications for the feasibility of quantum advantage experiments and the design of quantum circuits.

title: Quantum Computational Complexity Of Matrix Functions
authors: Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, And Leandro Aolita
abstract:
Author(s): Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, and Leandro Aolita

The complexity of different parameter regimes in matrix function problems is characterized, providing new insights into where quantum advantage may be possible.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020364] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper characterizes the quantum computational complexity of matrix functions, identifying regimes where quantum advantage may exist.
motivation: Understanding the complexity of matrix functions is fundamental for quantum algorithms, but the paper focuses on complexity classification rather than direct information-theoretic results.
method: The authors analyze different parameter regimes of matrix function problems using quantum computational complexity theory.
result: They provide a characterization of complexity classes for matrix functions, highlighting potential quantum advantage in certain regimes.
conclusion: The work offers insights into where quantum computers may outperform classical ones for matrix function problems, but it is more about complexity theory than core quantum information topics.

title: Symmetry-Accelerated Classical Simulation Of Clifford-Dominated Circuits
authors: Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, And Juani Bermejo-Vega
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, and Juani Bermejo-Vega

Strong and weak symmetry reductions render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries beyond previous limits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020356] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces symmetry-accelerated classical simulation methods for Clifford-dominated circuits by exploiting stabilizer decompositions.
motivation: Efficient classical simulation of quantum circuits is crucial for benchmarking and verifying quantum computers, especially in the noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) era.
method: The authors develop strong and weak symmetry reduction techniques to optimize stabilizer decompositions, enabling tractable simulation of multiqubit unitaries beyond previous limits.
result: The proposed methods significantly reduce the computational cost of simulating Clifford-dominated circuits, extending the reach of classical simulation.
conclusion: Symmetry-accelerated stabilizer decompositions provide a practical tool for classical simulation of near-term quantum circuits, with potential applications in verification and benchmarking.

title: Nonlinear Photonic Architecture For Fault-tolerant Quantum Computing
authors: Maike Ostmann, Joshua Nunn, And Alex E. Jones
abstract:
Author(s): Maike Ostmann, Joshua Nunn, and Alex E. Jones

We propose an architecture for fault-tolerant quantum computing that incorporates strong single-photon nonlinearities into a photonic Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger-measurement-based architecture. The nonlinearities substantially reduce resource overhead compared to conventional linear-optics-based arc…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012618] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a photonic architecture for fault-tolerant quantum computing using strong nonlinearities to reduce resource overhead.
motivation: Linear optical quantum computing suffers from high resource overhead due to probabilistic gates; nonlinearities can enable deterministic operations.
method: Integrates strong single-photon nonlinearities into a Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger-measurement-based architecture, leveraging nonlinear optical effects.
result: Substantial reduction in resource overhead compared to linear-optics-based architectures, enabling more efficient fault-tolerant quantum computing.
conclusion: Nonlinear photonic architectures offer a promising path toward scalable fault-tolerant quantum computing with reduced resource requirements.

title: Expander Quantum Low Density Parity Check Codes Against Long-range Correlated Errors In Memory
authors: Yash Deepak Kashtikar, Pranay Mathur, Sudharsan Senthil, And Avhishek Chatterjee
abstract:
Author(s): Yash Deepak Kashtikar, Pranay Mathur, Sudharsan Senthil, and Avhishek Chatterjee

Fault tolerance using constant space overhead against long-range correlated errors is an important practical question. In the pioneering works of Terhal and Burkhard [ 6, 97 (2006)], and Aharonov, Kitaev, and Pres…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012444] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the performance of expander quantum LDPC codes against long-range correlated errors in quantum memory, showing that such codes can achieve fault tolerance with constant space overhead under certain noise models.
motivation: Fault tolerance with constant space overhead is crucial for practical quantum computing, but most existing analyses assume independent or local errors. Understanding how quantum LDPC codes perform under long-range correlated errors is important for realistic noise models.
method: The authors analyze the error correction capability of expander quantum LDPC codes under a noise model where errors are correlated over long distances, using analytical bounds and numerical simulations.
result: They demonstrate that expander quantum LDPC codes can tolerate long-range correlated errors with constant space overhead, provided the correlation strength is below a threshold.
conclusion: Expander quantum LDPC codes are promising for fault-tolerant quantum memory even under non-local noise, but the results are specific to certain correlation models and may not generalize to all practical scenarios.

title: Biased-noise Thresholds Of Zero-rate Holographic Codes With Tensor-network Decoding
authors: J. Fan, M. Steinberg, A. Jahn, C. Cao, And S. Feld
abstract:
Author(s): J. Fan, M. Steinberg, A. Jahn, C. Cao, and S. Feld

A crucial insight for practical quantum error correction is that different types of errors, such as single-qubit Pauli operators, typically occur with different probabilities. Finding an optimal quantum code under such biased noise is a challenging problem, related to the (generally unknown) maximum…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012447] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies biased-noise thresholds of zero-rate holographic codes using tensor-network decoding.
motivation: Practical quantum error correction requires codes optimized for biased noise, but finding optimal codes is challenging.
method: The authors analyze holographic quantum codes under biased noise models and employ tensor-network decoding to compute thresholds.
result: They determine biased-noise thresholds for zero-rate holographic codes and compare performance with other code families.
conclusion: Holographic codes show potential for biased noise, but their zero-rate nature limits practical applicability.

title: Training The Classification Capability Of Large-scale Quantum Cellular Automata
authors: Mario Boneberg, Simon Kochsiek, Gabriele Perfetto, And Igor Lesanovsky
abstract:
Author(s): Mario Boneberg, Simon Kochsiek, Gabriele Perfetto, and Igor Lesanovsky

In the vicinity of a phase transition ergodicity can be broken. Here, different initial many-body configurations evolve toward one of several fixed points, which are macroscopically distinguishable through an order parameter. This mechanism enables state classification in quantum cellular automata a…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012209] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses quantum cellular automata near a phase transition to classify many-body states, demonstrating a classification capability.
motivation: To explore how ergodicity breaking near phase transitions can be harnessed for state classification in quantum cellular automata.
method: The authors study a quantum cellular automaton model and analyze its dynamics near a phase transition, using order parameters to distinguish different initial configurations.
result: They show that the automaton can classify initial states into macroscopically distinct fixed points, effectively performing a classification task.
conclusion: Quantum cellular automata near phase transitions can serve as classifiers, linking many-body physics to computational tasks.

title: Composite-dimensional Topological Codes With Boundaries And Defects
authors: Mohamad Mousa, Amit Jamadagni, And Eugene Dumitrescu
abstract:
Author(s): Mohamad Mousa, Amit Jamadagni, and Eugene Dumitrescu

We introduce new algorithms and provide example constructions of stabilizer models for the gapped boundaries, domain walls, and [MATH] defects of Abelian composite-dimensional twisted quantum doubles. Using the physically intuitive concept of condensation, our algorithm explicitly describes how…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012438] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces algorithms and constructions for stabilizer models of gapped boundaries, domain walls, and defects in Abelian composite-dimensional twisted quantum doubles.
motivation: Topological codes with boundaries and defects are important for fault-tolerant quantum computation, but constructing such codes for composite-dimensional systems is challenging.
method: The authors use the concept of condensation to develop algorithms that explicitly describe stabilizer models for boundaries, domain walls, and defects in composite-dimensional twisted quantum doubles.
result: New stabilizer models and example constructions are provided for gapped boundaries, domain walls, and defects in Abelian composite-dimensional twisted quantum doubles.
conclusion: The work extends the theory of topological codes to composite dimensions, potentially enabling more flexible fault-tolerant quantum computing architectures.

title: Runtime Reduction In Lattice Surgery Utilizing Timelike Soft Information
authors: Yutaro Akahoshi, Riki Toshio, Jun Fujisaki, Hirotaka Oshima, Shintaro Sato, And Keisuke Fujii
abstract:
Author(s): Yutaro Akahoshi, Riki Toshio, Jun Fujisaki, Hirotaka Oshima, Shintaro Sato, and Keisuke Fujii

Runtime optimization of the quantum computing within a given computational resource is important to achieve practical quantum advantage. In this paper, we propose a runtime reduction protocol for the lattice surgery, which utilizes the soft information corresponding to the logical measurement error.…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033085] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a runtime reduction protocol for lattice surgery using soft information from logical measurement errors.
motivation: Optimizing runtime within given computational resources is crucial for practical quantum advantage.
method: Utilizes soft information corresponding to logical measurement errors to reduce the number of syndrome extraction rounds in lattice surgery.
result: Demonstrates runtime reduction while maintaining fault tolerance.
conclusion: The protocol offers a practical improvement for surface code quantum computing.

title: Critical States Preparation In Light-matter Systems With Deep Reinforcement Learning
authors: Jia-Wen Yu, Yiming Yu, Ke-Xiong Yan, Jun-Hao Lin, Jie Song, Ye-Hong Chen, And Yan Xia
abstract:
Author(s): Jia-Wen Yu, Yiming Yu, Ke-Xiong Yan, Jun-Hao Lin, Jie Song, Ye-Hong Chen, and Yan Xia

The fast and efficient preparation of quantum critical states is a challenging yet crucial task for various quantum technologies. This difficulty is most particularly for systems near a quantum phase transition, where the closure of the energy gap fundamentally limits the timescale of adiabatic proc…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033063] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses deep reinforcement learning to prepare quantum critical states in light-matter systems, focusing on fast state preparation near quantum phase transitions.
motivation: Preparing quantum critical states is challenging due to the closure of the energy gap near phase transitions, which limits adiabatic timescales.
method: The authors employ deep reinforcement learning to design control pulses that efficiently drive the system into critical states.
result: The method achieves faster and more efficient preparation of critical states compared to traditional adiabatic approaches.
conclusion: Deep reinforcement learning offers a promising tool for quantum state preparation in critical systems, with potential applications in quantum technologies.

title: Universal Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation In 2d Without Getting Tied In Knots
authors: Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, And Benjamin J. Brown
abstract:
Author(s): Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, and Benjamin J. Brown

Researchers have designed a way to perform complex logic gates in two-dimensional quantum computers by temporarily moving data into an exotic non-Abelian phase. This method provides a path toward large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031001] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method for universal fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D using non-Abelian anyons, avoiding complex braiding.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation in two dimensions is challenging due to the difficulty of implementing logical gates without braiding. The authors aim to overcome this by leveraging non-Abelian phases.
method: The method involves temporarily moving data into an exotic non-Abelian phase to perform complex logic gates, enabling universal computation without knotting.
result: The approach provides a path toward large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D architectures.
conclusion: This work advances the feasibility of fault-tolerant quantum computing in planar geometries, potentially simplifying hardware requirements.

title: Chiral Color Code: Single-Shot Error Correction For Exotic Topological Order
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

A family of three-dimensional stabilizer codes achieving single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders is proposed, introducing new platforms for fault-tolerant quantum computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033015] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a family of 3D stabilizer codes achieving single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders.
motivation: To enable fault-tolerant quantum computation for exotic topological orders that are not captured by conventional codes.
method: Constructs three-dimensional stabilizer codes with single-shot error correction properties, leveraging topological order.
result: Demonstrates that single-shot error correction is possible for fermionic and chiral topological phases.
conclusion: The proposed codes provide new platforms for fault-tolerant quantum computation with exotic topological orders.

title: Accelerating Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation With Good Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Guo Zhang, Yuanye Zhu, And Ying Li
abstract:
Author(s): Guo Zhang, Yuanye Zhu, and Ying Li

Fault-tolerant quantum computation with constant qubit overhead and low time overhead is enabled by parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033012] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a fault-tolerant quantum computation scheme using good quantum LDPC codes to achieve constant qubit overhead and low time overhead via parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation with low overhead is crucial for practical quantum computers. Current schemes often require high qubit overhead, and this work aims to reduce both qubit and time overhead using advanced quantum LDPC codes.
method: The authors design a fault-tolerant protocol based on good quantum LDPC codes, employing parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation to achieve constant qubit overhead and logarithmic time overhead.
result: The scheme achieves constant qubit overhead and low time overhead, demonstrating that fault-tolerant quantum computation can be more resource-efficient than previously thought.
conclusion: Good quantum LDPC codes enable practical fault-tolerant quantum computation with significantly reduced overhead, bringing us closer to scalable quantum computers.

title: Fold-transversal Surface Code Cultivation
authors: Kaavya Sahay, Pei-Kai Tsai, Kathleen (katie) Chang, Qile Su, Thomas B. Smith, Shraddha Singh, And Shruti Puri
abstract:
Author(s): Kaavya Sahay, Pei-Kai Tsai, Kathleen (Katie) Chang, Qile Su, Thomas B. Smith, Shraddha Singh, and Shruti Puri

A new strategy for magic-state cultivation achieves low spacetime overhead for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033006] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: A new strategy for magic-state cultivation using fold-transversal surface codes achieves low spacetime overhead for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.
motivation: Magic state distillation is a key component for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but existing protocols have high overhead. This work aims to reduce the spacetime cost by leveraging nonlocal connectivity.
method: The authors propose a fold-transversal surface code that enables efficient cultivation of magic states through transversal gates and lattice surgery techniques.
result: The protocol achieves significantly lower spacetime overhead compared to standard distillation methods, making it suitable for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.
conclusion: Fold-transversal surface code cultivation offers a practical path toward low-overhead magic state preparation in quantum computers with nonlocal connectivity.

title: Beam Search Decoder For Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Min Ye, Dave Wecker, And Nicolas Delfosse
abstract:
Author(s): Min Ye, Dave Wecker, and Nicolas Delfosse

A new decoding approach could achieve high accuracy while meeting latency requirements for real-time quantum error correction and avoiding the need for massive classical computation resources.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033002] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: A beam search decoder for quantum LDPC codes achieves high accuracy and low latency for real-time quantum error correction.
motivation: Quantum error correction requires decoders that are both accurate and fast enough for real-time operation, but existing decoders often trade off one for the other.
method: The authors propose a beam search decoder that explores a limited set of candidate error patterns, using a heuristic to prune the search space while maintaining high decoding accuracy.
result: The beam search decoder achieves comparable or better accuracy than existing decoders (e.g., BP-OSD) with significantly lower latency, meeting real-time requirements.
conclusion: This decoder offers a practical solution for real-time decoding of quantum LDPC codes, advancing fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Nontrivial Multiproduct Commutation Relation Toward Reducing $T$-Count In Sequential Pauli-Based Computation
authors: Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, And Keisuke Fujii
abstract:
Author(s): Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, and Keisuke Fujii

By harnessing nontrivial commuting structures in quantum circuits, a novel multiproduct commutation relation significantly reduces the costly
[PRX Quantum 7, 020345] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a multiproduct commutation relation to reduce T-count in sequential Pauli-based computation, a technique for fault-tolerant quantum computing.
motivation: Reducing the number of T gates is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, as T gates are costly to implement. The paper aims to exploit commuting structures to achieve this reduction.
method: The authors derive a nontrivial multiproduct commutation relation that allows multiple Pauli operators to be commuted through T gates simultaneously, leading to a more efficient circuit compilation.
result: The proposed relation significantly reduces the T-count in sequential Pauli-based computation, as demonstrated by theoretical analysis and examples.
conclusion: The work provides a new tool for optimizing quantum circuits in fault-tolerant settings, though its impact is limited to specific circuit structures.

title: Quantifying Robustness And Locality Of Majorana Bound States In Interacting Systems
authors: William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, And Viktor Svensson
abstract:
