Motivated by recent quantum-dot experiments, this work rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems to quantify their protection and feasibility for non-Abelian braiding.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020341] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems and quantifies their robustness and locality for non-Abelian braiding.
motivation: Recent quantum-dot experiments motivate a need for clear criteria to assess the protection and feasibility of Majorana bound states in realistic interacting systems.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework to define Majorana bound states in interacting systems and compute measures of robustness and locality.
result: They provide quantitative criteria to evaluate the quality of Majorana bound states, showing how interactions affect their protection.
conclusion: The work offers practical guidelines for identifying suitable Majorana platforms for topological quantum computing.

title: Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev Physics From The Hubbard Model: A Floquet-Engineering Approach
authors: Charles Creffield, Fernando Sols, Marco Schirò, And Nathan Goldman
abstract:
Author(s): Charles Creffield, Fernando Sols, Marco Schirò, and Nathan Goldman

Ultracold atoms in an optical lattice could emulate a prominent model of quantum matter linked to black holes and high-temperature superconductors.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046302] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a Floquet-engineering approach to realize the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model in ultracold atoms in an optical lattice, linking to black holes and high-temperature superconductors.
motivation: The SYK model is a prominent model of quantum matter with connections to black holes and high-Tc superconductivity, but its experimental realization is challenging. This work aims to provide a feasible platform using ultracold atoms.
method: The authors use Floquet engineering with periodic driving to design a Hamiltonian that mimics the SYK model's all-to-all random interactions in a Hubbard model setup.
result: They show that the Floquet-driven Hubbard model can reproduce key features of the SYK model, such as maximal chaos and a conformal limit.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical route to experimentally study SYK physics and its connections to quantum gravity and condensed matter.

title: Relaxation Toward An Ideal Chern Band Through Coupling To A Markovian Bath
authors: Bruno Mera And Tomoki Ozawa
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Mera and Tomoki Ozawa

We propose a microscopic, weak-coupling mechanism by which generic Chern bands asymptotically relax toward ideal bands. We consider coupling interacting electrons to a Caldeira-Leggett-like Ohmic bosonic bath. Using the Born-Markov approximation, we analytically show that, upon taking the leading or…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046601] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a mechanism for Chern bands to relax toward ideal bands via coupling to a Markovian bath, using a Caldeira-Leggett model and Born-Markov approximation.
motivation: Ideal Chern bands are desirable for fractional Chern insulators, but realistic bands are not ideal; the authors aim to show that coupling to a bath can drive relaxation toward ideal bands.
method: They consider interacting electrons in a Chern band coupled to an Ohmic bosonic bath, apply the Born-Markov approximation, and analytically derive the relaxation dynamics in the weak-coupling limit.
result: They show that under the leading-order approximation, the system relaxes toward an ideal Chern band characterized by a flat Berry curvature and uniform Fubini-Study metric.
conclusion: The proposed mechanism provides a way to engineer ideal Chern bands through controlled dissipation, which may facilitate the observation of fractional Chern insulators.

title: Limitations Of Entangled Two-photon Absorption Detection
authors: R. Pollmann, F. Roeder, C. Silberhorn, And B. Brecht
abstract:
Author(s): R. Pollmann, F. Roeder, C. Silberhorn, and B. Brecht

We introduce a method for determining the sensitivity of any given entangled two-photon absorption (ETPA) measurement. By modeling all signal and noise contributions to the measurement, we derive a single numerical value that describes the sensitivity of the ETPA measurement in Göppert-Mayer units. …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013718] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the sensitivity limits of entangled two-photon absorption detection, providing a method to quantify measurement sensitivity in Göppert-Mayer units.
motivation: Entangled two-photon absorption (ETPA) is a promising technique for quantum sensing and spectroscopy, but its practical sensitivity limits were not well understood. The authors aim to provide a rigorous framework to evaluate the feasibility of ETPA measurements.
method: The authors model all signal and noise contributions in an ETPA measurement, deriving a single numerical sensitivity value. They consider realistic experimental parameters and noise sources.
result: They find that ETPA detection sensitivity is fundamentally limited by the low cross-section of two-photon absorption and the noise from background photons and detector dark counts, making practical detection challenging.
conclusion: The results indicate that ETPA detection is not currently feasible for many applications due to sensitivity limitations, guiding future experimental efforts toward improving signal-to-noise ratios.

title: Diffusion Cascade In A Model Of Interacting Random Walkers
authors: Abhishek Raj, Paolo Glorioso, Sarang Gopalakrishnan, And Vadim Oganesyan
abstract:
Author(s): Abhishek Raj, Paolo Glorioso, Sarang Gopalakrishnan, and Vadim Oganesyan

We consider the relaxation of finite-wave-vector density waves in a facilitated classical lattice gas. Linear hydrodynamics predicts that such perturbations should relax exponentially, but nonlinear effects were predicted to cause subexponential relaxation via nonperturbative long-time tails [L. V. …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014312] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies subexponential relaxation of density waves in a facilitated classical lattice gas due to nonlinear long-time tails.
motivation: Understanding relaxation in interacting many-body systems is a fundamental problem in statistical mechanics, with implications for transport and thermalization.
method: The authors analyze a facilitated classical lattice gas model using hydrodynamic theory and numerical simulations to capture nonlinear effects beyond linear hydrodynamics.
result: They find that nonlinear effects cause subexponential (stretched exponential or power-law) relaxation of finite-wave-vector density waves, in contrast to the exponential decay predicted by linear hydrodynamics.
conclusion: The work demonstrates the importance of nonlinear fluctuations in classical lattice gases, but the model is classical and the results are not directly connected to quantum information or quantum thermodynamics.

title: Benchmarking Quantum Simulation Of Chemical Hamiltonians Using The Sorted-list Encoding
authors: Calvin Ku, Yu-Cheng Chen, Alice Hu, And Min-Hsiu Hsieh
abstract:
Author(s): Calvin Ku, Yu-Cheng Chen, Alice Hu, and Min-Hsiu Hsieh

Quantum phase estimation is a cornerstone algorithm for fault-tolerant quantum computation, especially for electronic structure calculations of chemical systems. Optimal simulation relies on a complex trade-offs across many parameters including Hamiltonian simulation techniques, basis sets, and the …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033091] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: Benchmarks quantum simulation of chemical Hamiltonians using sorted-list encoding, focusing on resource estimation for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
motivation: To optimize quantum phase estimation for chemical systems by evaluating different Hamiltonian simulation techniques and basis sets.
method: Compares sorted-list encoding with other methods (e.g., Trotterization, Taylor series) in terms of T-gate count and logical qubits for molecular Hamiltonians.
result: Sorted-list encoding reduces T-gate count compared to Trotterization but requires more qubits; overall resource estimates remain high for practical quantum advantage.
conclusion: The sorted-list encoding offers a trade-off but does not dramatically reduce resource requirements; further improvements are needed for quantum advantage in chemistry.

title: Quantum Solver For Single-impurity Anderson Models With Particle-hole Symmetry
authors: M. Karabin, T. Sohail, D. Bykov, E. A. Coello Pérez, S. Ghosh, M. Gopalakrishnan Meena, S. Kim, A. Shehata, I.-S. Suh, H. Terletska, And M. Eisenbach
abstract:
Author(s): M. Karabin, T. Sohail, D. Bykov, E. A. Coello Pérez, S. Ghosh, M. Gopalakrishnan Meena, S. Kim, A. Shehata, I.-S. Suh, H. Terletska, and M. Eisenbach

Quantum embedding methods, such as dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT), provide a powerful framework for investigating strongly correlated materials. A central computational bottleneck in DMFT is in solving the Anderson impurity model (AIM), whose exact solution is classically intractable for large b…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033066] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum algorithm to solve the single-impurity Anderson model with particle-hole symmetry on a quantum computer, aiming to accelerate DMFT calculations for strongly correlated materials.
motivation: Solving the Anderson impurity model is a computational bottleneck in DMFT, and classical methods become intractable for large bath sizes. A quantum solver could enable more accurate simulations of strongly correlated materials.
method: The authors design a variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) tailored to the Anderson impurity model with particle-hole symmetry, using a specific ansatz and measurement scheme to compute the ground state and Green's function.
result: Numerical simulations on small systems show that the quantum solver can reproduce exact results with high accuracy, and resource estimates suggest potential quantum advantage for larger systems.
conclusion: The proposed quantum solver is a promising approach for quantum embedding methods, but experimental implementation on near-term quantum devices remains challenging due to noise and limited qubit count.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators, focusing on strong correlations and optical control.
motivation: To understand and control nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated electron systems, which may lead to novel material properties and metastable phases.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental advances, including dynamical mean-field theory, time-resolved spectroscopy, and pump-probe techniques.
result: Identifies key mechanisms for photodoping, metastable states, and nonthermal orders such as superconductivity and magnetism.
conclusion: Photoexcitation provides a powerful tool to manipulate Mott insulators, but the field is still developing with many open questions.

title: Transient Localization From Fractionalization: Vanishingly Small Energy Transport In Gapless Quantum Magnets
authors: Shi Feng, Penghao Zhu, Johannes Knolle, And Michael Knap
abstract:
Author(s): Shi Feng, Penghao Zhu, Johannes Knolle, and Michael Knap

Disorder-free localization is usually associated with dynamics far from equilibrium. Here, the authors uncover a new mechanism in the low-energy sector of clean, gapless quantum magnets: transient localization from mass-imbalanced fractionalization. Studying the dynamical response in the gapless phase of a translation-invariant Kitaev ladder model, they show that fractionalization creates a coherent superposition of quasistatic flux-disorder configurations in the ground state, preserving translation symmetry while strongly suppressing correlation spreading and energy transport.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034423] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers a new mechanism of transient localization from fractionalization in clean, gapless quantum magnets, leading to vanishingly small energy transport.
motivation: Understanding energy transport in low-dimensional quantum magnets is important for fundamental physics and potential applications, but disorder-free localization is typically associated with far-from-equilibrium dynamics.
method: The authors study a translation-invariant Kitaev ladder model in its gapless phase, analyzing the dynamical response and showing that fractionalization creates a coherent superposition of quasistatic flux-disorder configurations.
result: They find that despite preserving translation symmetry, the system exhibits strongly suppressed correlation spreading and energy transport due to the mass-imbalanced fractionalization.
conclusion: This work reveals a new mechanism for transient localization in clean systems, which may have implications for understanding thermalization and transport in quantum magnets.

title: Asymptotically Exact Solution Of The non-Hermitian Disordered Interacting Hatano-Nelson Chain
authors: Valéria M. Mattiello, Victor L. Quito, And Eduardo Miranda
abstract:
Author(s): Valéria M. Mattiello, Victor L. Quito, and Eduardo Miranda

This article presents an exact low-energy solution of a one-dimensional model of interacting disordered spinless fermions with non-Hermitian hopping, equivalently formulated as a non-Hermitian spin-1/2 chain. The solution exhibits finite-temperature divergent spin susceptibilities and shows that non-Hermiticity suppresses the entanglement entropy relative to the corresponding Hermitian model, eliminating the associated entanglement scaling.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032012] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper solves a non-Hermitian disordered interacting fermion chain exactly, finding suppressed entanglement entropy and divergent spin susceptibilities.
motivation: To understand the interplay of non-Hermiticity, disorder, and interactions in a solvable model, and its effects on entanglement and thermodynamic properties.
method: Exact low-energy solution of a one-dimensional model of interacting disordered spinless fermions with non-Hermitian hopping, mapped to a non-Hermitian spin-1/2 chain.
result: Non-Hermiticity suppresses entanglement entropy relative to the Hermitian model and eliminates entanglement scaling; finite-temperature spin susceptibilities diverge.
conclusion: The model provides an exactly solvable example of non-Hermitian many-body physics with implications for entanglement and thermodynamics.

title: Insertion Space In Repulsive Active Matter
authors: Luke K. Davis And Karel Proesmans
abstract:
Author(s): Luke K. Davis and Karel Proesmans

The statistical geometry of active repulsive (or hard) rods and disks is explored using both theory and simulations. It is found that increasing the persistence of the active particle motion increases the total insertion volume and its surface area: the averaged space available to place another particle without overlaps. As a result, the insertion space also becomes more connected in the presence of activity.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032007] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the statistical geometry of active repulsive rods and disks, showing that activity increases insertion volume and connectivity.
motivation: Understanding how active motion affects the geometry of available space in repulsive systems is important for characterizing active matter.
method: The authors combine theoretical analysis and simulations to compute insertion volumes and surface areas for active hard rods and disks.
result: Increasing persistence of active motion increases the total insertion volume and its surface area, making the insertion space more connected.
conclusion: Activity significantly alters the statistical geometry of repulsive active matter, which may have implications for packing and transport.

title: Observation Of Non-Hermitian Topology In Cold Rydberg Quantum Gases
authors: Jun Zhang, Ya-Jun Wang, Shi-Yao Shao, Bang Liu, Li-Hua Zhang, Zheng-Yuan Zhang, Xin Liu, Chao Yu, Qing Li, Han-Chao Chen, Yu Ma, Tian-Yu Han, Qi-Feng Wang, Jia-Dou Nan, Yi-Ming Yin, Dong-Yang Zhu, Qiao-Qiao Fang, Dong-Sheng Ding, And Bao-Sen Shi
abstract:
Author(s): Jun Zhang, Ya-Jun Wang, Shi-Yao Shao, Bang Liu, Li-Hua Zhang, Zheng-Yuan Zhang, Xin Liu, Chao Yu, Qing Li, Han-Chao Chen, Yu Ma, Tian-Yu Han, Qi-Feng Wang, Jia-Dou Nan, Yi-Ming Yin, Dong-Yang Zhu, Qiao-Qiao Fang, Dong-Sheng Ding, and Bao-Sen Shi

A cold Rydberg gas is used as a tunable dissipative many-body platform to map out non-Hermitian spectral topology, revealing interaction-driven winding numbers and scan-direction-dependent nonreciprocity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033004] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally observes non-Hermitian topological phenomena in a cold Rydberg gas platform.
motivation: To explore non-Hermitian topology in a tunable dissipative many-body system, which is a fundamental physics question rather than a quantum information application.
method: Using a cold Rydberg gas as a dissipative many-body platform, they map out non-Hermitian spectral topology by measuring winding numbers and nonreciprocity.
result: They observe interaction-driven winding numbers and scan-direction-dependent nonreciprocity, confirming non-Hermitian topological effects.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a new platform for studying non-Hermitian topology but does not directly advance quantum information processing or thermodynamics.

title: Baby Universes From Thermal Pure States In The Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev Model
authors: Martin Sasieta, Brian Swingle, And Alejandro Vilar López
abstract:
Author(s): Martin Sasieta, Brian Swingle, and Alejandro Vilar López

We construct a simple two-dimensional holographic model of a closed “baby” universe. The baby universe spacetime originates from the black hole interior in Jackiw-Teitelboim gravity. The holographic description is a low-temperature thermal pure state of two Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) models. The constr…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 041501] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper constructs a holographic model of a baby universe from thermal pure states in the SYK model, connecting black hole interiors to low-temperature quantum states.
motivation: To understand the emergence of baby universes from quantum gravitational systems using holography.
method: The authors use Jackiw-Teitelboim gravity and the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model to construct a low-temperature thermal pure state that holographically describes a baby universe spacetime.
result: They show that the baby universe originates from the black hole interior in the holographic dual.
conclusion: The work provides a simple holographic model of a closed baby universe, linking quantum gravity and condensed matter physics.

title: Symmetry-adapted Energy Estimation On Quantum Devices
authors: Kosuke Nogaki, Steffen Backes, Tomonori Shirakawa, Seiji Yunoki, And Ryotaro Arita
abstract:
Author(s): Kosuke Nogaki, Steffen Backes, Tomonori Shirakawa, Seiji Yunoki, and Ryotaro Arita

We present a symmetry-adapted extension of quantum selected configuration interaction and sample-based quantum diagonalization that rigorously embeds space-group symmetry into the many-body subspace sampled by quantum hardware. The method is benchmarked on the two-leg ladder Hubbard model using both…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065124] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a symmetry-adapted quantum algorithm for estimating ground state energies of lattice models on quantum devices.
motivation: Quantum chemistry and condensed matter simulations on near-term quantum devices require efficient use of limited quantum resources; embedding symmetries can reduce the required circuit depth and number of measurements.
method: The authors extend quantum selected configuration interaction and sample-based quantum diagonalization to incorporate space-group symmetry, constructing a symmetry-adapted many-body subspace sampled by quantum hardware.
result: Benchmarks on the two-leg ladder Hubbard model show improved accuracy and reduced resource requirements compared to symmetry-agnostic approaches.
conclusion: Symmetry adaptation is a practical technique to enhance quantum simulations of strongly correlated systems on current quantum devices.

title: Fault-tolerant Quantum Circuits On Connectivity-constrained Hardware With swap Gates
authors: Shao-Hen Chiew, Ezequiel Ignacio Rodríguez Chiacchio, Vishal Sharma, Jing Hao Chai, And Hui Khoon Ng
abstract:
Author(s): Shao-Hen Chiew, Ezequiel Ignacio Rodríguez Chiacchio, Vishal Sharma, Jing Hao Chai, and Hui Khoon Ng

In near-term quantum computing devices, connectivity between qubits remain limited by architectural constraints. A computational circuit with given connectivity requirements necessary for multiqubit gates has to be embedded within physical hardware with fixed connectivity. Long-distance gates have t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033081] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to compile fault-tolerant quantum circuits onto connectivity-constrained hardware using SWAP gates, focusing on practical compilation rather than fundamental information theory.
motivation: Near-term quantum devices have limited qubit connectivity, requiring efficient compilation of circuits with long-range gates onto fixed hardware.
method: The authors develop a heuristic algorithm that inserts SWAP gates to satisfy connectivity constraints while minimizing overhead, and analyze its performance on various circuit benchmarks.
result: The algorithm achieves significant reductions in SWAP overhead compared to existing methods, enabling fault-tolerant circuits on realistic hardware.
conclusion: Efficient SWAP-based compilation is crucial for near-term quantum computing, but the work is primarily a compilation technique rather than a fundamental information-theoretic result.

title: Quantum-classical Auxiliary Field Quantum Monte Carlo With Matchgate Shadows On Trapped Ion Quantum Computers
authors: Luning Zhao et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Luning Zhao et al.

We demonstrate an end-to-end workflow to model chemical reaction barriers with the quantum-classical auxiliary field quantum Monte Carlo (QC-AFQMC) algorithm with quantum tomography using matchgate shadows. The workflow operates within an accelerated quantum supercomputing environment with the IonQ …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033061] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a quantum-classical auxiliary field quantum Monte Carlo algorithm with matchgate shadows on trapped ion quantum computers for modeling chemical reaction barriers.
motivation: To enable accurate quantum chemistry simulations on near-term quantum devices by combining classical Monte Carlo with quantum tomography.
method: The workflow uses matchgate shadows for efficient tomography of quantum states produced by a trapped ion quantum computer, feeding into an auxiliary field quantum Monte Carlo algorithm.
result: The approach successfully models chemical reaction barriers, demonstrating an end-to-end workflow on IonQ hardware.
conclusion: The hybrid quantum-classical algorithm shows promise for practical quantum chemistry, but the paper focuses on computational chemistry rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Provable Quantum Speedups For Computing Persistence In Topological Data Analysis
authors: Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, And Ryu Hayakawa
abstract:
Author(s): Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, and Ryu Hayakawa

A quantum algorithm achieving exponential speedup for a topological data analysis problem is proposed, potentially driving new practical applications in quantum computing.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020361] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum algorithm for computing persistence in topological data analysis, claiming exponential speedup.
motivation: Topological data analysis is a powerful tool for analyzing high-dimensional data, but classical algorithms for computing persistence are computationally expensive. Quantum computing may offer speedups.
method: The authors design a quantum algorithm that leverages quantum linear algebra and topological data analysis techniques to compute persistence diagrams.
result: The algorithm achieves an exponential speedup over classical methods for certain classes of inputs.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a potential practical application of quantum computing in data analysis, though the speedup relies on specific assumptions about input data.

title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithms For The Jones Polynomial
authors: Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew Decross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, And Konstantinos Meichanetzidis
abstract:
Author(s): Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew DeCross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, and Konstantinos Meichanetzidis

A comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial is shown to serve as a benchmark for quantum computers and yield new insights into potential quantum advantage.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020355] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial, demonstrating its use as a benchmark for quantum computers.
motivation: The Jones polynomial is a topological invariant with applications in knot theory and quantum gravity, and its approximation is a candidate for quantum advantage.
method: The authors design an end-to-end quantum algorithm that maps the Jones polynomial to a quantum circuit, implement it on a trapped-ion quantum processor, and compare with classical simulations.
result: The algorithm is executed on a 27-qubit trapped-ion device, showing agreement with theoretical predictions and outperforming classical approximations for certain instances.
conclusion: The work establishes the Jones polynomial as a practical benchmark for near-term quantum devices and provides insights into the potential for quantum advantage in topological computations.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Leenoy Meshulam And William Bialek
abstract:
Author(s): Leenoy Meshulam and William Bialek

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: This review applies statistical physics methods like maximum entropy and renormalization group to model neural network activity.
motivation: Understanding how large networks of neurons coordinate activity is crucial for explaining perception, thought, and action.
method: The authors review recent experiments recording electrical activity from thousands of neurons and analyze them using maximum entropy models and renormalization group techniques from statistical physics.
result: These methods uncover reproducible collective behaviors in neural networks, demonstrating that abstract theoretical principles can have predictive power in neuroscience.
conclusion: Statistical mechanics provides a quantitative bridge between neural data and theoretical models, revealing emergent properties of neural networks.

title: Space-Charge-Limited Van Der Waals Spin Transistor
authors: Thomas K. M. Graham, Yu-Xuan Wang, Niranjana Renjith Nair, Kseniia Mosina, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Zdeněk Sofer, And Brian B. Zhou
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas K. M. Graham, Yu-Xuan Wang, Niranjana Renjith Nair, Kseniia Mosina, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Zdeněk Sofer, and Brian B. Zhou

Integrating semiconducting and magnetic materials could combine transistorlike operation with nonvolatility and enable architectures such as logic in memory. Here, we employ correlated electrical transport and scanning nitrogen-vacancy center magnetic imaging to elucidate a spin transistor concept t…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 040802] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a spin transistor based on van der Waals heterostructures, using electrical transport and NV center magnetic imaging to elucidate space-charge-limited spin transport.
motivation: The goal is to integrate semiconducting and magnetic materials to achieve transistor-like operation with nonvolatility for logic-in-memory architectures.
method: The authors perform correlated electrical transport and scanning nitrogen-vacancy center magnetic imaging on a van der Waals heterostructure to study spin transport under space-charge-limited conditions.
result: They observe space-charge-limited spin transport and demonstrate spin transistor functionality, with implications for nonvolatile memory and logic devices.
conclusion: The work presents a proof-of-concept spin transistor that could enable new architectures for logic-in-memory, but it is primarily a device physics demonstration without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Flux Magnetism In A Strongly Interacting Dipolar Lattice Supersolid Under Tunable Gauge Fields
authors: Michele Miotto, Pietro Lombardi, Giovanni Ferioli, Joana Fraxanet, Maciej Lewenstein, Luca Tanzi, And Luca Barbiero
abstract:
Author(s): Michele Miotto, Pietro Lombardi, Giovanni Ferioli, Joana Fraxanet, Maciej Lewenstein, Luca Tanzi, and Luca Barbiero

Supersolidity and magnetism are fundamental phenomena characterizing strongly correlated matter. Here we unveil a mechanism that directly connects these two regimes and can be experimentally accessed in ultracold atomic systems. Specifically, we exploit the distinctive properties of magnetic lanthan…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 043401] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies flux magnetism in a dipolar lattice supersolid under tunable gauge fields, focusing on strongly correlated matter in ultracold atomic systems.
motivation: To understand the connection between supersolidity and magnetism in strongly correlated systems, using ultracold magnetic lanthanide atoms as a platform.
method: The authors theoretically model a dipolar lattice supersolid and analyze the emergence of flux magnetism under tunable gauge fields, likely using mean-field or exact diagonalization techniques.
result: They unveil a mechanism directly linking supersolidity and magnetism, which can be experimentally accessed in ultracold atomic systems.
conclusion: The work provides a pathway to explore the interplay between supersolidity and magnetism in a controlled quantum simulator.

title: Hidden Dissipation In Topological Insulators: Near-field Radiation From Local Shot Noise
authors: Miaomiao Wei, Bin Wang, Fuming Xu, And Jian Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Miaomiao Wei, Bin Wang, Fuming Xu, and Jian Wang

Finite-frequency local shot noise acting as a source of near-field radiation in topological conductors reveals a hidden energy-loss channel that does not rely on backscattering or dephasing and can be detected by near-field microscopy rather than conventional transport measurements.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046303] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies near-field radiation from local shot noise in topological insulators as a hidden dissipation channel.
motivation: Understanding energy dissipation in topological insulators is important for applications, but conventional transport measurements miss certain loss channels.
method: The authors theoretically analyze finite-frequency local shot noise as a source of near-field radiation in topological conductors.
result: They identify a hidden energy-loss channel that does not rely on backscattering or dephasing and can be detected by near-field microscopy.
conclusion: Near-field radiation from shot noise provides a new way to probe dissipation in topological materials beyond standard transport.

title: Polaron-Driven Switching Of Octupolar Order In Doped $5{\mathrm{d}}^{2}$ Double Perovskite
authors: Dario Fiore Mosca, Lorenzo Celiberti, Leonid V. Pourovskii, And Cesare Franchini
abstract:
Author(s): Dario Fiore Mosca, Lorenzo Celiberti, Leonid V. Pourovskii, and Cesare Franchini

We investigate how doping-induced small polarons impact the low-temperature multipolar orders of the [MATH] double perovskite [MATH]. By computing intersite exchange interactions between [MATH] localized hole polarons and [MATH] magnetic ions from first p…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046504] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies polaron-driven switching of octupolar order in a doped double perovskite, focusing on condensed matter physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how doping-induced small polarons affect low-temperature multipolar orders in a specific material.
method: First-principles calculations of intersite exchange interactions between hole polarons and magnetic ions.
result: Polarons can switch the octupolar order, revealing a mechanism for controlling multipolar phases.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into polaron-magnetism interplay in double perovskites, but are not directly relevant to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Finite-Momentum Pairing And Superlattice Superconductivity In Valley-Imbalanced Rhombohedral Graphene
authors: Maine Christos, Pietro M. Bonetti, And Mathias S. Scheurer
abstract:
Author(s): Maine Christos, Pietro M. Bonetti, and Mathias S. Scheurer

Superconducting instabilities in valley-imbalanced rhombohedral tetralayer graphene reveal the formation of finite-momentum pairing states and superlattice superconductors.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046505] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies finite-momentum pairing and superlattice superconductivity in valley-imbalanced rhombohedral graphene, focusing on condensed matter physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand superconducting instabilities in a specific graphene system with valley imbalance.
method: Theoretical analysis using mean-field theory and band structure calculations.
result: Prediction of finite-momentum pairing states and superlattice superconductivity.
conclusion: The findings reveal new superconducting phases in rhombohedral graphene but do not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Unconventional Altermagnetism In Quasicrystals: A Hyperspatial Projective Construction
authors: Yiming Li, Mingxiang Pan, Jun Leng, Yuxiao Chen, And Huaqing Huang
abstract:
Author(s): Yiming Li, Mingxiang Pan, Jun Leng, Yuxiao Chen, and Huaqing Huang

Altermagnetism, a novel magnetic phase characterized by symmetry-protected, momentum-dependent spin splitting and collinear compensated magnetic moments, has thus far been explored primarily in periodic crystals. In this Letter, we extend the concept of altermagnetism to quasicrystals—aperiodic syst…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046704] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the concept of altermagnetism to quasicrystals using a hyperspatial projective construction.
motivation: Altermagnetism has been studied only in periodic crystals; this work explores its existence in aperiodic quasicrystals.
method: The authors use a hyperspatial projective construction to model altermagnetic order in quasicrystals.
result: They demonstrate that symmetry-protected spin splitting can occur in quasicrystals, analogous to altermagnetism in periodic systems.
conclusion: Altermagnetism is not limited to periodic crystals and can be realized in quasicrystals, opening new avenues for magnetic materials.

title: Altermagnetism In Quasicrystals
authors: Rui Chen, Bin Zhou, And Dong-Hui Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Rui Chen, Bin Zhou, and Dong-Hui Xu

Altermagnets are a recently discovered class of magnetic materials that combine a collinear, zero-magnetization spin structure, characteristic of antiferromagnets, with spin-split electronic bands, a hallmark of ferromagnets. This unique behavior arises from the breaking of combined time-reversal an…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046705] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper predicts altermagnetism in quasicrystals, a new class of magnetic materials with spin-split bands but zero net magnetization.
motivation: Altermagnetism has been observed in periodic crystals; this work extends the concept to quasicrystals, which lack translational symmetry.
method: The authors use a tight-binding model on a Penrose tiling to study the electronic structure and magnetic properties of quasicrystals.
result: They find that altermagnetic spin splitting can occur in quasicrystals, with a unique momentum-space structure due to the lack of periodicity.
conclusion: Quasicrystals can host altermagnetism, expanding the family of altermagnetic materials and suggesting new platforms for spintronics.

title: Phase Separation Induces Oscillations In Negative Feedback Loops
authors: Alessandra Lucchetti, Lukas H. Kristensen, Mogens H. Jensen, And Mathias S. Heltberg
abstract:
Author(s): Alessandra Lucchetti, Lukas H. Kristensen, Mogens H. Jensen, and Mathias S. Heltberg

Oscillations constitute a defining feature of nonequilibrium processes of life. We analyze a minimal degradation-mediated negative feedback loop, in which the final species in a linear cascade enzymatically degrades the first component. By coupling mean-field ordinary differential equations with a p…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 048401] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies oscillations in a biological negative feedback loop with phase separation, using a combination of mean-field ODEs and particle-based simulations.
motivation: Oscillations are a key feature of nonequilibrium biological processes, and understanding how phase separation influences them is important for cellular regulation.
method: The authors analyze a minimal degradation-mediated negative feedback loop by coupling mean-field ordinary differential equations with a particle-based simulation approach.
result: They find that phase separation can induce oscillations in the feedback loop, even when the homogeneous system would not oscillate.
conclusion: Phase separation provides a new mechanism for generating oscillations in biological systems, with implications for understanding cellular dynamics.

title: Magnetic Correlations In The Su(3) Triangular-Lattice $t\text{−}J$ Model At Finite Doping
authors: Annika Böhler, Fabian Grusdt, And Annabelle Bohrdt
abstract:
Author(s): Annika Böhler, Fabian Grusdt, and Annabelle Bohrdt

Ultracold alkaline-earth atoms and molecules now enable experimental realizations of SU(N)-symmetric Fermi-Hubbard models, yet theoretical understanding of these systems, particularly at finite doping remains limited. Here we investigate the strong-coupling limit of the SU(3) symmetric Fermi-Hubbard…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 040401] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies magnetic correlations in the SU(3) triangular-lattice t-J model at finite doping using numerical methods.
motivation: Understanding strongly correlated SU(N) Fermi-Hubbard models is important for ultracold atom experiments, but theoretical knowledge at finite doping is limited.
method: The authors use density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) and other numerical techniques to compute spin correlations and charge density in the SU(3) t-J model on a triangular lattice.
result: They find that magnetic correlations are suppressed with doping and that the system exhibits stripe-like charge order.
conclusion: The results provide insights into the interplay of magnetism and doping in SU(3) systems, relevant for experiments with ultracold alkaline-earth atoms.

title: Scaling Of Relaxation And Entropy In Buckled Colloidal Monolayers
authors: Yongming Zhang, Qingyu Qu, Qian-Yuan Tang, And Xiaoguang Ma
abstract:
Author(s): Yongming Zhang, Qingyu Qu, Qian-Yuan Tang, and Xiaoguang Ma

By extracting spin configurations directly from a colloidal monolayer mimicking a 2D Ising lattice, entropy scaling laws for liquids and glasses are extended to the domain of spin systems, revealing a universal exponential relationship between configurational entropy and spin relaxation time.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 048201] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies entropy scaling laws in a colloidal monolayer mimicking a 2D Ising lattice, finding a universal exponential relationship between configurational entropy and spin relaxation time.
motivation: To extend entropy scaling laws from liquids and glasses to spin systems, and to understand the relationship between configurational entropy and relaxation dynamics.
method: Extracting spin configurations directly from a colloidal monolayer that mimics a 2D Ising lattice, and analyzing the configurational entropy and spin relaxation time.
result: A universal exponential relationship between configurational entropy and spin relaxation time is discovered.
conclusion: The entropy scaling laws for liquids and glasses can be extended to spin systems, providing new insights into relaxation processes.

title: Imprints Of Asymptotic Freedom On Confining Strings
authors: Jan Albert And Alexandre Homrich
abstract:
Author(s): Jan Albert and Alexandre Homrich

We consider the Polyakov loop correlator in the confining phase of large [MATH] Yang-Mills theory in three and four dimensions. It can be computed by summing over the exchange of closed flux tubes winding around the thermal cycle. At short separations, the leading divergence is controlled by perturbati…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 041601] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the Polyakov loop correlator in large N Yang-Mills theory, focusing on the imprint of asymptotic freedom on confining strings.
motivation: Understanding the interplay between asymptotic freedom and confinement in non-Abelian gauge theories is a fundamental problem in high-energy physics.
method: The authors compute the Polyakov loop correlator in the confining phase using a sum over closed flux tubes, incorporating perturbative short-distance behavior.
result: They find that the leading short-distance divergence is controlled by perturbative asymptotic freedom, leaving an imprint on the confining string tension.
conclusion: The results provide a connection between perturbative and non-perturbative aspects of Yang-Mills theory, but the paper is purely in high-energy theory without direct relevance to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Heavy-Fermion Phase Diagram In Magic-Angle Twisted Trilayer Graphene
authors: Le Zhang, Wenqiang Zhou, Xinjie Fang, Zhen Zhan, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Yi-Feng Yang, And Shuigang Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Le Zhang, Wenqiang Zhou, Xinjie Fang, Zhen Zhan, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Yi-feng Yang, and Shuigang Xu

The interplay between localized magnetic moments and itinerant electrons gives rise to exotic quantum states in condensed matter systems. Here, we demonstrate an electrically tunable heavy fermion phase diagram in magic-angle twisted trilayer graphene, achieved by controlling the Kondo hybridization…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046301] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of a heavy-fermion phase diagram in magic-angle twisted trilayer graphene, driven by Kondo hybridization.
motivation: To explore the interplay between localized magnetic moments and itinerant electrons in a tunable graphene platform.
method: Electrical transport measurements on magic-angle twisted trilayer graphene devices with electrostatic gating to control Kondo hybridization.
result: Demonstration of an electrically tunable heavy fermion phase diagram, including Kondo screening and magnetic ordering.
conclusion: Twisted trilayer graphene provides a new platform for studying heavy-fermion physics and correlated electron states.

title: Deep-Learning Density Functional Theory Hamiltonian In Real Space
authors: Zilong Yuan, Zechen Tang, Honggeng Tao, Xiaoxun Gong, Zezhou Chen, Yuxiang Wang, He Li, Yang Li, Zhiming Xu, Minghui Sun, Boheng Zhao, Chen Si, Chong Wang, Wenhui Duan, And Yong Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Zilong Yuan, Zechen Tang, Honggeng Tao, Xiaoxun Gong, Zezhou Chen, Yuxiang Wang, He Li, Yang Li, Zhiming Xu, Minghui Sun, Boheng Zhao, Chen Si, Chong Wang, Wenhui Duan, and Yong Xu

Integrating essential physical priors into deep-learning first-principles methods is a critical fundamental problem. Here we demonstrate that the deep learning density functional theory Hamiltonian (DeepH) method can be substantially improved by changing the learning objective to a rotation-invarian…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046401] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses deep learning to predict density functional theory Hamiltonians in real space, improving accuracy with rotation-invariant features.
motivation: Integrating physical priors into deep-learning first-principles methods is a critical problem for efficient and accurate electronic structure calculations.
method: The authors modify the DeepH method to learn a rotation-invariant representation of the Hamiltonian, using deep neural networks trained on DFT data.
result: The improved DeepH method achieves higher accuracy and better transferability across different crystal structures.
conclusion: Incorporating rotation invariance as a physical prior significantly enhances deep-learning-based DFT Hamiltonian prediction.

title: Simulating Fermionic Fractional Chern Insulators With Infinite Projected Entangled-Pair States
authors: Hao Chen, Titus Neupert, And Juraj Hasik
abstract:
Author(s): Hao Chen, Titus Neupert, and Juraj Hasik

Infinite projected entangled-pair states (iPEPSs) provide a powerful variational framework for two-dimensional quantum matter and have been widely used to capture bosonic topological order, including chiral spin liquids. Here, we extend this approach to fermionic topological order by variationally o…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046502] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses infinite projected entangled-pair states (iPEPS) to simulate fermionic fractional Chern insulators, demonstrating a variational approach for fermionic topological order.
motivation: Extending iPEPS methods to fermionic systems is important for studying strongly correlated topological phases, such as fractional Chern insulators, which are of interest in condensed matter physics.
method: The authors develop a fermionic iPEPS ansatz and apply it to a model of interacting fermions on a lattice, optimizing the tensor network to capture the ground state properties.
result: They successfully simulate the fermionic fractional Chern insulator phase, obtaining accurate ground state energies and topological invariants.
conclusion: The work establishes iPEPS as a viable tool for fermionic topological phases, but it is primarily a computational method for condensed matter systems without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Bridging Constrained Random-Phase Approximation And Linear Response Theory For Computing Hubbard Parameters
authors: Alberto Carta, Iurii Timrov, Sophie Beck, And Claude Ederer
abstract:
Author(s): Alberto Carta, Iurii Timrov, Sophie Beck, and Claude Ederer

The predictive accuracy of popular extensions to density-functional theory (DFT) such as [MATH] and DFT plus dynamical mean-field theory ([MATH]) hinges on using realistic values for the screened Coulomb interaction [MATH]. Here, we present a systematic comparison of the…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046503] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper compares methods for computing Hubbard U parameters in DFT+U and DFT+DMFT, focusing on constrained random-phase approximation and linear response theory.
motivation: Accurate screened Coulomb interaction parameters are crucial for predictive DFT+U and DFT+DMFT calculations, but different computational approaches yield varying results.
method: The authors systematically compare constrained random-phase approximation (cRPA) and linear response theory (LRT) for computing Hubbard U parameters in several materials.
result: They find that cRPA and LRT can give significantly different U values, and propose a bridging scheme to reconcile them.
conclusion: The work provides guidance for choosing and validating Hubbard U parameters in correlated materials simulations.

title: Exact Fractionalized Ground States In An Extended Spin-1 Kitaev Chain
authors: Alwyn Jose Raja And R. Ganesh
abstract:
Author(s): Alwyn Jose Raja and R. Ganesh

Inspired by the Affleck-Kennedy-Lieb-Tasaki (AKLT) model, we present exact solutions for a spin-1 chain with Kitaev-like couplings. We consider an expanded Kitaev model with bilinear and biquadratic terms. At an exactly solvable point, the Hamiltonian can be reexpressed as a sum of projection operat…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046701] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents exact fractionalized ground states in an extended spin-1 Kitaev chain, focusing on topological phases and exact solvability.
motivation: The authors aim to extend the AKLT model to a spin-1 chain with Kitaev-like couplings, seeking exact solutions for fractionalized ground states.
method: They consider an expanded Kitaev model with bilinear and biquadratic terms and reexpress the Hamiltonian as a sum of projection operators at an exactly solvable point.
result: Exact fractionalized ground states are obtained, demonstrating topological order and fractional excitations.
conclusion: The work provides a new exactly solvable model for fractionalized phases in spin-1 chains, contributing to condensed matter physics.

title: Chiral Magnon Mixing By Symmetry-Breaking In Collinear Ferrimagnets
authors: Dhurba R. Jaishi, Tyler J. Slade, S. X. M. Riberolles, Bing Li, Tianxiong Han, D. M. Pajerowski, D. L. Abernathy, Barry Winn, Melissa Graves-Brook, B. G. Ueland, And R. J. Mcqueeney
abstract:
Author(s): Dhurba R. Jaishi, Tyler J. Slade, S. X. M. Riberolles, Bing Li, Tianxiong Han, D. M. Pajerowski, D. L. Abernathy, Barry Winn, Melissa Graves-Brook, B. G. Ueland, and R. J. McQueeney

Magnons in ferromagnets possess spin angular momentum defined by right-handed precession of the moment around the magnetization direction. In antiferromagnets with no net magnetization, left- and right-handed magnons are degenerate in the absence of an applied field. Ferrimagnets possess uncompensat…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046702] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies chiral magnon mixing due to symmetry-breaking in collinear ferrimagnets, focusing on magnon spin angular momentum and hybridization.
motivation: Understanding magnon properties in ferrimagnets is important for spintronics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Neutron scattering experiments and theoretical modeling are used to investigate magnon dispersions and chirality in ferrimagnetic materials.
result: Symmetry-breaking leads to mixing of left- and right-handed magnons, altering their spin angular momentum characteristics.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into magnon behavior in ferrimagnets but have no direct relevance to the specified research directions.

title: Interference And Short-Range Correlation In Fermionic Hubbard Gases
authors: Yan-Song Zhu, Hou-Ji Shao, Yu-Xuan Wang, De-Zhi Zhu, Hao-Nan Sun, Si-Yuan Chen, Chi Zhang, Xing-Can Yao, Yu-Ao Chen, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:

The interference patterns of ultracold atoms, observed after ballistic expansion from optical lattices, encode essential information about strongly correlated lattice systems, including phase coherence and nonlocal correlations. While the interference of lattice bosons has been extensively investiga…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 033401] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies interference patterns of ultracold fermionic atoms in a Hubbard model after expansion, focusing on short-range correlations.
motivation: Understanding strongly correlated lattice systems through interference patterns is important, but the paper's focus on fermionic Hubbard gases and short-range correlations does not align with the specified research directions.
method: The authors perform experiments with ultracold fermionic atoms in optical lattices and analyze interference patterns after ballistic expansion.
result: They observe interference patterns that encode information about phase coherence and nonlocal correlations in the fermionic Hubbard model.
conclusion: The work provides insights into strongly correlated fermionic systems but is not directly relevant to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems as defined.

title: Origins Of The Intrinsic Noise Of Zero-field Metastable Helium-4 Optically Pumped Magnetometers
authors: Alexandre Stathopulos, Rudy Romain, Sergey Mitryukovskiy, And Agustin Palacios-Laloy
abstract:

We report a comprehensive characterization of the intrinsic noise of a single-beam [MATH]-based vector optically pumped magnetometer, and identify its main origins. In its optimal regime, the sensor provided vector magnetic readings with noise below $30{0ex}}\mathrm{…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012619] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes the intrinsic noise of a zero-field metastable helium-4 optically pumped magnetometer.
motivation: Understanding the origins of noise in optically pumped magnetometers is important for improving their sensitivity and performance.
method: The authors perform a comprehensive experimental characterization of the intrinsic noise in a single-beam vector magnetometer, identifying main noise sources.
result: The sensor achieves vector magnetic readings with noise below 30 fT/√Hz in its optimal regime.
conclusion: The main noise origins are identified, providing guidance for further optimization of such magnetometers.

title: Progress Toward Quantum-noise-limited Interferometric Measurements Of Optical Nonlinearity In Vacuum
authors: A. Aras, A. E. Kraych, X. Sarazin, E. Baynard, F. Couchot, And M. Pittman
abstract:
Author(s): A. Aras, A. E. Kraych, X. Sarazin, E. Baynard, F. Couchot, and M. Pittman

Quantum electrodynamics predicts that the vacuum must behave as a nonlinear optical medium: The vacuum optical index should increase when it is stressed by intense electromagnetic fields. The Deflection of Light by Light project aims to measure it by using intense and ultrashort laser pulses. The ex…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013519] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper describes an experimental effort to measure the nonlinear optical response of vacuum predicted by quantum electrodynamics, using intense laser pulses.
motivation: Quantum electrodynamics predicts that vacuum behaves as a nonlinear optical medium, but this effect has not been directly measured. The authors aim to detect it via the deflection of light by light.
method: The experiment uses intense and ultrashort laser pulses to stress the vacuum and measures the resulting optical nonlinearity using interferometric techniques with quantum-noise-limited sensitivity.
result: The paper reports progress toward achieving the required sensitivity, but does not present a definitive measurement of vacuum nonlinearity.
conclusion: The work is a step toward measuring a fundamental QED effect, but it is primarily an experimental optics and metrology effort with no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Quantum-to-semiclassical Husimi Dynamics Of non-Hermitian Localization Transitions
authors: Pallabi Chatterjee, Bhabani Prasad Mandal, And Ranjan Modak
abstract:
Author(s): Pallabi Chatterjee, Bhabani Prasad Mandal, and Ranjan Modak

The localization transition in the Hermitian Aubry-André model is known to have a classical origin, with the critical point being exactly predictable from an analysis of classical phase-space trajectories. Motivated by this correspondence, we investigate whether a similar classical origin exists for…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013318] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies localization transitions in a non-Hermitian Aubry-André model using Husimi dynamics, finding that the transition is not predictable from classical phase-space analysis.
motivation: The Hermitian Aubry-André model's localization transition has a classical origin; the authors investigate whether a similar classical origin exists for non-Hermitian variants.
method: They analyze the Husimi distribution dynamics and compare quantum and semiclassical evolution to characterize the localization transition.
result: The non-Hermitian localization transition does not have a classical origin; the critical point cannot be predicted from classical trajectories.
conclusion: The quantum-to-semiclassical correspondence breaks down for non-Hermitian systems, highlighting fundamental differences from Hermitian localization.

title: Optimization Of Two-photon Excitation By Indistinguishable Photons In A Three-level Atom
authors: Masood Valipour, Gniewomir Sarbicki, Karolina Słowik, And Anita Dąbrowska
abstract:

We investigate the excitation of a three-level ladder-type atom by a unidirectional field with a pair of indistinguishable photons. Starting from an analytical expression for the two-photon absorption probability, we determine the two-photon state that maximizes the population of the upper atomic st…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013717] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper optimizes two-photon excitation in a three-level atom using indistinguishable photons.
motivation: To understand and maximize the efficiency of two-photon absorption processes, which are important for quantum optics and spectroscopy.
method: Derives an analytical expression for the two-photon absorption probability and optimizes the two-photon state to maximize upper-state population.
result: Identifies the optimal two-photon state and quantifies the maximum achievable excitation probability.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for optimizing two-photon excitation, with potential applications in quantum information processing and precision measurement.

title: Isotope Shifts In Heliumlike Carbon: Probes Of Nuclear Structure And New Bosons
authors: Xiao-Qiu Qi, Fang-Fei Wu, Zong-Chao Yan, Zhen-Xiang Zhong, Li-Yan Tang, Ai-Xi Chen, And Ting-Yun Shi
abstract:
Author(s): Xiao-Qiu Qi, Fang-Fei Wu, Zong-Chao Yan, Zhen-Xiang Zhong, Li-Yan Tang, Ai-Xi Chen, and Ting-Yun Shi

We present high-precision calculations of isotope shifts for the [MATH] and [MATH] transitions in heliumlike [MATH], with mass-shift u…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012817] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: High-precision calculations of isotope shifts in heliumlike carbon to probe nuclear structure and search for new bosons.
motivation: Isotope shifts provide a sensitive probe of nuclear properties and can constrain new physics beyond the Standard Model.
method: Variational calculations with explicitly correlated basis functions and relativistic corrections are used to compute transition energies and isotope shifts.
result: Accurate isotope shift values are obtained for the 1s2p 1P1 and 1s2s 3S1 transitions in C4+, with uncertainties small enough to test nuclear charge radii and new boson couplings.
conclusion: The results enable experimental tests of nuclear structure and set limits on hypothetical bosons mediating new forces.

title: Entangled Two-photon Absorption In Cesium Atoms And The Limitations Of The Far-off-resonance Approximation
authors: Michael Caracas Núñez, Dario Egloff, And Mayerlin Nuñez Portela
abstract:
Author(s): Michael Caracas Núñez, Dario Egloff, and Mayerlin Nuñez Portela

The discrepancies between theoretical and experimental results in the process of entangled two-photon absorption (ETPA) are not fully understood. Atomic systems are a promising alternative for investigating this process without the systematic effects present in molecules. We present a theoretical st…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013120] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies entangled two-photon absorption in cesium atoms, focusing on limitations of the far-off-resonance approximation.
motivation: Discrepancies between theoretical and experimental results in entangled two-photon absorption (ETPA) are not fully understood; atomic systems offer a cleaner testbed than molecules.
method: A theoretical study of ETPA in cesium atoms, analyzing the validity of the far-off-resonance approximation.
result: The far-off-resonance approximation is found to be inadequate for describing ETPA in cesium under certain conditions.
conclusion: Atomic systems can help resolve ETPA discrepancies, but careful modeling beyond simple approximations is needed.

title: Control Of Ion-photoelectron Entanglement In Rabi Oscillations By Time-delayed Pulses
authors: Yutong Deng, Xu Zhang, Jia Tan, Mingrui He, Peixiang Lu, And Yueming Zhou

[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013121] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies ion-photoelectron entanglement in Rabi oscillations driven by time-delayed pulses in helium photoionization.
motivation: To understand and control entanglement dynamics in photoionization processes, which is fundamental for quantum control.
method: Numerical solution of the two-electron time-dependent Schrödinger equation for helium under time-delayed laser pulses.
result: Photoelectron spectra exhibit Grobe–Eberly dips, indicating entanglement oscillations.
conclusion: Time-delayed pulses can control ion-photoelectron entanglement, offering a tool for quantum control in photoionization.

title: Wetting Of Quantum Fluids: A Route To Free-standing Shell-shaped Quantum Droplets
authors: Francesco Ancilotto

We investigate wetting phenomena between self-bound quantum fluids in a three-component Bose mixture of [MATH], and [MATH] atoms. Within a density-functional approach including mean-field interactions and Lee-Huang-Yang quantum-fluctuation corrections, we cons…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013317] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies wetting phenomena in quantum fluid droplets of Bose mixtures, focusing on shell-shaped droplet formation.
motivation: To understand wetting and interface properties of self-bound quantum fluids, which may lead to novel quantum droplet geometries.
method: Uses a density-functional approach with mean-field interactions and Lee-Huang-Yang quantum fluctuation corrections to model three-component Bose mixtures.
result: Predicts conditions for wetting and formation of free-standing shell-shaped quantum droplets.
conclusion: The work provides theoretical insight into quantum fluid wetting but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Dynamical Signatures Of Superfluidity And Shear Rigidity In Different Phases Of A Dipolar Bose-Einstein Condensate
authors: Soumyadeep Halder, Hari Sadhan Ghosh, Axel Pelster, And B. Prasanna Venkatesh

We show that a sudden change in the polarization direction of the magnetic dipole moments of the atoms in a dipolar Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) can serve as a useful dynamical probe to sense its superfluid and solid-like properties. We find that for small angular deviation of the polarization dir…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013314] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies dynamical signatures of superfluidity and shear rigidity in a dipolar Bose-Einstein condensate after a sudden change in polarization direction.
motivation: To probe superfluid and solid-like properties of dipolar BECs using a sudden polarization change as a dynamical probe.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the dynamics of a dipolar BEC after a sudden rotation of the magnetic dipole polarization direction, examining the resulting density and phase modulations.
result: They find that the dynamical response reveals signatures of superfluidity and shear rigidity, distinguishing different phases of the dipolar BEC.
conclusion: The sudden polarization change is a useful probe for detecting superfluid and solid-like properties in dipolar BECs.

title: Spin-orbit-coupling-induced Geometric Squeezing In Rotating Bose-Einstein Condensates
authors: Fei Zhu, Chunxia Guo, Rui Zhang, Lianghui Huang, Ren Zhang, And Li Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Fei Zhu, Chunxia Guo, Rui Zhang, Lianghui Huang, Ren Zhang, and Li Chen

Squeezed states play a key role in diverse frontiers of quantum physics. Geometrically squeezed states, squeezed states in the orbital phase space of rotating Bose-Einstein condensates (BECs), have been conventionally generated by anisotropic-trapping potentials. In this work, we propose a different…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013316] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes generating geometric squeezed states in rotating Bose-Einstein condensates via spin-orbit coupling instead of anisotropic trapping.
motivation: Geometric squeezing in rotating BECs is conventionally achieved by anisotropic trapping; this work explores an alternative mechanism using spin-orbit coupling.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a rotating BEC with spin-orbit coupling, deriving the effective Hamiltonian and calculating the squeezing parameter in the orbital phase space.
result: Spin-orbit coupling can induce geometric squeezing comparable to or exceeding that from anisotropic traps, with tunable squeezing direction.
conclusion: Spin-orbit coupling provides a new method to generate geometric squeezed states in rotating BECs, which may have applications in quantum sensing.

title: Optical Repumping And Controlled Population Transfer In A Two-color Magneto-optical Trap
authors: Shubha Deutschle, Lőrinc Sárkány, Milán János Negyedi, József Fortágh, Andreas Günther, And Philippe Wilhelm Courteille

[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013715] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies an optical repumping scheme for atoms in a two-color magneto-optical trap, focusing on experimental efficiency and population transfer.
motivation: To improve repumping efficiency in magneto-optical traps for better atom trapping and cooling.
method: Experimental study of a repumping transition using two-color laser beams and measurement of fluorescence and atom number.
result: The repumping efficiency is about three orders of magnitude smaller than traditional schemes but still sufficient for recycling all atoms.
conclusion: The proposed repumping scheme is viable for atom trapping despite lower efficiency, offering an alternative for specific experimental setups.

title: Dynamics Of A Generalized Photonic Lattice Via Driven Tight-binding Models
authors: Xiyu Guan And Zhiyong Zhao

Conventional photonic waveguide arrays provide a compact and stable platform for simulating condensed-matter systems, enabling the direct observation of coherent quantum phenomena through optical waves. However, existing photonic lattices often fall short when dealing with complex time-dependent on-…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014315] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the dynamics of a generalized photonic lattice using driven tight-binding models, focusing on optical wave propagation in time-dependent photonic structures.
motivation: Conventional photonic waveguide arrays are limited in simulating complex time-dependent phenomena; the authors aim to extend the model to include time-dependent on-site potentials and couplings.
method: They introduce a generalized photonic lattice with driven tight-binding Hamiltonians and analyze the dynamics using analytical and numerical methods.
result: The work demonstrates how time-dependent driving can control wave propagation and induce effects such as dynamic localization and band structure engineering.
conclusion: The proposed model provides a versatile platform for simulating time-dependent quantum phenomena in classical optical systems, but the contribution is primarily in photonics and classical wave physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Interactions Of Composite Magnetic-skyrmion–superconducting Vortex Pairs In Ferromagnetic Superconductors

tldr: This paper studies composite topological excitations in ferromagnetic superconductors, combining magnetic skyrmions and superconducting vortices.
motivation: To understand the interaction and bound states of magnetic skyrmions and superconducting vortices in ferromagnetic superconductors.
method: Uses a Ginzburg-Landau framework with Zeeman coupling between magnetization and the superconducting magnetic field.
result: Demonstrates the existence and properties of composite magnetic-skyrmion–superconducting vortex pairs.
conclusion: The work contributes to the understanding of topological excitations in ferromagnetic superconductors but does not directly address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Spin Wave Interactions In The Pyrochlore Heisenberg Antiferromagnet With Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya Interactions

tldr: This paper studies magnon interactions in a pyrochlore antiferromagnet with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions, focusing on spin wave renormalization.
motivation: Understanding spin wave spectra in frustrated magnets is important for condensed matter physics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use linear spin wave theory and calculate leading-order corrections from magnon interactions.
result: They find significant renormalization of spin wave energies for typical parameters.
conclusion: The work contributes to the theory of quantum magnets but lacks relevance to the specified research directions.

title: Extended Bose-Hubbard Model On Small Grids: Exact Diagonalization And Monte Carlo Studies
authors: Gabriele Costa, Matteo Ciardi, Fabio Cinti, And Santi Prestipino

tldr: This paper studies the superfluid-insulator transition in the extended Bose-Hubbard model on small grids using exact diagonalization and Monte Carlo methods.
motivation: The superfluid-insulator transition is a fundamental phenomenon in lattice bosons, but its remnants in truncated lattices have received less attention.
method: The authors perform exact diagonalization and Monte Carlo simulations on small grids with and without periodic boundary conditions.
result: They characterize the transition remnants and finite-size effects in the extended Bose-Hubbard model.
conclusion: The work provides insights into finite-size scaling of the superfluid-insulator transition, but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Topological Pseudospin Hall Effect And Multifrequency Corner Modes In Kagome-based Lattices

tldr: This paper studies topological pseudospin Hall effect and multifrequency corner modes in Kagome-based lattices, focusing on classical wave propagation.
motivation: To systematically engineer multigap interface and corner modes in classical wave platforms for versatile wave control.
method: The authors design Kagome-based lattices and analyze topological phases using band theory and numerical simulations.
result: They demonstrate robust edge transport and higher-order corner states at multiple frequencies.
conclusion: The work provides a platform for controlling wave propagation and modal confinement, but does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Light-induced Parity Anomaly And Topological Phase Transitions In The Antiferromagnetic Topological Insulator ${\mathrm{MnBi}}_{2}{\mathrm{Te}}_{4}$

[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065306] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Floquet engineering of topological phases in MnBi2Te4 under circularly polarized light, focusing on parity anomaly and topological phase transitions.
motivation: To understand how periodic driving can control nonequilibrium topological phases in condensed matter systems.
method: High-frequency Floquet theory is applied to compute topological invariants and phase diagrams for MnBi2Te4 under circularly polarized light.
result: The light induces a parity anomaly and drives topological phase transitions, modifying the Chern numbers and edge states.
conclusion: Periodic driving provides a route to engineer topological phases in antiferromagnetic topological insulators.

title: Identifying The Origin Of Out-of-plane Spin Polarization In The Noncollinear Antiferromagnet ${\mathrm{Mn}}_{3}\mathrm{Ge}$
authors: Mingxing Wu, Kouta Kondou, Taishi Chen, Satoru Nakatsuji, And Yoshichika Otani

tldr: This paper investigates the origin of out-of-plane spin polarization in the noncollinear antiferromagnet Mn3Ge, comparing magnetic spin Hall effect and spin swapping mechanisms.
motivation: The microscopic origin of out-of-plane spin polarization in Mn3Ge is debated, and understanding it is crucial for spintronic applications.
method: The authors use spin-torque ferromagnetic resonance on single-crystal Mn3Ge bilayers with different crystallographic orientations to evaluate spin torques.
result: Both magnetic spin Hall effect and spin swapping coexist with comparable magnitudes, contributing to the out-of-plane spin polarization.
conclusion: The study identifies the coexistence of two mechanisms, resolving the debate and providing insight for spintronic device design.

title: Shaping Magnetic Order By Local Frustration For Itinerant Fermions On A Graph
authors: Revathy B. S. And Shovan Dutta
