motivation: Understanding how lattice topology and frustration affect magnetic order in strongly correlated fermion systems.
method: The authors analyze a Hubbard model on a specific graph geometry, using analytical and numerical methods to study the ground state magnetic properties.
result: They find that local frustration can shape magnetic order, leading to novel phases not present in conventional lattices.
conclusion: The work highlights the role of lattice topology in kinetic magnetism, but is primarily a condensed matter physics result without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Mobility-edge-embedded Hofstadter Butterfly From A Tilt-induced Quasiperiodic Potential
authors: Sanghoon Lee And Kyoung-Min Kim
abstract:
Author(s): Sanghoon Lee and Kyoung-Min Kim

The Hofstadter butterfly (HB) and mobility edges (MEs) are hallmark phenomena of quasiperiodic systems, yet their interplay remains elusive. Here, we demonstrate their coexistence within a tilt-induced quasiperiodic potential on a square lattice, giving rise to a “mobility-edge-embedded Hofstadter b…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014207] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the coexistence of Hofstadter butterfly and mobility edges in a tilt-induced quasiperiodic potential on a square lattice.
motivation: The interplay between Hofstadter butterfly and mobility edges in quasiperiodic systems has been elusive; this work aims to demonstrate their coexistence.
method: The authors consider a tilt-induced quasiperiodic potential on a square lattice and analyze the resulting energy spectrum and localization properties.
result: They find a mobility-edge-embedded Hofstadter butterfly, where mobility edges appear within the fractal spectrum.
conclusion: The work reveals a new phenomenon combining two hallmark features of quasiperiodic systems, but it is primarily a condensed matter physics result without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Localization And Flat Bands In Bond-inflated Lattices
authors: Richard Berkovits
abstract:
Author(s): Richard Berkovits

We study localization and flat-band formation in lattices generated by repeated bond inflation of square, honeycomb, and triangular parent lattices. Replacing each bond by a finite tight-binding chain produces several distinct classes of flat bands: chain-induced flat bands at the eigenenergies of t…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014208] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies localization and flat-band formation in bond-inflated lattices, focusing on condensed matter physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how bond inflation in lattices leads to flat bands and localization, which are relevant to condensed matter physics.
method: The authors generate lattices by repeatedly replacing bonds with finite tight-binding chains and analyze the resulting band structures and localization properties.
result: They identify several classes of flat bands and localization phenomena in square, honeycomb, and triangular parent lattices.
conclusion: Bond inflation is a systematic way to produce flat bands and localized states, but the work does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Machine Learning Protocol To Identify Pairing Symmetries Via Quasiparticle Interference Imaging In Ising Superconductors
authors: Adam Hložný, Jozef Haniš, Martin Gmitra, And Marko Milivojević
abstract:
Author(s): Adam Hložný, Jozef Haniš, Martin Gmitra, and Marko Milivojević

Identifying the pairing symmetry in unconventional superconductors is essential for reliably characterizing their superconducting states and for enabling their integration into realistic quantum devices. Here, we introduce a machine-learning-guided strategy to determine pairing symmetry from quasipa…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024511] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses machine learning to identify pairing symmetries in Ising superconductors from quasiparticle interference imaging.
motivation: Identifying pairing symmetry in unconventional superconductors is crucial for characterizing superconducting states and enabling integration into quantum devices.
method: The authors introduce a machine-learning-guided strategy that analyzes quasiparticle interference patterns to determine the pairing symmetry.
result: The method successfully identifies pairing symmetries from simulated imaging data.
conclusion: Machine learning can effectively classify pairing symmetries, aiding in the characterization of superconductors for quantum applications.

title: Proximate Spin Liquid Ground State Arising From Competing Stripy And ${120}^{∘}$ Spin Correlations In The Triangular Quantum Antiferromagnet ${\mathrm{ErMgGaO}}_{4}$
authors: S. H.-Y. Huang, S. Petit, B. Yuan, Z. W. Cronkwright, C. Pinvidic, Y. Wang, E. M. Smith, S. Bhattacharya, C. Yang, J.-M. Zanotti, Q. Berrod, M. B. Stone, A. I. Kolesnikov, R. J. Cava, E. Kermarrec, And B. D. Gaulin
abstract:

[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034421] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports experimental observation of a proximate spin liquid ground state in the triangular quantum antiferromagnet ErMgGaO4, driven by competing stripy and 120° spin correlations.
motivation: To understand the nature of the ground state in a triangular lattice quantum antiferromagnet with strong frustration, which may host a quantum spin liquid.
method: The authors performed inelastic neutron scattering and elastic scattering measurements on powder samples, and analyzed the data using a theoretical J1-J2-JΔ model to extract spin Hamiltonian parameters.
result: They observed a continuum of inelastic scattering and two-dimensional Warren lineshapes, indicating proximity to a quantum phase boundary between a spin liquid and a stripy ordered phase.
conclusion: ErMgGaO4 is a candidate material for a quantum spin liquid ground state, with competing magnetic correlations preventing long-range order.

title: Hinge Modes Of Three-dimensional Euler Insulators
authors: Yutaro Tanaka And Shingo Kobayashi
abstract:
Author(s): Yutaro Tanaka and Shingo Kobayashi

In two-dimensional systems with space-time inversion symmetry, such as [MATH], the reality condition on wave functions gives rise to real band topology characterized by the Euler class, a [MATH]-valued topological invariant for a pair of real bands in the Brillouin zone. In this…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045120] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies hinge modes in three-dimensional Euler insulators, a topological phase of matter.
motivation: To understand the boundary signatures of real band topology characterized by the Euler class in three dimensions.
method: The authors analyze the topological properties of Euler insulators using theoretical models and compute hinge modes.
result: They find that three-dimensional Euler insulators host hinge modes protected by the Euler class.
conclusion: The work extends the concept of Euler topology to three dimensions and reveals novel hinge states.

title: Magnetoelectric Effect In Multiferroic Metals Via A Direct Spin-charge Interaction
authors: Zefei Han, Haojin Wang, And Yuanchang Li
abstract:
Author(s): Zefei Han, Haojin Wang, and Yuanchang Li

Much is known about the magnetoelectric effect of multiferroic insulators, yet little is understood about multiferroic metals. In this work, we propose a stacking engineering strategy based on monolayer magnets to construct multiferroic metals, with validation through first-principles calculations o…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045424] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a stacking engineering strategy to construct multiferroic metals and validates it via first-principles calculations.
motivation: Understanding the magnetoelectric effect in multiferroic metals is largely unexplored compared to insulators.
method: The authors use first-principles calculations to design and analyze stacked monolayer magnets.
result: They demonstrate a direct spin-charge interaction leading to a magnetoelectric effect in the proposed multiferroic metals.
conclusion: Stacking engineering is a viable route to realize multiferroic metals with potential applications.

title: Nonlocal Effects In Charge And Energy Transport With Dissipative Electrodes
authors: Rodolfo A. Jalabert
abstract:
Author(s): Rodolfo A. Jalabert

Recent advances in nanothermometry have led to an extension of the Landauer-Büttiker scattering theory to include the nonlocal dissipation associated with charge transport. Such a program is implemented by describing the inelastic scattering in the connecting electrodes within an electrostatically s…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045425] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends Landauer-Büttiker scattering theory to include nonlocal dissipation in charge transport with dissipative electrodes.
motivation: Recent advances in nanothermometry require a theoretical framework for nonlocal dissipation in charge transport.
method: The authors describe inelastic scattering in connecting electrodes within an electrostatic framework, extending the Landauer-Büttiker formalism.
result: A theory of nonlocal dissipation associated with charge transport is developed.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical basis for understanding nonlocal effects in charge and energy transport with dissipative electrodes.

title: Bipolarized Weyl Semimetals And Quantum Crystal Valley Hall Effect In Two-dimensional Altermagnetic Materials
authors: Chao-Yang Tan, Ze-Feng Gao, Huan-Cheng Yang, Kai Liu, Peng-Jie Guo, And Zhong-Yi Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Chao-Yang Tan, Ze-Feng Gao, Huan-Cheng Yang, Kai Liu, Peng-Jie Guo, and Zhong-Yi Lu

Magnetism and topology are two major areas of condensed matter physics. The combination of magnetism and topology gives rise to more novel physical effects, which have attracted strongly theoretical and experimental attention. Recently, the concept of altermagnetism has been introduced, characterize…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 055125] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies bipolarized Weyl semimetals and the quantum crystal valley Hall effect in two-dimensional altermagnetic materials.
motivation: To explore novel physical effects arising from the combination of magnetism and topology in altermagnetic materials.
method: First-principles calculations and theoretical analysis of electronic band structure and topological properties.
result: Prediction of bipolarized Weyl semimetals and a quantum crystal valley Hall effect in 2D altermagnets.
conclusion: The findings reveal new topological phases in altermagnetic materials, expanding the understanding of magnetism-topology interplay.

title: Probing non-Fermi-liquid Behavior Of A Composite Fermi Liquid Via Efficient Thermal Simulations
authors: Bin-Bin Chen, Hongyu Lu, And Zi Yang Meng
abstract:
Author(s): Bin-Bin Chen, Hongyu Lu, and Zi Yang Meng

The physics of two-dimensional electron gas in a perpendicular magnetic field, i.e., the quantum Hall system, is remarkably rich. At half filling of the lowest Landau level, it has been predicted that “composite fermions”—emergent quasiparticles consisting of an electron attached to two magnetic flu…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065127] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses thermal simulations to study non-Fermi-liquid behavior in composite Fermi liquids in quantum Hall systems.
motivation: Understanding the low-energy properties of composite fermions at half filling of the lowest Landau level is a key challenge in condensed matter physics.
method: The authors perform efficient thermal simulations, likely using tensor network or Monte Carlo methods, to compute thermodynamic quantities.
result: They observe signatures of non-Fermi-liquid behavior, such as anomalous temperature dependence of specific heat or compressibility.
conclusion: The composite Fermi liquid exhibits non-Fermi-liquid behavior, providing insights into the nature of the quantum Hall state at half filling.

title: Raman Spectroscopy Of The Van Der Waals Topological Magnet GdGaI
authors: Nan Jiang, Yijin Zhang, Yujie Xia, Tomo Higashihara, Ryutaro Okuma, Jun-Ichi Yamaura, Yoshinori Okada, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Tiantian Zhang, Tomoki Machida, And Yasuhiro Niimi
abstract:

We report polarization-resolved Raman spectroscopy of a van der Waals compound [MATH] that is a candidate for excitonic insulators. By combining the symmetry analysis with density functional theory calculations, we identify six Raman-active phonons. The spectra exhibit only the expected an…

tldr: This paper reports polarization-resolved Raman spectroscopy of the van der Waals topological magnet GdGaI, identifying six Raman-active phonons via symmetry analysis and DFT calculations.
motivation: To characterize the phonon modes of GdGaI, a candidate excitonic insulator, using Raman spectroscopy.
method: Polarization-resolved Raman spectroscopy combined with symmetry analysis and density functional theory calculations.
result: Six Raman-active phonons were identified, and the spectra matched expectations from symmetry analysis.
conclusion: The study provides a detailed phonon characterization of GdGaI, relevant for understanding its excitonic insulator properties.

title: $H$-linear Magnetoresistance In The ${t}^{2}$ Resistivity Regime Of Overdoped Infinite-layer Nickelate ${\mathrm{La}}_{1x}{\mathrm{Sr}}_{x}{\mathrm{NiO}}_{2}$
authors: Yong-Cheng Pan, Tommy Kotte, Toni Helm, Motoki Osada, Atsushi Tsukazaki, And Yu-Te Hsu
abstract:

We report a systematic magnetotransport study on high-crystallinity [MATH] (LSNO) thin films with [MATH]. By conducting pulsed-field transport experiment up to 62 T, we reveal two salient features of the normal-state transport in overdoped LSN…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L020508] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports magnetotransport measurements on overdoped infinite-layer nickelate thin films, revealing H-linear magnetoresistance in the T^2 resistivity regime.
motivation: To understand the normal-state transport properties of overdoped infinite-layer nickelates, which are relevant to high-temperature superconductivity.
method: Pulsed-field magnetotransport experiments up to 62 T on high-crystallinity La1-xSrxNiO2 thin films.
result: Observation of H-linear magnetoresistance in the T^2 resistivity regime, indicating a possible quantum linear magnetoresistance mechanism.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into the electronic structure and scattering mechanisms in overdoped nickelates, but the paper focuses on condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Ground State Properties Of The Doped Kitaev-Heisenberg Chain: Topological Superconducting And Mott-insulating Phases Driven By Magnetic Frustration
authors: Cliò Efthimia Agrapidis And Satoshi Nishimoto
abstract:
Author(s): Cliò Efthimia Agrapidis and Satoshi Nishimoto

We study the hole-doped Kitaev-Heisenberg chain using the density-matrix renormalization group. In the Kitaev-only limit, the bond-directional exchange itself promotes pairing, favoring spin-singlet and spin-triplet superconducting tendencies for antiferromagnetic and ferromagnetic Kitaev couplings,…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L051109] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the doped Kitaev-Heisenberg chain, focusing on topological superconducting and Mott-insulating phases driven by magnetic frustration.
motivation: To understand the interplay of magnetic frustration and hole doping in Kitaev-Heisenberg chains, which may lead to exotic superconducting phases.
method: The authors use density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) to numerically study the ground state properties of the doped Kitaev-Heisenberg chain.
result: They find that bond-directional exchange promotes pairing, leading to spin-singlet and spin-triplet superconducting tendencies depending on the sign of the Kitaev coupling.
conclusion: The Kitaev-Heisenberg chain exhibits rich phase diagram with topological superconducting and Mott-insulating phases, driven by magnetic frustration.

title: Phenomenological Formulation Of Hybrid Transverse Magnetothermoelectric Conversion In Artificially Tilted Multilayers
authors: Fuyuki Ando, Yebin Lee, Takamasa Hirai, And Ken-Ichi Uchida
abstract:
Author(s): Fuyuki Ando, Yebin Lee, Takamasa Hirai, and Ken-ichi Uchida

Hybridizing multiple transverse thermoelectric effects in a single material synergistically enhances the dimensionless figure of merit for transverse thermoelectric conversion owing to the square-law characteristics of the superimposed transverse thermopowers. Here, we phenomenologically formulate t…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014420] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a phenomenological formulation of hybrid transverse magnetothermoelectric conversion in artificially tilted multilayers, focusing on thermoelectric figure of merit enhancement.
motivation: To understand and optimize hybrid transverse thermoelectric effects in multilayered structures for improved energy conversion efficiency.
method: The authors develop a phenomenological model based on the superposition of transverse thermopowers in artificially tilted multilayers, analyzing the square-law enhancement of the figure of merit.
result: The model predicts synergistic enhancement of the transverse thermoelectric figure of merit due to the square-law characteristics of superimposed thermopowers.
conclusion: The phenomenological formulation provides a framework for designing materials with enhanced transverse thermoelectric conversion, but the work is primarily in condensed matter physics and materials science without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: High-field Crossover From Linear To Nonlinear Magnetoelectric Effect In ${\mathrm{Co}}_{3}{\mathrm{O}}_{4}$
authors: S. Ghara, Y. Kinoshita, A. Miyake, Y. Ishii, L. Prodan, V. Tsurkan, Y. Skourski, J. Wosnitza, Y. H. Matsuda, S. Miyahara, M. Tokunaga, And I. Kézsmárki

tldr: This paper reports experimental observation of a crossover from linear to nonlinear magnetoelectric effect in Co3O4 under high magnetic fields.
motivation: To understand the magnetoelectric coupling in Co3O4, a simple antiferromagnet with linear magnetoelectric effect, and explore nonlinear behavior at high fields.
method: Magnetization and electric polarization measurements on single crystals of Co3O4 under pulsed high magnetic fields up to 60 T.
result: A crossover from linear to nonlinear magnetoelectric effect is observed at high fields, with the electric polarization showing quadratic dependence on magnetic field.
conclusion: The nonlinear magnetoelectric effect in Co3O4 arises from field-induced spin canting and lattice distortions, providing insight into magnetoelectric mechanisms in antiferromagnets.

title: Sublattice Polarization And Filamentary Superconductivity In Strained Graphene
authors: Tao Zhou
abstract:
Author(s): Tao Zhou

Periodic strain engineering in monolayer graphene provides a versatile platform to generate colossal pseudomagnetic fields and flat pseudo-Landau levels directly in a single atomic sheet. While the electronic topology and transport properties of the normal state in these systems have been extensivel…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024509] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies sublattice polarization and filamentary superconductivity in strained graphene, focusing on electronic topology and transport properties.
motivation: To understand the interplay between strain-induced pseudomagnetic fields and superconductivity in graphene.
method: Theoretical analysis using a model for strained graphene with periodic strain engineering.
result: Predicts sublattice polarization and filamentary superconductivity in strained graphene.
conclusion: Strained graphene provides a platform for novel superconducting phases driven by pseudomagnetic fields.

title: Semiclassical Theory For Proximity-induced Superconducting Systems With Spin-orbit Coupling
authors: Zhen-Cheng Liao, Cong Xiao, Zhi Wang, And Qian Niu
abstract:
Author(s): Zhen-Cheng Liao, Cong Xiao, Zhi Wang, and Qian Niu

We develop a semiclassical theory of superconducting quasiparticles for proximity-induced superconducting systems, where spin-orbit coupling plays a critical role in shaping the quasiparticle dynamics. We reveal the structure of superconducting Berry curvatures in such systems, and derive the Berry …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024510] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: Develops a semiclassical theory for proximity-induced superconductivity with spin-orbit coupling, focusing on Berry curvatures of quasiparticles.
motivation: To understand the dynamics of superconducting quasiparticles in systems where spin-orbit coupling is significant, which is important for proximity-induced superconductivity.
method: Derives a semiclassical equation of motion for quasiparticles incorporating Berry curvatures from the Bogoliubov-de Gennes Hamiltonian with spin-orbit coupling.
result: Reveals the structure of superconducting Berry curvatures and their effect on quasiparticle dynamics.
conclusion: The semiclassical framework provides a useful tool for studying transport and topological properties in proximity-induced superconducting systems.

title: Effect Of Positional Disorder On Phase Transitions In Planar Josephson Networks With Two-band Superconducting Grains
authors: Jie Li And Hai Huang
abstract:
Author(s): Jie Li and Hai Huang

The critical behavior of two-dimensional Josephson-junction network with the positional disorder is studied via Monte Carlo simulations. We consider a two-band model in which each superconducting grain is randomly displaced from its ideal position on a square lattice and the effective strength of th…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034507] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies phase transitions in disordered planar Josephson networks with two-band superconducting grains using Monte Carlo simulations.
motivation: To understand how positional disorder affects the critical behavior of Josephson-junction networks, which is relevant for superconducting materials.
method: Monte Carlo simulations of a two-band model on a square lattice with random displacements of superconducting grains.
result: The critical temperature and scaling behavior are modified by disorder, with a shift in the phase transition.
conclusion: Positional disorder significantly impacts the phase transition properties of two-band Josephson networks, which may inform the design of superconducting devices.

title: Beyond The Random Phase Approximation In Electron-hole Bilayer Superfluidity

We derive the normal and anomalous proper polarization functions and the screened Coulomb interactions in a two-dimensional superfluid electron-hole bilayer, including all first-order corrections beyond the Random Phase Approximation (RPA) at zero temperature. [Phys. Rev. B 114, 034508] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies electron-hole bilayer superfluidity beyond the random phase approximation, focusing on condensed matter physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To improve the description of superfluidity in electron-hole bilayers by including corrections beyond RPA, which are important for understanding exciton condensation.
method: Derives normal and anomalous proper polarization functions and screened Coulomb interactions including all first-order corrections beyond RPA at zero temperature.
result: Obtains modified polarization functions and screened interactions that go beyond the standard RPA treatment.
conclusion: The work provides a more accurate theoretical framework for electron-hole bilayer superfluidity, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Muonium Reaction In ${\mathrm{La}}_{2}{\mathrm{O}}_{3}$: Investigation Of The Last Steps In Muon Implantation

We report on a muon spin rotation study of the wide band-gap material [MATH]. The focus is on the implantation process and the configurations formed at the end of the implantation trajectory. The data are analyzed in the recently developed “doorway model.” First-principl…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045205] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies muonium reactions in La2O3 using muon spin rotation, focusing on the implantation process and final configurations.
motivation: Understanding the last steps of muon implantation in wide band-gap materials is important for interpreting muon spin rotation experiments.
method: The authors analyze experimental muon spin rotation data using the 'doorway model' and first-principles calculations.
result: They identify the configurations formed at the end of the implantation trajectory and characterize the reaction dynamics.
conclusion: The study provides insights into muon behavior in La2O3, relevant for material science but not for quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Current-induced Spin-orbit Torque On The Surface Of A Transition Metal Dichalcogenide Connected To The Two-dimensional Ferromagnet ${\mathrm{CrI}}_{3}$: Effects Of Twisting And Gating
authors: Leyla Majidi, Azadeh Faridi, And Reza Asgari
abstract:
Author(s): Leyla Majidi, Azadeh Faridi, and Reza Asgari

Motivated by recent progress in employing two key classes of two-dimensional materials—topological insulators and transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs)—as spin sources for generating spin-orbit torque (SOT), we investigate current-induced spin polarization and the resulting SOT in bilayers compos…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045422] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies current-induced spin-orbit torque in a bilayer of transition metal dichalcogenide and ferromagnetic CrI3, focusing on twisting and gating effects.
motivation: To understand spin-orbit torque generation in two-dimensional heterostructures for potential spintronic applications.
method: The authors use first-principles calculations and a model Hamiltonian to compute spin polarization and torque as functions of twist angle and gate voltage.
result: They find that the spin-orbit torque can be tuned by twisting and gating, with significant dependence on the interface geometry.
conclusion: Twisting and gating provide control over spin-orbit torque in TMDC/ferromagnet bilayers, which may be useful for spintronic devices.

title: Twistoptics In Planar Heterostructures With An Arbitrary Number Of Rotated Three-dimensional Thin Layers And Two-dimensional Conductive Sheets
authors: Christian Lanza, José Álvarez-Cuervo, Kirill V. Voronin, Gonzalo Álvarez-Pérez, Aitana Tarazaga Martín-Luengo, Javier Martín-Sánchez, Alexey Y. Nikitin, And Pablo Alonso-González

Twistoptics has recently emerged as a branch of nano-optics that explores light propagation in stacks of thin anisotropic layers rotated relative to one another. The concept is particularly relevant for polaritons—hybrid light-matter quasiparticles—in van der Waals (vdW) materials, where strong in-p…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045423] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies twistoptics in planar heterostructures with rotated layers and conductive sheets, focusing on polariton propagation.
motivation: To understand and control light propagation in stacked anisotropic layers, which is relevant for nano-optics and polaritonics.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework using transfer matrix methods to model electromagnetic fields in heterostructures with arbitrary numbers of rotated layers and 2D conductive sheets.
result: They derive general expressions for reflection, transmission, and absorption, and analyze the effect of twist angles on polariton dispersion and propagation.
conclusion: Twistoptics provides a versatile platform for engineering polariton propagation in van der Waals heterostructures.

title: Functional Renormalization Group For Extremely Correlated Electrons
authors: Jonas Arnold, Peter Kopietz, And Andreas Rückriegel

At strong on-site repulsion [MATH], the fermionic Hubbard model realizes an extremely correlated electron system. In this regime, it is natural to derive the low-energy physics with the help of noncanonical operators acting on a projected Hilbert space without double occupancies. Using a strong-couplin…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 055123] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a functional renormalization group approach for the Hubbard model in the strong-coupling limit using noncanonical operators.
motivation: The Hubbard model at strong on-site repulsion is difficult to treat with conventional methods; a functional renormalization group approach using projected Hilbert space may capture low-energy physics.
method: The authors derive a functional renormalization group for extremely correlated electrons using noncanonical operators and a strong-coupling expansion.
result: They obtain flow equations for the self-energy and vertex functions that incorporate the constraints of no double occupancy.
conclusion: The method provides a systematic way to study strongly correlated electron systems beyond the Gutzwiller approximation.

title: Pressure Tuning Of Electronic Correlations And Flat Bands In ${\mathrm{CsCr}}_{3}{\mathrm{Sb}}_{5}$

tldr: This paper studies the electronic correlations and flat bands in the kagome superconductor CsCr3Sb5 under pressure.
motivation: To understand the interplay between electronic correlations, flat bands, and superconductivity in a strongly correlated kagome system.
method: First-principles calculations and effective model analysis to study the pressure dependence of electronic structure and correlations.
result: Pressure tunes the flat bands and electronic correlations, affecting the superconducting and density wave orders.
conclusion: The study provides insights into the physics of kagome superconductors but does not directly contribute to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Bistability Of Electron Temperature In Atomically Thin Semiconductors In The Presence Of Exciton Photogeneration
authors: A. M. Shentsev
abstract:

We study the dynamic equilibrium between trions and excitons in monolayers of transition metal dichalcogenides in the presence of resident charge carriers and continuous photogeneration of excitons. [Phys. Rev. B 114, 055416] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies bistability of electron temperature in atomically thin semiconductors due to exciton photogeneration and Drude absorption.
motivation: Understanding the dynamic equilibrium between trions and excitons in transition metal dichalcogenides is important for optoelectronic applications.
method: The authors model the system with rate equations and heat balance, considering Drude absorption of low-frequency radiation.
result: They find that heating via Drude absorption leads to bistability of the electron temperature.
conclusion: The bistability effect could be exploited for novel optoelectronic devices.

title: Amplitude Death And Phase-locked Oscillations In Delay-coupled Oscillators With Frequency Mismatch And Nonisochronism
authors: Keiji Konishi, Koki Yoshida, Yoshiki Sugitani, And Naoyuki Hara
abstract:
Author(s): Keiji Konishi, Koki Yoshida, Yoshiki Sugitani, and Naoyuki Hara

This paper presents an investigation of amplitude death and phase-locked oscillations in delay-coupled Stuart-Landau oscillators with frequency mismatch. These oscillators exhibit nonisochronism, in which the rotation velocities depend on amplitudes. We provide a simple procedure to numerically obta…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014221] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies amplitude death and phase-locked oscillations in delay-coupled Stuart-Landau oscillators with frequency mismatch and nonisochronism.
motivation: Understanding collective dynamics in coupled oscillators is important for various fields, but this work focuses on classical nonlinear dynamics without quantum or information-theoretic aspects.
method: The authors provide a numerical procedure to obtain stability boundaries and analyze the effects of frequency mismatch and nonisochronism on amplitude death and phase-locked oscillations.
result: They find that frequency mismatch and nonisochronism significantly affect the regions of amplitude death and phase-locked oscillations.
conclusion: The results contribute to the theory of coupled oscillators but have no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Variational Approach To Yukawa Fluids. I. Thermodynamics
authors: S. A. Khrapak And A. G. Khrapak
abstract:
Author(s): S. A. Khrapak and A. G. Khrapak

The excess energy, entropy, and pressure of a strongly coupled Yukawa fluid are calculated from the variational approach using the fluid of hard spheres as a reference system. As in the case of the one-component plasma, the Percus-Yevick virial entropy is appropriate for such calculations and delive…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015216] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses a variational approach with hard-sphere reference to compute thermodynamic properties of Yukawa fluids.
motivation: To accurately calculate excess energy, entropy, and pressure of strongly coupled Yukawa fluids, which are relevant in plasma physics and colloidal systems.
method: The variational method is applied using the Percus-Yevick virial entropy for the hard-sphere reference system.
result: The approach yields accurate thermodynamic quantities for Yukawa fluids across a range of coupling parameters.
conclusion: The variational method with hard-sphere reference is effective for describing thermodynamics of Yukawa fluids.

title: Exact Stationary State Of A $d$-dimensional Run-and-tumble Particle In A Harmonic Potential
authors: Mathis Guéneau, Satya N. Majumdar, And Grégory Schehr
abstract:
Author(s): Mathis Guéneau, Satya N. Majumdar, and Grégory Schehr

Understanding how active particles, such as swimming bacteria, move in confined environments remains a challenge. The authors obtain the exact stationary distribution of a run-and-tumble particle trapped by a harmonic potential in one, two, and three dimensions, providing quantitative benchmarks for experiments on confined active matter.

#SoftMatterSpotlight #TechnicalAdvancement


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014144] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives the exact stationary distribution of a run-and-tumble particle in a harmonic potential in 1, 2, and 3 dimensions.
motivation: Understanding active particle motion in confined environments is important for biological and soft matter systems, but exact solutions are rare.
method: The authors solve the Fokker-Planck equation for run-and-tumble dynamics in a harmonic trap using separation of variables and Fourier methods.
result: They obtain closed-form expressions for the stationary probability density in one, two, and three dimensions.
conclusion: The exact results provide quantitative benchmarks for experiments on confined active matter and deepen theoretical understanding of active systems.

title: Short-term Plasticity-based Working Memory Spiking Model Is Resilient To Synaptic Heterogeneity
authors: Gianmarco Tiddia, Luca Sergi, Simone Rubiu, Antonio Incollu, And Bruno Golosio
abstract:
Author(s): Gianmarco Tiddia, Luca Sergi, Simone Rubiu, Antonio Incollu, and Bruno Golosio

The presence of activity-silent working memory has been increasingly supported by experimental observation, and short-term synaptic facilitation is suggested to underlie this phenomenon. Originally proposed in the early 2000s, the synaptic theory of working memory was supported by a relatively simpl…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014409] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: A computational neuroscience paper proposing a spiking neural network model for activity-silent working memory based on short-term synaptic plasticity, and testing its robustness to synaptic heterogeneity.
motivation: Experimental evidence supports activity-silent working memory, and short-term facilitation is a candidate mechanism. The original model was simple; this work extends it to more realistic conditions with heterogeneous synapses.
method: The authors develop a spiking neural network model with short-term plasticity (facilitation and depression) and simulate its dynamics under varying degrees of synaptic heterogeneity, analyzing memory retention and recall performance.
result: The model is resilient to moderate levels of synaptic heterogeneity, maintaining working memory function despite variability in synaptic parameters.
conclusion: Short-term plasticity-based working memory models are robust to biological variability, supporting their plausibility as a neural mechanism for activity-silent working memory.

title: Stokes-Einstein-like Scaling Across Fluidized And Caged Transport Regimes In A Driven Complex Plasma
authors: Adrian Scurtu, Dorina Ticoş, Nicoleta Udrea, Maria L. Mitu, Beatrice Paraschiv, And Cătălin M. Ticoş
abstract:
Author(s): Adrian Scurtu, Dorina Ticoş, Nicoleta Udrea, Maria L. Mitu, Beatrice Paraschiv, and Cătălin M. Ticoş

The Stokes-Einstein (SE) relation links microscopic fluctuations to macroscopic dissipation. Whether it survives in driven-dissipative, strongly coupled systems far from global equilibrium remains an open question. Using a macroscopic dust vortex in a radio-frequency complex plasma, we isolate therm…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015215] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the Stokes-Einstein relation in a driven complex plasma, focusing on transport regimes in a classical dissipative system.
motivation: To test whether the Stokes-Einstein relation holds in driven-dissipative, strongly coupled systems far from global equilibrium.
method: Experimental observation of a macroscopic dust vortex in a radio-frequency complex plasma, analyzing microscopic fluctuations and macroscopic dissipation.
result: The Stokes-Einstein-like scaling is observed across fluidized and caged transport regimes.
conclusion: The Stokes-Einstein relation can survive in certain driven-dissipative systems, providing insight into transport in complex plasmas.

title: Self-organized Model For The Flicker Noise In Interacting Two-dimensional Electron Gas
authors: Maryam Pirgholi, Morteza Nattagh Najafi, And Vadood Adami
abstract:
Author(s): Maryam Pirgholi, Morteza Nattagh Najafi, and Vadood Adami

We investigate self-organized criticality in a two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) by introducing a lattice-based model that incorporates electron-electron interactions through the concept of coherence length. Our numerical simulations demonstrate that in the strongly interacting regime, the system …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014141] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies self-organized criticality and flicker noise in a 2D electron gas with electron-electron interactions, using a lattice model and numerical simulations.
motivation: Understanding the origin of 1/f noise in interacting electron systems is a long-standing problem in condensed matter physics.
method: A lattice-based model incorporating coherence length to capture electron-electron interactions is simulated numerically to study self-organized criticality.
result: In the strongly interacting regime, the system exhibits self-organized criticality and produces flicker noise (1/f spectrum).
conclusion: The model provides a possible mechanism for 1/f noise in 2DEG based on self-organized criticality.

title: Spectral Statistics And Localization Properties Of A ${\mathrm{C}}_{3}$-symmetric Billiard
authors: Matic Orel And Marko Robnik
abstract:
Author(s): Matic Orel and Marko Robnik

We revisit the spectral statistics of the [MATH]-symmetric billiard introduced by F. Leyvraz et al. [
tldr: This paper studies spectral statistics and localization properties of a C3-symmetric billiard, showing GOE and GUE statistics depending on symmetry block.
motivation: To understand quantum chaos and spectral properties in systems with discrete symmetry, specifically a C3-symmetric billiard.
method: High-precision numerical computation of eigenvalues and eigenfunctions, analysis of level spacing distributions and localization measures.
result: The system exhibits both GOE and GUE statistics depending on the symmetry block, with certain states showing localization.
conclusion: The C3-symmetric billiard provides a rich example of symmetry-induced spectral statistics and localization phenomena.

title: Stability And Interactions Of Hopfions In Confined Chiral Systems: Role Of The Background Phase
authors: Andrey O. Leonov
abstract:
Author(s): Andrey O. Leonov

We present a systematic study of isolated hopfions in confined layers of chiral magnets and cholesteric liquid crystals with strong surface anchoring and a film thickness fixed to one spiral pitch. We focus on the structure, stability, and interactions of hopfions under these conditions. Using numer…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015416] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies hopfions in confined chiral magnets and cholesteric liquid crystals, focusing on their stability and interactions.
motivation: Hopfions are topological solitons that may have applications in spintronics and liquid crystal displays, but their behavior in confined geometries is not well understood.
method: Numerical simulations are used to model hopfions in thin films with strong surface anchoring, varying the background phase to study stability and interactions.
result: The stability and interaction of hopfions depend sensitively on the background phase, with certain phases enabling stable hopfion configurations.
conclusion: Controlling the background phase is crucial for realizing stable hopfions in confined chiral systems, which may guide experimental efforts.

title: Finite-size Scaling To Resolve Spurious Multifractality In The Two-dimensional Ising Model
authors: S. Jaroszewicz, N. Mendez, Maria P. Beccar-Varela, And Maria Cristina Mariani
abstract:
Author(s): S. Jaroszewicz, N. Mendez, Maria P. Beccar-Varela, and Maria Cristina Mariani

Multifractal detrended fluctuation analysis has emerged as a standard tool for characterizing scale invariance in complex systems, yet its application to discrete spin models is frequently marred by reports of “spurious multifractality” that contradict established theory. In this work, we resolve th…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014139] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper resolves spurious multifractality in the 2D Ising model using finite-size scaling.
motivation: Multifractal detrended fluctuation analysis often yields spurious multifractality in discrete spin models, contradicting established theory.
method: The authors apply finite-size scaling techniques to multifractal detrended fluctuation analysis of the 2D Ising model.
result: They show that the apparent multifractality is an artifact of finite-size effects and can be resolved by proper scaling.
conclusion: Finite-size scaling is essential to avoid misinterpretation of multifractal analysis in spin systems.

title: Dynamics-induced Activity Patterns Of Active-inactive Clusters In Complex Networks
authors: Anil Kumar, V. K. Chandrasekar, And D. V. Senthilkumar
abstract:
Author(s): Anil Kumar, V. K. Chandrasekar, and D. V. Senthilkumar

Synchrony patterns describe network states in which nodes of a coupled dynamical system are grouped into clusters based on synchronization between nodes. Beyond simple synchrony, synchronized clusters may also exhibit active or inactive states, and the collection of all such clusters constitutes an …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014219] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies synchrony patterns in complex networks, focusing on active-inactive cluster dynamics.
motivation: Understanding how synchronized clusters form and transition between active and inactive states in coupled dynamical systems.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of coupled oscillators on complex networks, identifying conditions for cluster synchronization and activity patterns.
result: Identified dynamics-induced activity patterns where clusters can be active or inactive depending on coupling and network topology.
conclusion: The work provides insights into emergent collective behavior in networked systems, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Phenomenological Renormalization Group In Neuronal Models Near Criticality
authors: Kaio F. R. Nascimento, Daniel M. Castro, Gustavo G. Cambrainha, And Mauro Copelli
abstract:
Author(s): Kaio F. R. Nascimento, Daniel M. Castro, Gustavo G. Cambrainha, and Mauro Copelli

The phenomenological renormalization group (PRG) has been applied to the study of scale-invariant phenomena in neuronal data, providing evidence for critical phenomena in the brain. However, it remains unclear how reliably these observed signatures indicate genuine critical behavior, as it is not we…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014310] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper applies phenomenological renormalization group to neuronal models to study criticality, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To test whether scale-invariant signatures in neuronal data reliably indicate genuine critical behavior.
method: The authors use phenomenological renormalization group (PRG) on neuronal models and compare with known critical exponents.
result: The PRG method can produce signatures that mimic criticality even in non-critical models, questioning the reliability of such evidence.
conclusion: Care must be taken when interpreting PRG results as evidence of criticality in neuronal systems.

title: Absence Of O(2) Symmetry In The Vicsek Model
authors: Yushin Takahashi, Kota Mitsui, Tsuyoshi Mizohata, And Hideyuki Miyahara
abstract:
Author(s): Yushin Takahashi, Kota Mitsui, Tsuyoshi Mizohata, and Hideyuki Miyahara

The phase transition in the Vicsek model is widely believed to be associated with spontaneous symmetry breaking of the two-dimensional rotational symmetry [MATH]. In this paper, we revisit the original model introduced by Vicsek et al. [
tldr: This paper demonstrates that the Vicsek model does not exhibit O(2) symmetry breaking, contrary to common belief.
motivation: The Vicsek model is a paradigmatic model for collective motion, and its phase transition is often attributed to spontaneous breaking of O(2) rotational symmetry. The authors aim to test this assumption.
method: The authors revisit the original Vicsek model and analyze its symmetry properties using numerical simulations and theoretical arguments.
result: They find that the model's order parameter is not a vector but a scalar, and the transition is not associated with O(2) symmetry breaking.
conclusion: The widely held belief about O(2) symmetry breaking in the Vicsek model is incorrect; the transition is of a different nature.

title: First-passage Times For The Space-fractional Fokker-Planck Equation
authors: Christopher N. Angstmann, Daniel S. Han, Bruce I. Henry, And Boris Z. Huang
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher N. Angstmann, Daniel S. Han, Bruce I. Henry, and Boris Z. Huang

We extend the random walk framework to include compounded steps, providing first-passage time (FPT) properties for a class of superdiffusive processes which are governed by the space-fractional spectral Fokker-Planck equation. This first-passage process introduces FPT properties, different from Lévy…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014136] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies first-passage times for superdiffusive processes governed by the space-fractional Fokker-Planck equation.
motivation: Understanding first-passage times in anomalous diffusion is important for various physical systems, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors extend the random walk framework to include compounded steps and derive first-passage time properties for space-fractional Fokker-Planck dynamics.
result: They obtain first-passage time distributions that differ from those of Lévy flights, highlighting the role of step correlations.
conclusion: The work contributes to the theory of anomalous diffusion but has no direct relevance to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Optimal Navigation In Two-dimensional Flows: Control Theory And Reinforcement Learning
authors: Vladimir Parfenyev
abstract:
Author(s): Vladimir Parfenyev

Zermelo's navigation problem seeks the trajectory of minimal travel time between two points in a fluid flow. We address this problem for an agent—such as a floating drone or active particle—that is advected by a two-dimensional flow, self-propels at a fixed speed smaller than or comparable to the ch…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015104] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper solves Zermelo's navigation problem for an agent in a two-dimensional flow using control theory and reinforcement learning.
motivation: Finding optimal paths in fluid flows is important for autonomous vehicles and marine robotics, but the problem is challenging when the agent's speed is comparable to the flow speed.
method: The authors formulate the problem as a time-optimal control problem and apply reinforcement learning (specifically, a value iteration algorithm) to compute optimal trajectories in a given flow field.
result: They demonstrate that the reinforcement learning approach successfully finds near-optimal paths and outperforms heuristic strategies in complex flow patterns.
conclusion: Reinforcement learning is an effective tool for solving Zermelo's navigation problem in two-dimensional flows, with potential applications to autonomous navigation in realistic environments.

title: Localization-delocalization Transition In Low-dimensional Asymmetric Resetting Random Walks
authors: Reza Sepehrinia
abstract:
Author(s): Reza Sepehrinia

We investigate biased random walks with stochastic resetting to previously visited sites and demonstrate how directional drift fundamentally alters the emergence of localized stationary states. We show that bias acts as a competing mechanism and can weaken or suppress localization. This competition …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014128] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies biased random walks with stochastic resetting, showing that directional drift can suppress localization.
motivation: To understand how bias affects the emergence of localized stationary states in resetting random walks.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of low-dimensional asymmetric random walks with resetting to previously visited sites.
result: Bias acts as a competing mechanism that can weaken or suppress localization, leading to a localization-delocalization transition.
conclusion: Directional drift fundamentally alters the stationary state properties of resetting random walks.

title: Continuous-time Random Walks With Asymmetric Waiting-time And Jump-length Distributions As A Model Of Biased Anomalous Transport
authors: Guohua Li, Andrey G. Cherstvy, Hong Zhang, Zeyu Tu, And Ralf Metzler
abstract:
Author(s): Guohua Li, Andrey G. Cherstvy, Hong Zhang, Zeyu Tu, and Ralf Metzler

Continuous-time random walks (CTRWs) are highly appreciated as a model of anomalous diffusion (AD) in complex media such as structured and heterogeneous environments. These walks are used to describe AD phenomena characterized by a nonlinear functional dependence of the mean-squared displacement (MS…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014129] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies continuous-time random walks with asymmetric waiting-time and jump-length distributions as a model of biased anomalous transport.
motivation: Anomalous diffusion is common in complex media, and biased transport (e.g., due to external fields) is important in many systems. The paper aims to extend CTRW models to incorporate asymmetry in both waiting times and jump lengths.
method: The authors derive analytical expressions for the mean-squared displacement and other transport characteristics using a generalized CTRW framework with coupled asymmetric distributions.
result: They find that asymmetry in waiting-time and jump-length distributions leads to rich transport behavior, including superdiffusion, subdiffusion, and ballistic regimes depending on the parameters.
conclusion: The model provides a versatile tool for describing biased anomalous transport in heterogeneous environments, but the work is primarily a classical statistical physics study without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Universality Of Order Statistics For Brownian Reshuffling
authors: Zdzislaw Burda, Mario Kieburg, And Tomasz Maciocha
abstract:
Author(s): Zdzislaw Burda, Mario Kieburg, and Tomasz Maciocha

In a one-dimensional gas of particles confined by an asymptotically power-law potential, the ordering of the particles changes as they perform Brownian motion. The authors show that the order statistics that describe how the particles are reshuffled are universal and independent of the potential’s exponent, while the timescale of the reshuffling does depend on it.

#UniversalBehavior #AdvancingField


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014130] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies universal order statistics in a one-dimensional gas of Brownian particles confined by a power-law potential.
motivation: Understanding how particle ordering changes over time in a diffusive system is a fundamental statistical mechanics problem.
method: The authors analyze the order statistics of Brownian particles under an asymptotically power-law confining potential, deriving universal behavior independent of the potential exponent.
result: The order statistics are universal, while the reshuffling timescale depends on the potential exponent.
conclusion: The universality of order statistics holds for a class of confining potentials, providing insight into the dynamics of particle ordering.

title: Dynamic Effects Of Electric Fields In A Hybrid-coupled Thermosensitive Neuronal Network
authors: Ediline L. F. Nguessap, Antonio C. Roque, And Fernando F. Ferreira

Author(s): Ediline L. F. Nguessap, Antonio C. Roque, and Fernando F. Ferreira

The dynamics of thermosensitive FitzHugh-Nagumo neuronal networks under hybrid synaptic coupling and external electric fields is investigated in a ring topology. Numerical simulations show collective behavior ranging from incoherent activity to coherent traveling waves and chimera and multichimera s…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014218] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies collective dynamics in a thermosensitive neuronal network under electric fields, which is unrelated to quantum information or quantum thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding how electric fields affect neuronal network dynamics is important for neuroscience, but the paper does not connect to quantum information theory or thermodynamics.
method: Numerical simulations of FitzHugh-Nagumo neurons with hybrid synaptic coupling and external electric fields in a ring topology.
result: Observed collective behaviors including incoherent activity, coherent traveling waves, and chimera states.
conclusion: The study provides insights into neuronal network dynamics but has no relevance to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Realizable Entropic Lattice Boltzmann Method For high-Péclet Scalar Transport
authors: Jingsen Feng, Yang Liu, And Xu Chu
abstract:

We present a realizable entropic lattice Boltzmann method (RELBM) for scalar transport at high Péclet (Pe) number. The method combines an ADE-tailored entropic relaxation with a nonorthogonality correction to ghost-mode damping and a strictly conservative population-space realizability limiter activ…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L013301] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a numerical method for scalar transport in fluid dynamics, unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: High-Péclet scalar transport is challenging for lattice Boltzmann methods due to instabilities; the authors aim to develop a realizable entropic method.
method: They combine an ADE-tailored entropic relaxation, nonorthogonality correction for ghost-mode damping, and a conservative realizability limiter.
result: The method achieves stability and accuracy for high Péclet numbers, demonstrated on benchmark problems.
conclusion: The proposed RELBM is effective for high-Péclet scalar transport, but the work is purely classical computational fluid dynamics.

title: Distance Function For Stochastic Matrices
authors: Antony R. Lee, Peter Tiňo, And Iain B. Styles
abstract:
Author(s): Antony R. Lee, Peter Tiňo, and Iain B. Styles

The ability to quantify the similarity of stochastic processes is important in a wide range of areas including communications, simulation, and operational research. Such processes are commonly modeled as Markov Chains and so a natural way to compare their similarity is to compute distances between p…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014125] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a distance function for stochastic matrices based on the Kullback-Leibler divergence rate, applied to Markov chains.
motivation: Quantifying similarity between stochastic processes is important in communications, simulation, and operational research, but existing distance measures have limitations.
method: The authors define a distance function using the Kullback-Leibler divergence rate between Markov chains and prove it satisfies metric properties.
result: The proposed distance is shown to be a valid metric and is demonstrated on synthetic and real-world data.
conclusion: The distance function provides a principled way to compare stochastic processes, with potential applications in clustering and classification.

title: Intermediate Scattering Function Of Brownian Particles In A Tilted Cosine Potential
authors: Regina Rusch And Thomas Franosch
abstract:
Author(s): Regina Rusch and Thomas Franosch

We solve the Fokker-Planck equation for a Brownian particle in a tilted cosine potential and derive the intermediate scattering function (ISF), which captures the full spatiotemporal dynamics of the system. The model consists of a single overdamped Brownian particle in one dimension. We derive a gen…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014127] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper solves the Fokker-Planck equation for a Brownian particle in a tilted cosine potential and derives the intermediate scattering function.
motivation: Understanding the spatiotemporal dynamics of Brownian particles in periodic potentials is important for condensed matter physics and soft matter.
method: The authors solve the Fokker-Planck equation analytically and numerically to obtain the intermediate scattering function for an overdamped Brownian particle in a tilted cosine potential.
result: They derive a general expression for the intermediate scattering function that captures the full spatiotemporal dynamics.
conclusion: The work provides a complete characterization of the dynamics of a Brownian particle in a tilted periodic potential, which may be useful for interpreting scattering experiments.

title: Floquet Resonances In The Double Kicked Top
authors: Avadhut V. Purohit And Udaysinh T. Bhosale

We study exact quantum resonances in the double kicked top (DKT), a driven spin model that extends the quantum kicked top (QKT) by introducing an additional time-reversal symmetry-breaking kick. By expressing the dynamics in terms of effective parameters [MATH], we analytically show the…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014214] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies exact quantum resonances in a driven spin model called the double kicked top, extending the quantum kicked top with an additional time-reversal symmetry-breaking kick.
motivation: To understand quantum resonance phenomena in periodically driven systems, which are important for quantum chaos and control.
method: The dynamics are expressed in terms of effective parameters, and analytical conditions for resonances are derived.
result: Exact quantum resonances are identified and characterized for the double kicked top model.
conclusion: The work provides insight into resonance behavior in driven quantum systems, but does not directly connect to the user's specified research directions.

title: Emergence Of Higher-order Interactions In Systems Of Coupled Kuramoto Oscillators With Time Delay
authors: Narumi Fujii, Keisuke Taga, Riccardo Muolo, Bob Rink, And Hiroya Nakao
abstract:
Author(s): Narumi Fujii, Keisuke Taga, Riccardo Muolo, Bob Rink, and Hiroya Nakao

We show that higher-order interactions naturally emerge from time-delayed pairwise coupling in Kuramoto oscillators. [Phys. Rev. E 114, 014215] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that higher-order interactions emerge from time-delayed pairwise coupling in Kuramoto oscillators.
motivation: To understand the origin of higher-order interactions in complex systems, which are often assumed but not derived from first principles.
method: The authors expand the delayed pairwise coupling to second order, deriving a delay-free Kuramoto model with both pairwise and three-body interactions, and perform numerical simulations.
result: Higher-order interactions naturally emerge from time-delayed pairwise coupling, and the derived model captures synchronization dynamics.
conclusion: Time delay in pairwise interactions can effectively generate higher-order couplings, providing a mechanistic explanation for their prevalence in natural systems.

title: Dynamical Origin Of Extreme Events In Mutually Coupled And Networked Brusselator
authors: S. V. Manivelan, S. Sabarathinam, K. Thamilmaran, And I. Manimehan
abstract:
Author(s): S. V. Manivelan, S. Sabarathinam, K. Thamilmaran, and I. Manimehan

This study investigates the dynamical origins and statistical properties of extreme events (EEs) in a diffusively coupled theoretical Brusselator system, extending from pairwise interactions to globally coupled networks. Statistically, the emergence of EEs is characterized by heavy-tailed probabilit…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014217] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies extreme events in coupled Brusselator systems, a topic in nonlinear dynamics and complex systems, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding the dynamical origins of extreme events in chemical oscillator networks is important for predicting rare, large-amplitude fluctuations.
method: The authors analyze a diffusively coupled Brusselator model, from pairwise to globally coupled networks, using statistical and dynamical systems methods.
result: Extreme events are characterized by heavy-tailed probability distributions and are linked to specific bifurcation scenarios.
conclusion: The study provides insights into the emergence of extreme events in coupled nonlinear oscillators, relevant to fields like chemistry and climate science.

title: Nonperturbative Effects Of Short-range Spatial Correlations At The Two-particle Level
authors: Michael Meixner, Matthias Reitner, Thomas Schäfer, And Alessandro Toschi

[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033093] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nonperturbative effects of short-range spatial correlations in two-dimensional systems using cellular dynamical mean-field theory, focusing on the Mott transition.
motivation: To understand how short-range correlations drive the breakdown of self-consistent perturbation theory and the associated Mott transition in two-dimensional systems.
method: The authors employ cellular dynamical mean-field theory (CDMFT) to analyze the effects of short-range correlations at the two-particle level.
result: They identify nonperturbative effects due to short-range correlations and their impact on the CDMFT Mott transition.
conclusion: Short-range spatial correlations play a crucial role in the nonperturbative behavior of correlated electron systems, affecting the Mott transition.

title: Orbital Hall Effect From Orbital Magnetic Moments Of Bloch States: The Role Of A New Correction Term
authors: Tarik P. Cysne, Ivo Souza, And Tatiana G. Rappoport
abstract:

We present a rigorous derivation of the matrix elements of the orbital magnetic moment (OMM) of Bloch states. Our calculations include the Berry connection term in the [MATH]-derivatives of Bloch states, which was omitted in previous works. The resulting formula for the OMM matrix elements applies to a…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033086] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives a correction term for the orbital magnetic moment of Bloch states and applies it to the orbital Hall effect.
motivation: To correct previous derivations of the orbital magnetic moment matrix elements by including a Berry connection term that was omitted, and to study its impact on the orbital Hall effect.
method: Rigorous derivation of the orbital magnetic moment matrix elements including the Berry connection term, followed by first-principles calculations for specific materials.
result: The correction term significantly affects the orbital magnetic moment and the orbital Hall conductivity in certain materials.
conclusion: The inclusion of the Berry connection term is essential for accurate predictions of the orbital Hall effect.

title: Twist-driven Interlayer Hybridization And Multiple Mobility Edges In Bilayer Quasiperiodic Lattices
authors: Ankit Mishra And Kang Hao Cheong
abstract:

We investigate two coupled one-dimensional Aubry-André-Harper rings with [MATH] sites, where a site-dependent angular twist in the second ring generates a spatially varying mosaic of distance-modulated couplings. By varying the quasiperiodic potential strength [MATH] and twist periodicity [MATH], we find mul…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033079] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies mobility edges in bilayer quasiperiodic lattices with twist-induced interlayer hybridization.
motivation: Understanding localization and mobility edges in quasiperiodic systems is a fundamental problem in condensed matter physics.
method: The authors investigate two coupled Aubry-André-Harper rings with a site-dependent angular twist, varying quasiperiodic potential strength and twist periodicity.
result: They find multiple mobility edges and a rich phase diagram due to the interplay of quasiperiodicity and interlayer coupling.
conclusion: The work reveals new phenomena in quasiperiodic systems but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Characterizing Topology At Nonzero Temperature: Topological Invariants And Indicators In The Extended Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Model
authors: Julia D. Hannukainen And Nigel R. Cooper
abstract:
Author(s): Julia D. Hannukainen and Nigel R. Cooper

We compare three complementary diagnostics for mixed Gaussian states at nonzero temperature, focusing on the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chain and its inversion-symmetric extension. While the ensemble geometric phase, a mixed-state generalization of the Zak phase, remains well defined at nonzero temp…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033080] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological invariants for mixed Gaussian states at nonzero temperature in the SSH model, focusing on the ensemble geometric phase and other diagnostics.
motivation: Understanding how topological properties persist at finite temperature is important for realistic systems, but the paper's focus on condensed matter topology does not align with the user's research interests.
method: The authors compare three diagnostics for mixed Gaussian states: ensemble geometric phase, Uhlmann phase, and a many-body invariant, applied to the SSH chain and its inversion-symmetric extension.
result: The ensemble geometric phase remains well-defined at nonzero temperature and captures topological transitions, while the other diagnostics show different behaviors.
conclusion: The ensemble geometric phase is a robust topological indicator for mixed states, but the work is primarily a condensed matter topology study without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Quantum Combinatorial Reasoning For Large Language Models
authors: Carlos Flores-Garrigós, Gaurav Dev, Michael Falkenthal, Alejandro Gomez Cadavid, Anton Simen, Shubham Kumar, Enrique Solano, And Narendra N. Hegade
abstract:
Author(s): Carlos Flores-Garrigós, Gaurav Dev, Michael Falkenthal, Alejandro Gomez Cadavid, Anton Simen, Shubham Kumar, Enrique Solano, and Narendra N. Hegade

We design and implement a quantum combinatorial reasoning framework for large language models (QCR-LLM), integrating a real quantum computer in the hybrid workflow. QCR-LLM reformulates reasoning aggregation as a higher-order unconstrained binary optimization problem. In this sense, reasoning fragme…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033070] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a hybrid quantum-classical framework for combinatorial reasoning in large language models, using a quantum computer to solve optimization problems derived from reasoning aggregation.
motivation: Large language models often struggle with complex reasoning tasks that require combinatorial optimization; the authors aim to enhance reasoning capabilities by leveraging quantum computing.
method: The framework reformulates reasoning aggregation as a higher-order unconstrained binary optimization (HUBO) problem, which is solved on a real quantum computer via variational algorithms, integrated into a hybrid workflow with classical LLMs.
result: The approach demonstrates improved performance on selected reasoning benchmarks compared to classical baselines, showing that quantum optimization can assist LLM reasoning.
conclusion: Quantum combinatorial reasoning can augment LLMs for tasks requiring combinatorial logic, but the current implementation is limited by quantum hardware constraints and problem size.

title: Programmable Transport Of Rotating Particles In Obstacle Arrays
authors: Marcos Puerto, Alfredo Alexander-Katz, Juan L. Aragones, And J. V. Alvarez
abstract:
Author(s): Marcos Puerto, Alfredo Alexander-Katz, Juan L. Aragones, and J. V. Alvarez

Rotating colloids, or spinners, in obstacle arrays exhibit frequency-set stationary orbits and currents set by the competition between an inertial, Magnus-like lift and short-range attraction. Fully resolved lattice-Boltzmann simulations reveal the hydrodynamic coupling and identify the lift mechani…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033071] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the transport of rotating colloids in obstacle arrays using lattice-Boltzmann simulations, focusing on hydrodynamic lift and short-range attraction.
motivation: Understanding the motion of rotating particles in complex environments is important for microfluidics and active matter, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Fully resolved lattice-Boltzmann simulations are used to model rotating colloids in obstacle arrays, capturing hydrodynamic coupling and lift forces.
result: The simulations reveal frequency-set stationary orbits and currents determined by the competition between Magnus-like lift and short-range attraction.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the transport of spinners in structured environments, but has no relevance to quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

authors: Alireza Jozani And Roderich Tumulka

There are several inequivalent proposals in the literature for how to compute the probability distribution of the time that a detector registers for the arrival of a quantum particle. For three of these proposals, based on two kinds of absorbing boundary conditions and imaginary potentials, we compu…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033072] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper compares three proposals for computing detection time distributions in quantum mechanics using absorbing boundary conditions and imaginary potentials.
motivation: There are multiple inequivalent proposals for the probability distribution of detection times, and the authors aim to compare their predictions.
method: The authors compute the detection time distribution for three proposals: two based on absorbing boundary conditions and one based on imaginary potentials.
result: The three proposals yield different predictions for the detection time distribution.
conclusion: The choice of proposal affects the predicted detection time distribution, highlighting the need for experimental discrimination.

Building on prior work that used 2D ion crystals to investigate one-dimensional nanofr…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033044] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies shell formation and nanofriction in 3D ion Coulomb crystals, which is a topic in classical or mesoscopic physics with no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

method: Experimental and theoretical analysis of 3D ion Coulomb crystals in a linear Paul trap, observing shell structures and measuring friction forces.
result: Observation of concentric shell formation and characterization of two-dimensional nanofriction at the interface between shells.
conclusion: Ion Coulomb crystals provide a tunable platform for studying nanofriction, but the work does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

authors: Jean Barbier, Francesco Camilli, Minh-Toan Nguyen, Mauro Pastore, And Rudy Skerk
abstract:

result: They uncover mechanisms governing how feature learning propagates across layers and affects generalization.
conclusion: The work provides theoretical insights into deep learning but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

result: The proposed method significantly improves the accuracy of solving QUBO problems compared to standard Ising machines.
conclusion: Floquet-based modulation is an effective technique to enhance the performance of Ising machines for combinatorial optimization.

title: Candidate For A Fractional Topological Insulator In Twisted ${\mathrm{MoTe}}_{2}$
authors: Yiping Wang, Gillian E. Minarik, Weijie Li, Yves Kwan, Shuai Yuan, Eric Anderson, Chaowei Hu, Julian Ingham, Jeongheon Choe, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Xavier Roy, Jiun-Haw Chu, Raquel Queiroz, James C. Hone, N. Regnault, Xiaodong Xu, And Xiaoyang Zhu

Pump-probe modulation spectroscopy of a MoTe

tldr: This paper reports experimental signatures of a fractional topological insulator in twisted MoTe2 bilayers.
motivation: Fractional topological insulators are a novel phase of matter that could host exotic quasiparticles, but experimental evidence has been lacking.
method: Pump-probe modulation spectroscopy is used to measure the out-of-plane magneto-optical response of a MoTe2 bilayer superlattice.
result: An out-of-plane antiferromagnetic response is observed, consistent with theoretical predictions for a fractional topological insulator.

title: Covariant Path Integrals For Quantum Fields Backreacting On Classical Space-Time
authors: Jonathan Oppenheim And Zachary Weller-Davies
abstract:
Author(s): Jonathan Oppenheim and Zachary Weller-Davies

Researchers have developed a mathematical framework to bridge the gap between Einstein’s classical gravity and quantum mechanics. Their theory allows matter to remain quantum while space-time stays classical, offering a way to test if space and time truly require a quantum explanation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031007] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a covariant path integral framework for quantum fields on a classical spacetime, aiming to reconcile quantum mechanics with classical gravity.
motivation: To bridge the gap between quantum field theory and general relativity by allowing matter to be quantum while spacetime remains classical, providing a testable framework for quantum gravity.
method: The authors construct a covariant path integral formulation that describes the backreaction of quantum fields on a classical spacetime, using a consistent mathematical framework.
result: They derive a formalism that yields well-defined dynamics for the combined system, including a stochastic element that captures the effect of quantum fluctuations on spacetime.
conclusion: The framework offers a potential avenue for testing whether spacetime is fundamentally classical or quantum, and provides a consistent semiclassical gravity theory.

title: Electric-Field Control Of Interlayer Binding And Friction In $h$-BN Contacts
authors: Penghua Ying, Michael Urbakh, And Oded Hod
abstract:

External electric fields can be used to control sliding resistance in layered materials, providing a way to control friction in some systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031003] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies electric-field control of interlayer binding and friction in h-BN contacts, a topic in nanoscale tribology.
motivation: Understanding and controlling friction in layered materials is important for nanomechanical devices.
method: The authors use first-principles calculations and molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the effect of external electric fields on interlayer interactions and sliding resistance.
result: They find that electric fields can significantly modulate interlayer binding and friction, offering a means to control sliding resistance.
conclusion: External electric fields provide a viable route for tuning friction in layered materials like h-BN.

title: Vast World Of Quantum Advantage
authors: Hsin-Yuan Huang, Soonwon Choi, Jarrod R. Mcclean, And John Preskill
abstract:

motivation: To survey and categorize the different types of quantum advantage beyond the standard computational speedup.
method: The authors review known results and conceptual frameworks for quantum advantage in computation, simulation, communication, and sensing.
result: They present a taxonomy of quantum advantage and discuss the conditions under which quantum systems outperform classical ones.
conclusion: Quantum advantage is multifaceted and context-dependent, with many open questions remaining.

title: Rare Cage Escapes Drive Relaxation In Deeply Supercooled Liquids
authors: Francesco Rusciano, Raffaele Pastore, Francesco Greco, And Walter Kob
