motivation: Understanding the microscopic mechanisms of relaxation in supercooled liquids is crucial for glass transition theory.
method: Molecular dynamics simulations are performed at temperatures significantly below the mode coupling temperature to observe rare cage escape events.
result: Rare cage escapes are identified as the primary mechanism for structural relaxation in deeply supercooled liquids.
conclusion: The findings provide new insights into the dynamics of glass-forming systems and the nature of the glass transition.

title: Complexity-Theoretic Foundations Of BosonSampling With A Linear Number Of Modes
authors: Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, And Michał Oszmaniec
abstract:
Author(s): Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, and Michał Oszmaniec

Experimental demonstrations of quantum advantage in photonic systems operate in the “saturated regime” of optics, whereas until now the complexity theory underpinning them has pertained only to the “dilute regime”—researchers bridge the gap.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021059] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes complexity-theoretic foundations for BosonSampling in the saturated regime with a linear number of modes.
motivation: Previous BosonSampling complexity proofs only applied to the dilute regime, but experimental demonstrations operate in the saturated regime; this gap needed to be bridged.
method: The authors prove that approximate sampling from the output distribution of linear-optical networks with a linear number of modes is hard for classical computers under standard complexity assumptions, using techniques from random matrix theory and anticoncentration.
result: They show that BosonSampling with a linear number of modes is classically hard, and provide evidence that the distribution anticoncentrates, which is necessary for hardness.
conclusion: The results validate the complexity-theoretic basis for current photonic quantum advantage experiments operating in the saturated regime.

title: Dynamics Of Quantum Chiral Solitons

method: A nonperturbative quantization approach is applied to chiral solitons in spin chains, analyzing their condensation into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid.
result: Chiral solitons condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid and appear as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase.

authors: Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, And Mohammad Hafezi

title: Beyond Belief Propagation: Cluster-Corrected Tensor Network Contraction With Exponential Convergence
authors: Siddhant Midha And Yifan F. Zhang

[PRX Quantum 7, 020101] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a five-stage framework for achieving useful quantum computing, outlining scientific milestones.
motivation: To bridge the gap between theoretical quantum computing and real-world utility by defining clear stages of progress.
method: The authors propose a structured five-stage framework based on their expertise and analysis of current quantum computing capabilities.
result: A roadmap with five stages detailing the necessary scientific and engineering milestones for practical quantum advantage.
conclusion: The framework provides a high-level vision for the quantum computing community to focus efforts on achieving useful applications.

title: 2d Van Der Waals Magnets: From Fundamental Physics To Applications
authors: Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, And Nuh Gedik
abstract:
Author(s): Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, and Nuh Gedik

Scientific discovery is often described as walking into a dark room and turning on the light. The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials in 2016 was one such leap forward, removing one spatial dimension from macroscopic materials. The study of 2D magnets has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials. The field encompasses not just the traditional study of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets but also topology, quantum and nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons and spintronics, and the interaction of magnetism with light, phonons, and electric fields (multiferroics). The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025003] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A review of 2D van der Waals magnets covering fundamental physics and applications.
motivation: To summarize the current state of knowledge and recent discoveries in 2D magnetism, which has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena.
method: The paper is a review that synthesizes experimental and theoretical results on 2D van der Waals magnets, including topics like topology, quantum dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons, and spintronics.
result: The review highlights the rapid progress in understanding 2D magnetism and its potential for applications.
conclusion: The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.

title: Radiation Forces And Torques In Optics And Acoustics
authors: Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, And Konstantin Y. Bliokh
abstract:
Author(s): Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, and Konstantin Y. Bliokh

This review presents a unified perspective of how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in optical and acoustic wave fields induce forces and torques on particles—a topic that has captivated researchers for centuries. Applications discussed include trapping and manipulation of atoms and nanoparticles by light, sorting of biological cells by the combination of acoustics and microfluidics, and pulling forces that draw particles against the direction of wave propagation.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025002] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: A review of radiation forces and torques in optical and acoustic fields, focusing on particle manipulation.
motivation: To provide a unified perspective on how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in wave fields induce forces and torques on particles.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work on optical and acoustic radiation forces, including trapping, sorting, and pulling effects.
result: Summarizes key principles and applications of radiation forces and torques in optics and acoustics.
conclusion: The field has broad applications in particle manipulation but is not directly related to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review of space-time duality in quantum many-body dynamics, focusing on brickwork quantum circuits.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; space-time duality offers a unified approach.
method: The review explains how discretizing time evolution on a lattice and treating space and time symmetrically leads to solvable models via brickwork quantum circuits.
result: The paper provides a pedagogical overview of exactly solvable quantum many-body dynamics using space-time duality.
conclusion: Space-time duality and brickwork circuits provide a powerful framework for understanding quantum many-body dynamics, with connections to quantum computation.

title: Kagome Metals
authors: Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, And Stephen D. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, and Stephen D. Wilson

The kagome lattice is a two-dimensional tiling of hexagons and triangles named after a Japanese basket weaving technique. Its geometry gives rise to highly frustrated interactions and interference effects experienced by electrons and their multiple degrees of freedom. In metals, the exploration of materials with kagome conduction networks is driven by predictions of realizing new electronic states where these interference effects are dominant, amplifying electronic interactions and many-body effects. In these kagome metals, these amplified correlation effects in combination with spin-orbit coupling and other forms of frustration have given rise to a wealth of phenomena beyond expectations. These include unusual states and responses born from topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, sublattice interference effects at saddle points such as unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism and flux phases, amplified anomalous Hall effects, and electronic nematic states. This review examines the theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, with the aim of elucidating fundamental mechanisms underlying the observed exotic phenomena.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015002] Published Thu Feb 12, 2026.
tldr: A review of kagome metals, focusing on exotic electronic states arising from the frustrated lattice geometry.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms behind unusual phenomena in kagome metals, such as unconventional superconductivity and topological flat bands.
method: The paper reviews theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, synthesizing findings from multiple studies.
result: Kagome metals exhibit a wealth of exotic phenomena including topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, and unconventional superconductivity.
conclusion: The kagome lattice provides a rich platform for studying strongly correlated and topological electronic states.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems in biology, ecology, and epidemiology.
motivation: To unify diverse approaches for modeling complex systems with many interacting agents using field theories.
method: The authors review and apply field-theoretic methods, such as Doi-Peliti formalism and path integrals, to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems.
result: The review demonstrates how field theories provide a powerful framework for analyzing these systems, with applications beyond chemistry.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods are valuable for studying stochastic reaction-diffusion systems across multiple disciplines.

title: Spin-glass Dynamics: Experiment, Theory, And Simulation
authors: E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, And D. Yllanes
abstract:
Author(s): E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, and D. Yllanes

This review updates the field of spin glasses with broad application to a large variety of physical systems. In particular, this review tracks the progress of experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations. It highlights the importance of their synergy, from the inception of the field to the present day, and includes future opportunities for research.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045005] Published Mon Dec 15, 2025.
tldr: A review of spin-glass dynamics covering experiment, theory, and simulation.
motivation: To provide an updated overview of spin-glass research and highlight the synergy between experimental, theoretical, and computational approaches.
method: Review of experimental techniques, theoretical models, and large-scale simulations of spin glasses.
result: Summarizes key advances in understanding spin-glass dynamics and identifies future research opportunities.
conclusion: Spin-glass dynamics remain a rich field with broad applications, and continued interdisciplinary collaboration is essential.

title: Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, And Hae-Young Kee
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, and Hae-Young Kee

Frustration in spin systems can prevent ordering even at =0, creating quantum spin liquids that have been sought since Anderson’s pioneering work in 1973 and his influential 1987 paper connecting them to high-temperature superconductivity. Kitaev’s solvable spin-1/2 models on a honeycomb lattice brought renewed attention to this field, with Jackeli and Khaliullin later revealing how to engineer Kitaev interactions in real materials. This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045003] Published Wed Dec 03, 2025.
tldr: A review of Kitaev quantum spin liquids, focusing on candidate materials and topological properties.
motivation: To provide an overview of theoretical and experimental progress in Kitaev spin liquids, which are a type of quantum spin liquid with potential applications in topological quantum computing.
method: The paper reviews theoretical models (Kitaev honeycomb model) and experimental realizations in materials, highlighting chiral edge modes and other topological features.
result: The review summarizes key candidate materials and their properties, emphasizing the broad topological phenomena observed.
conclusion: Kitaev spin liquids remain an active area of research with promising directions for future study, particularly in material synthesis and characterization.

title: The Ups And Downs Of Internal Conversion
authors: Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, And Salvy P. Russo
abstract:
Author(s): Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, and Salvy P. Russo

This review examines the theoretical methods used to describe the photophysical process of internal conversion in quantum systems. These models explore all facets of the nonradiative mechanism, and the review presents an outlook on how they can be incorporated in studies relevant to applications, for example, in photonics and energy harvesting.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035003] Published Tue Sep 16, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical methods for internal conversion in quantum systems, focusing on nonradiative transitions and their applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
motivation: Internal conversion is a fundamental photophysical process, and understanding its theoretical underpinnings is important for applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
method: The paper reviews various theoretical models for internal conversion, including nonradiative decay mechanisms and their incorporation into studies of quantum systems.
result: The review provides an overview of current theoretical methods and an outlook on their application to photonics and energy harvesting.
conclusion: Theoretical methods for internal conversion are well-developed and can be applied to practical applications, but the paper does not present new results or directly advance quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews quantum properties and functionalities of magnetic skyrmions, focusing on their topological nature and potential applications.
motivation: Magnetic skyrmions are promising for future spintronic devices, and understanding their quantum aspects is crucial for advancing both fundamental physics and applications.
method: The paper surveys theoretical and experimental work on skyrmion formation, quantum features, and interactions, providing a comprehensive overview.
result: It highlights quantum-mechanical effects in skyrmion systems, such as quantum tunneling and entanglement, and discusses their potential for quantum information processing.
conclusion: Magnetic skyrmions exhibit rich quantum behavior that could be harnessed for novel quantum technologies, but the field is still in early stages.

title: Spin-dependent Exotic Interactions
authors: Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, And Dmitry Budker
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, and Dmitry Budker

This review presents a comprehensive summary of theoretical investigations and experimental searches for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model. These interactions may be mediated by various types of exotic bosons, and their existence and properties may, in turn, explain the nature of dark matter and dark energy. The described experiments also probe the discrete fundamental symmetries of nature.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025005] Published Tue Jun 24, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental searches for spin-dependent exotic interactions beyond the standard model, including their possible connection to dark matter and dark energy.
motivation: To understand the nature of dark matter and dark energy and to test fundamental symmetries of nature through spin-dependent interactions mediated by exotic bosons.
method: The paper surveys theoretical models of spin-dependent exotic interactions and reviews experimental techniques used to search for them, such as precision measurements with atomic, molecular, and optical systems.
result: The review summarizes current constraints on various spin-dependent interactions and highlights the potential of ongoing and future experiments to discover new physics.
conclusion: Spin-dependent exotic interactions provide a promising avenue for probing physics beyond the standard model, and further experimental and theoretical work is needed to fully explore their implications.

title: Quantum Physics Of Stars
authors: M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. Deboer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, And A. Tumino
abstract:
Author(s): M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. deBoer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, and A. Tumino

There are many nuclear reactions that are of central importance for stellar burning and element formation. In typical stars, these reactions take place at very low energy, and many of them have very small rates, making it difficult to measure them directly in the laboratory. On the theoretical side, the low-energy regime is governed by quantum-mechanical phenomena like tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects. This review summarizes the state of the art in the theory of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars and describes new ideas for studying these reactions on Earth.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025003] Published Tue May 27, 2025.
tldr: This review summarizes the state of the art in low-energy nuclear reactions in stars, focusing on quantum tunneling, resonances, and interference effects.
motivation: Nuclear reactions at stellar energies are difficult to measure directly due to very small rates, yet they are crucial for understanding stellar burning and nucleosynthesis.
method: The paper reviews theoretical approaches including quantum-mechanical tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects, and discusses new experimental ideas.
result: It provides a comprehensive overview of current theoretical methods and experimental challenges in low-energy nuclear astrophysics.
conclusion: Advances in theory and experiment are needed to better understand stellar nuclear reactions, which are governed by quantum phenomena.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining the violations by examining underlying assumptions.
motivation: To clarify why certain measurements exceed classical thermodynamic bounds and to show how materials can be designed to exploit these violations.
method: The paper surveys a wide variety of examples from different fields where measured properties exceed classical bounds, and analyzes which assumptions of the bounds are violated.
result: It identifies that violations occur because measurements are made in ways that violate assumptions such as equilibrium, linearity, or homogeneity, and demonstrates how designed materials can achieve extreme properties.
conclusion: Understanding the assumptions behind thermodynamic bounds allows for the design of materials with properties that surpass conventional limits, without violating thermodynamics.

title: Colloquium: Synthetic Quantum Matter In Nonstandard Geometries
authors: Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, And Christof Weitenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, and Christof Weitenberg

This Colloquium presents ways to implement fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems. The study of quantum many-body physics in these exotic geometries permits simulation of phenomena from topology in condensed matter to models of gravity and cosmology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 011001] Published Tue Mar 25, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on implementing fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems for quantum many-body physics.
motivation: To explore quantum many-body physics in nonstandard geometries, enabling simulation of phenomena from condensed matter topology to gravity and cosmology.
method: Reviews experimental and theoretical approaches for realizing fractal lattices, curved spaces, and synthetic dimensions in cold atoms, photonics, and electronic systems.
result: Summarizes recent progress in engineering exotic geometries and their potential for simulating topological phases and gravitational analogs.
conclusion: Synthetic quantum matter in nonstandard geometries is a rapidly advancing field with connections to condensed matter and high-energy physics, but it does not directly address the user's specified research directions.

title: Massive Quantum Systems As Interfaces Of Quantum Mechanics And Gravity
authors: Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, And Clara C. Wanjura
abstract:
Author(s): Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, and Clara C. Wanjura

The authors review theories and experimental state-of-the-art efforts to study the effects of gravity on massive quantum systems. Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force and may be addressed via precision quantum probes. Experiments testing whether the quantum nature of gravity causes decoherence and collapse of matter-wave functions and whether it can mediate entanglement between separate massive particles are underway, and their results will guide the theoretical description of gravity effects on a laboratory scale.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015003] Published Thu Feb 13, 2025.
tldr: A review of experimental and theoretical efforts to probe gravity using massive quantum systems, focusing on decoherence and entanglement mediated by gravity.
motivation: Classical gravity is the least precisely tested fundamental force, and quantum probes may reveal its quantum nature.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks (e.g., decoherence models, entanglement tests) and experimental platforms (e.g., matter-wave interferometry, optomechanics) for testing gravity with massive quantum systems.
result: Current experiments are approaching the sensitivity needed to test whether gravity induces decoherence or entanglement, but no definitive results have been obtained yet.
conclusion: Massive quantum systems offer a promising avenue to study the interplay between quantum mechanics and gravity, guiding future theoretical and experimental work.

title: Radiation Reaction Effects On Coherent Emission In Relativistic Magnetized Shocks
authors: Yu Zhang, Yuan-Pei Yang, And Liang-Liang Ji
abstract:
Author(s): Yu Zhang, Yuan-Pei Yang, and Liang-Liang Ji

Relativistic magnetized shocks are natural sources of coherent radiation, representing a promising framework for fast radio bursts (FRBs). This Letter explores how the radiation reaction (RR) effect, triggered by high-energy photon emissions during shock radiation, significantly alters particle dyna…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 045201] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies radiation reaction effects on coherent emission in relativistic magnetized shocks, relevant to astrophysical fast radio bursts.
motivation: Understanding the role of radiation reaction in relativistic shocks is important for explaining coherent radiation observed in FRBs.
method: The authors analyze particle dynamics under radiation reaction and its impact on coherent emission in magnetized shocks.
result: Radiation reaction significantly alters particle trajectories and reduces the efficiency of coherent emission.
conclusion: Radiation reaction must be considered in models of FRB emission from relativistic shocks.

title: Displacive Quantum Critical Point In Superconducting Hydrides: The Case Of ${\mathrm{H}}_{3}\mathrm{S}$
authors: Marco Cherubini, Abhishek Raghav, And Michele Casula
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Cherubini, Abhishek Raghav, and Michele Casula

[MATH] sulfur hydride has been widely investigated for its high superconducting critical temperature [MATH] of 203 K at about [MATH]. Despite being the precursor of superconducting hydrides, a detailed picture of its structural phase diagra…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046102] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates a displacive quantum critical point in superconducting H3S, focusing on its structural phase diagram and implications for high-temperature superconductivity.
motivation: Understanding the structural phase diagram of H3S is crucial for explaining its high superconducting critical temperature and for guiding the search for room-temperature superconductors.
method: The authors use first-principles calculations and anharmonic phonon theory to map the pressure-temperature phase diagram of H3S, identifying a displacive quantum critical point.
result: They find a quantum critical point associated with a structural phase transition that may influence the superconducting properties.
conclusion: The displacive quantum critical point provides a new perspective on the high Tc in H3S and may be relevant for other hydride superconductors.

title: Nmr Evidence For Spontaneous Electronic Chiral Order In URhSn
authors: Y. Tokunaga, T. Ishitobi, H. Sakai, S. Kambe, H. Harima, A. Nakamura, A. Maurya, D. Li, Y. Homma, F. Honda, D. Aoki, And Y. Shimizu
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Tokunaga, T. Ishitobi, H. Sakai, S. Kambe, H. Harima, A. Nakamura, A. Maurya, D. Li, Y. Homma, F. Honda, D. Aoki, and Y. Shimizu

The first direct evidence of spontaneous electronic chiral order in URhSn, a strongly correlated material without an inherently chiral lattice structure, fundamentally challenges the prevailing notion that electronic chirality requires a chiral crystal framework.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046501] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports NMR evidence for spontaneous electronic chiral order in URhSn, a strongly correlated material without a chiral lattice.
motivation: To challenge the prevailing notion that electronic chirality requires a chiral crystal framework by finding direct evidence in a non-chiral lattice.
method: Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) measurements on URhSn single crystals to detect chiral order.
result: First direct evidence of spontaneous electronic chiral order in a material without an inherently chiral lattice structure.
conclusion: Electronic chirality can emerge in non-chiral lattices, fundamentally changing the understanding of chiral order in strongly correlated materials.

title: Chirality Cannot Be Ferroic In Phase Transitions Leading To Enantiomorphic Space-Group Pairs
authors: F. Gómez-Ortiz, S. Mamoudou Taganga, Emma E. Mccabe, A. H. Romero, And E. Bousquet
abstract:
Author(s): F. Gómez-Ortiz, S. Mamoudou Taganga, Emma E. McCabe, A. H. Romero, and E. Bousquet

With growing interest in structural chirality in periodic solids, it has been suggested that chirality might constitute a new ferroic order parameter. In the work described, we demonstrate, by means of a formal group-theoretical proof and a systematic group-subgroup analysis, that achiral-to-chiral …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 036103] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that chirality cannot be a ferroic order parameter in structural phase transitions leading to enantiomorphic space-group pairs.
motivation: There is growing interest in structural chirality in periodic solids, and it has been suggested that chirality might constitute a new ferroic order parameter. The authors aim to clarify this possibility.
method: The authors use formal group-theoretical proof and systematic group-subgroup analysis to examine achiral-to-chiral phase transitions.
result: They demonstrate that chirality cannot be ferroic in such transitions, as it does not satisfy the necessary symmetry conditions for a ferroic order parameter.
conclusion: Chirality should not be classified as a ferroic property in the context of these phase transitions, resolving a conceptual ambiguity in the field.

title: Calculating Resonance Using Parametric Equations Of Motion In The Limit Of The Complex Absorbing Potential Strength Parameter ($η→{0}^{+}$)
authors: Deepak Kumar And Ashish Kumar Gupta
abstract:
Author(s): Deepak Kumar and Ashish Kumar Gupta

Since complex absorbing potentials (CAPs) are nonphysical in nature, they can introduce artificial perturbations into the system, which may lead to shifts in the calculated energy. This study presents a methodology to eliminate artificial reflections caused by the CAP using a backward parametric equ…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012818] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a method to eliminate artificial reflections from complex absorbing potentials in resonance calculations using parametric equations of motion.
motivation: Complex absorbing potentials introduce artificial perturbations that shift calculated resonance energies; the authors aim to correct this.
method: A backward parametric equation of motion is derived in the limit of vanishing CAP strength to remove artificial reflections.
result: The method yields accurate resonance energies without CAP-induced shifts.
conclusion: The proposed technique improves the reliability of CAP-based resonance calculations.

title: Magnetic Field Induced Magnon Portfolio In The Van Der Waals Magnet CrOCl
authors: T. Riccardi, F. Le Mardélé, L. A. Veyrat de Lachenal, A. Pawbake, I. Plutnarova, Z. Sofer, G. Jacquet, F. Petot, A. Saúl, B. Grémaud, A. L. Barra, M. Orlita, J. Coraux, C. Faugeras, And B. A. Piot
abstract:
Author(s): T. Riccardi, F. Le Mardélé, L. A. Veyrat de Lachenal, A. Pawbake, I. Plutnarova, Z. Sofer, G. Jacquet, F. Petot, A. Saúl, B. Grémaud, A. L. Barra, M. Orlita, J. Coraux, C. Faugeras, and B. A. Piot

Magnonic excitations are investigated in the CrOCl van der Waals (vdW) antiferromagnet with absorption experiments in a broad continuous energy range. In an external magnetic field, the dispersions of magnon branches characteristic of different magnetic orders are subsequently observed, revealing a strong biaxial anisotropy, hysteretic magnon spectra, as well as the formation of spatially separated magnetic phases. Theexperiments here show that competing exchange interactions broaden the options to generate different kinds of magnonic excitations within the same vdW material.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024419] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies magnon excitations in the van der Waals antiferromagnet CrOCl under magnetic fields, revealing biaxial anisotropy and hysteretic magnon spectra.
motivation: Understanding magnonic excitations in low-dimensional magnetic materials is important for spintronics and magnonics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Absorption spectroscopy in a broad energy range is used to probe magnon dispersions under varying magnetic fields.
result: Multiple magnon branches corresponding to different magnetic orders are observed, showing strong biaxial anisotropy and hysteresis.
conclusion: Competing exchange interactions in CrOCl enable diverse magnon excitations within the same material, but the work is purely condensed matter physics.

title: Spin-angle-controlled Nonreciprocal Nonlinear Optical Response In Janus ${\mathrm{Cr}}_{2}{\mathrm{I}}_{3}{\mathrm{Br}}_{3}$
authors: Y. Q. Liu, Yong Peng, Junwei Zhang, M. S. Si, G. P. Zhang, And Z. M. Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Q. Liu, Yong Peng, Junwei Zhang, M. S. Si, G. P. Zhang, and Z. M. Zhang

Noncollinear spin configurations can induce nonreciprocal nonlinear optical responses, but their microscopic mechanism remains unclear. Here, we start with an effective tight-binding model to investigate how the spin configuration affects the geometric Pancharatnam-Berry (PB) tensor which is at the …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034312] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spin-angle-controlled nonreciprocal nonlinear optical response in Janus Cr2I3Br3 using an effective tight-binding model.
motivation: The microscopic mechanism of how noncollinear spin configurations induce nonreciprocal nonlinear optical responses remains unclear.
method: The authors start with an effective tight-binding model to investigate how the spin configuration affects the geometric Pancharatnam-Berry tensor.
result: They find that the spin angle controls the nonreciprocal nonlinear optical response.
conclusion: The work provides insight into the microscopic origin of nonreciprocal nonlinear optics in magnetic materials.

title: Domains And Domain Walls In Amorphous Ferrimagnetic Alloys Across The Compensation Temperature
authors: Laura van Schie, Giacomo Sala, Min-Gu Kang, Nicholas Meinhardt, Marta D. Rossell, Christian Degen, And Pietro Gambardella
abstract:
Author(s): Laura van Schie, Giacomo Sala, Min-Gu Kang, Nicholas Meinhardt, Marta D. Rossell, Christian Degen, and Pietro Gambardella

Rare-earth transition-metal alloys are widely investigated as model ferrimagnetic systems for ultrafast magnetization dynamics and domain wall motion. Here, we investigate changes in the local magnetization and domain wall structure of GdFeCo thin films across the magnetic compensation temperature u…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034422] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies domain walls in amorphous ferrimagnetic alloys near the compensation temperature, focusing on magnetization reversal and domain wall structure.
motivation: Understanding domain wall behavior in ferrimagnets is important for spintronic applications, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use magnetic force microscopy and micromagnetic simulations to investigate domain wall width and structure as a function of temperature.
result: They observe changes in domain wall type and width across the compensation temperature, with Bloch walls at low temperature and Néel walls at high temperature.
conclusion: The study provides insights into domain wall physics in ferrimagnets but has no relevance to quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Including Nanoparticle Shape Into Macrospin Models
authors: Iago López-Vázquez, Òscar Iglesias, And David Serantes
abstract:
Author(s): Iago López-Vázquez, Òscar Iglesias, and David Serantes

We investigate the feasibility of the macrospin approximation to account for the actual shape of soft magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs) with realistic geometries. Specifically focusing on magnetite, we use the superellipsoidal parametrization to account for a variety of shapes, with a continuous interpo…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014421] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the macrospin approximation for soft magnetic nanoparticles with realistic shapes using superellipsoidal parametrization.
motivation: To account for the actual shape of magnetic nanoparticles in macrospin models, which is important for understanding their magnetic behavior.
method: The authors use superellipsoidal parametrization to model various nanoparticle shapes and compare macrospin predictions with micromagnetic simulations.
result: The macrospin approximation is found to be valid for certain shape regimes but fails for others, providing guidelines for its applicability.
conclusion: The study offers a systematic way to include shape effects in macrospin models, improving their accuracy for soft magnetic nanoparticles.

title: Tunable Electron-plasmon Coupling In The Layered Transition Metal Dichalcogenide ${\mathrm{ZrSe}}_{2−x}{\mathrm{Te}}_{x}$
authors: Tongrui Li, Yuzhe Wang, Haoyuan Yan, Jiexiong Sun, Rui Xu, Jianghao Yao, Sen Liao, Shiwu Su, Yunbo Wu, Zhanfeng Liu, Yilin Wang, Zhe Sun, Donglai Feng, And Juan Jiang
abstract:
Author(s): Tongrui Li, Yuzhe Wang, Haoyuan Yan, Jiexiong Sun, Rui Xu, Jianghao Yao, Sen Liao, Shiwu Su, Yunbo Wu, Zhanfeng Liu, Yilin Wang, Zhe Sun, Donglai Feng, and Juan Jiang

Electron-plasmon coupling, in which carriers are dressed by collective electronic oscillations, represents an important many-body interaction in solids. Here, using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy, we report the tunable electron-plasmon coupling in the layered transition metal dichalcogeni…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045121] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports tunable electron-plasmon coupling in a layered transition metal dichalcogenide using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy.
motivation: To study electron-plasmon coupling, an important many-body interaction in solids, and demonstrate its tunability in a specific material system.
method: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) was used to measure the electronic structure and plasmonic effects in ZrSe2-xTex alloys.
result: The electron-plasmon coupling strength can be tuned by varying the tellurium concentration in the alloy.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into many-body interactions in layered materials and may have implications for plasmonics and optoelectronics.

title: Large Earthquakes Follow Highly Unequal Ones
authors: Sudip Sarkar And Soumyajyoti Biswas
abstract:
Author(s): Sudip Sarkar and Soumyajyoti Biswas

It was conjectured for a long time that the tectonic plates are in a self-organized state of criticality and that the Gutenberg-Richter law is a manifestation of that. It was recently shown that for a system near criticality, the inequality of their responses due to external driving would sharply ri…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014143] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies inequality of earthquake magnitudes as a signature of criticality in tectonic plates, using a fiber bundle model.
motivation: To test the conjecture that tectonic plates are in a self-organized critical state and that the Gutenberg-Richter law is a manifestation of it.
method: Analyzes inequality measures (e.g., Gini index) of earthquake magnitudes from a fiber bundle model and real earthquake catalogs.
result: Large earthquakes tend to follow periods of high inequality in earthquake magnitudes, suggesting a precursory signal.
conclusion: Inequality of earthquake magnitudes can serve as a potential precursor for large earthquakes, supporting the criticality hypothesis.

title: Multiscale Feedback Drives Viral Evolution And Epidemic Dynamics
authors: Juan C. Muñoz-Sánchez, J. Tomás Lázaro, Josep Sardanyés, And Santiago F. Elena
abstract:
Author(s): Juan C. Muñoz-Sánchez, J. Tomás Lázaro, Josep Sardanyés, and Santiago F. Elena

We introduce a minimal multiscale framework that links within-host virus dynamics to population-level susceptible-infectious-recovered-susceptible (SIRS) epidemiology through explicit, bidirectional coupling. At the microscopic layer, a two-variant quasispecies (master and mutant genomes with packag…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033097] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: A multiscale model coupling within-host viral quasispecies dynamics to population-level SIRS epidemiology.
motivation: To understand how within-host viral evolution and feedback with epidemic dynamics shape viral emergence and disease spread.
method: Develops a minimal mathematical framework with bidirectional coupling between a two-variant quasispecies model and a SIRS compartmental model.
result: The model shows that multiscale feedback can lead to complex epidemic patterns including oscillations and extinction.
conclusion: Multiscale feedback is crucial for realistic modeling of viral evolution and epidemic dynamics.

title: Exactly Solvable Population Model With Square-root Growth Noise And Cell-size Regulation
authors: Farshid Jafarpour
abstract:
Author(s): Farshid Jafarpour

Stochastic exponential growth is nearly ubiquitous across cellular life, but how its microscopic noise structure shapes population growth remains poorly understood. Here, we introduce an exactly solvable population model in which cells grow exponentially with fluctuations that scale with the square …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033082] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an exactly solvable stochastic population model with square-root growth noise and cell-size regulation.
motivation: Understanding how microscopic noise structure affects population growth in cellular systems is poorly understood.
method: The author introduces a stochastic model where cells grow exponentially with fluctuations scaling as the square root of cell size, and solves it exactly.
result: The model yields exact analytical expressions for population dynamics and size distributions.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for stochastic exponential growth with cell-size regulation, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Mie-tronics Supermodes And Symmetry Breaking In Nonlocal Metasurfaces
authors: Thanh Xuan Hoang, Ayan Nussupbekov, Jie Ji, Daniel Leykam, Jaime Gómez Rivas, And Yuri Kivshar
abstract:
Author(s): Thanh Xuan Hoang, Ayan Nussupbekov, Jie Ji, Daniel Leykam, Jaime Gómez Rivas, and Yuri Kivshar

It is usually believed that symmetry breaking in photonic systems leads to weaker confinement, such as in the case of metasurfaces when bound states in the continuum are replaced by quasibound states with lower quality [MATH] factors. Here, in contrast, we reveal that symmetry breaking can instead en…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033076] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies symmetry breaking in nonlocal metasurfaces, showing that it can enhance confinement and Q-factors, contrary to conventional wisdom.
motivation: To challenge the common belief that symmetry breaking in photonic systems leads to weaker confinement and lower Q-factors.
method: The authors analyze Mie-tronics supermodes in nonlocal metasurfaces, using theoretical modeling and numerical simulations to study the effect of symmetry breaking on mode confinement and quality factors.
result: They find that symmetry breaking can actually enhance confinement and increase Q-factors, enabling supermode formation with improved performance.
conclusion: Symmetry breaking in nonlocal metasurfaces can be exploited to achieve stronger confinement and higher Q-factors, offering new design principles for photonic devices.

title: Inhibition Of Explosive Transitions In Spreading Dynamics By Nonlinear Higher-order Adaptation
authors: Longzhao Liu, Hongwei Zheng, Zhihao Han, Xin Wang, And Shaoting Tang
abstract:
Author(s): Longzhao Liu, Hongwei Zheng, Zhihao Han, Xin Wang, and Shaoting Tang

The coevolution of structure and dynamics, known as adaptation, is a fundamental property in various systems and drives diverse emergent behaviors. However, the adaptation in most works primarily stems from pairwise situations, which is insufficient to capture ubiquitous higher-order characteristics…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033068] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies explosive transitions in spreading dynamics on higher-order networks with nonlinear adaptation, which is unrelated to quantum information theory.
motivation: Understanding how higher-order interactions and nonlinear adaptation affect explosive transitions in spreading dynamics.
method: The authors develop a model of spreading dynamics on simplicial complexes with nonlinear adaptation rules and analyze it using mean-field theory and numerical simulations.
result: Nonlinear higher-order adaptation can inhibit explosive transitions, leading to continuous phase transitions instead.
conclusion: Higher-order interactions and nonlinear adaptation play a crucial role in shaping collective dynamics, offering insights for controlling spreading processes.

title: Colloquium: What Do We Mean By ‘active Matter’?
authors: Michael Te Vrugt, Benno Liebchen, And Michael E. Cates
abstract:
Author(s): Michael te Vrugt, Benno Liebchen, and Michael E. Cates

Active matter has become a lively topic in recent years, but what exactly is meant by the term ‘active matter’ is often unclear. This Colloquium discusses the scientific and semantic issues underlying this ambiguity, as well as the history of the field, and offers a definition of active matter as a well-defined subset of nonequilibrium systems. It then surveys recent developments including nonreciprocal interactions, intracellular phase separation, and quantum active matter.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 031001] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium discusses the definition, history, and recent developments of active matter, a subset of nonequilibrium systems.
motivation: The term 'active matter' is often used ambiguously; the paper aims to clarify its meaning and scope.
method: The authors review the history of the field, propose a definition, and survey recent topics including nonreciprocal interactions, intracellular phase separation, and quantum active matter.
result: A clear definition of active matter is provided, and connections to quantum active matter are briefly discussed.
conclusion: Active matter is a well-defined subset of nonequilibrium systems, but the paper does not present new technical results in quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Tip-enhanced Molecular Fluorescence Microscopy With Atomic-scale Resolution
authors: Anna Rosławska, Katharina Kaiser, Sofia Canola, Song Jiang, Fabrice Scheurer, Javier Aizpurua, Tomáš Neuman, And Guillaume Schull
abstract:
Author(s): Anna Rosławska, Katharina Kaiser, Sofia Canola, Song Jiang, Fabrice Scheurer, Javier Aizpurua, Tomáš Neuman, and Guillaume Schull

Scanning probe techniques have transformed our ability to study materials at the atomic scale, providing atom-by-atom views of surfaces. Tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy combines scanning probes with optical fluorescence. Such optical techniques normally have spatial resolution limited by the wavelength of the light used. However, using the scanning tip itself as a nanoscale optical antenna confines the electromagnetic field to the tip apex, achieving superresolution down to the atomic scale. Fluorescence is a fundamental probe of materials that reveals electronic structure and vibronic properties by exciting electrons to higher levels and observing the photons emitted when they relax. These capabilities are of particular interest for studying and identifying molecules, submolecular structures, and their reactions. This review discusses the techniques of tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy and the new insights they have revealed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025007] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This review discusses tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy achieving atomic-scale resolution using scanning probe techniques.
motivation: To overcome the diffraction limit in optical microscopy and achieve atomic-scale spatial resolution for studying molecular electronic and vibronic properties.
method: Combines scanning tunneling microscopy with a nanoscale optical antenna at the tip apex to confine the electromagnetic field and enhance fluorescence.
result: Achieves superresolution down to the atomic scale, enabling the study of individual molecules and submolecular structures.
conclusion: Tip-enhanced fluorescence microscopy provides a powerful tool for nanoscale optical imaging and spectroscopy of molecules.

title: Neutron Stars And The Dense Matter Equation Of State
authors: Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, And Anna L. Watts
abstract:
Author(s): Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, and Anna L. Watts

Neutron stars, the remnants of supernova explosions, are the densest objects in the Universe. A typical neutron star has a mass between one and two solar masses, and a radius of around 12 km. The density at the center of the star is higher than that in atomic nuclei. As a result, the properties of neutron stars provide important information about the behavior of ordinary matter under extreme compression. In recent years, new information about neutron stars has emerged from two sources. The first is the observation of the gravitational-wave signal from the final inspiral of a coalescing binary neutron star. The second is a careful measurement of the x-ray pulse profile of a spinning neutron star. This review discusses these measurements and summarizes how they constrain masses, radii, and central densities. The results are compared to predictions based on calculations of the nuclear equation of state at densities comparable to that in atomic nuclei, which are then extrapolated to higher density. The review ends with an outlook on future observational opportunities.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045007] Published Wed Dec 24, 2025.
tldr: A review of neutron star observations and the dense matter equation of state, focusing on gravitational-wave and X-ray measurements.
motivation: To understand the behavior of matter at extreme densities found in neutron stars, which is not directly related to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Review of observational data from gravitational-wave events and X-ray pulse profiles, compared to nuclear equation of state calculations.
result: Constraints on neutron star masses, radii, and central densities are summarized.
conclusion: Future observations will further constrain the equation of state, but the paper does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Order And Disorder At The Atomic Scale: Microscopy Applied To Semiconductors
authors: Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, And Lorenzo Rigutti
abstract:
Author(s): Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, and Lorenzo Rigutti

Atomic-scale details, especially those of disorder, are important for material properties, especially in semiconductors, but they are also extremely difficult to measure. Real-space methods can give direct access to this information, but typically, that access is limited. This review reports the application of three real-space techniques for measuring disorder to compound semiconductor materials: scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy. Where possible, it emphasizes cases in which the probes have been combined to achieve a more complete picture of the defects.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025006] Published Thu Jun 26, 2025.
tldr: This review covers three real-space microscopy techniques for measuring atomic-scale disorder in semiconductors.
motivation: Atomic-scale disorder critically affects semiconductor properties but is difficult to measure; the review aims to showcase how scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy can be combined to characterize such disorder.
method: The authors review applications of scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy to compound semiconductors, emphasizing cases where multiple techniques are combined.
result: The review demonstrates that combining these real-space techniques provides a more complete picture of atomic-scale defects and disorder in semiconductors.
conclusion: Real-space microscopy techniques are powerful for characterizing atomic-scale disorder, and their combination yields deeper insights into semiconductor materials.

title: Ghost Mechanism: An Analytical Model Of Abrupt Learning In Recurrent Networks
authors: Fatih Dinc, Ege Cirakman, Bariscan Kurtkaya, Mert Yuksekgonul, Yiqi Jiang, Mark J. Schnitzer, And Hidenori Tanaka
abstract:
Author(s): Fatih Dinc, Ege Cirakman, Bariscan Kurtkaya, Mert Yuksekgonul, Yiqi Jiang, Mark J. Schnitzer, and Hidenori Tanaka

This study establishes the ghost mechanism as an underlying mechanism for abrupt learning, whereby the recurrent neural network develops ghost points—transient dynamical bottlenecks—and identifies ways to overcome the training instabilities.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021058] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a ghost mechanism in recurrent neural networks to explain abrupt learning, but it is unrelated to quantum information theory or quantum thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding abrupt learning in recurrent neural networks is important for machine learning, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors develop an analytical model of ghost points as transient dynamical bottlenecks in recurrent networks.
result: They identify ghost points as a mechanism for abrupt learning and propose ways to overcome training instabilities.
conclusion: The ghost mechanism provides insight into learning dynamics in recurrent networks, but the work is purely in machine learning and not relevant to the user's research interests.

title: Flow-Induced Intermittent Transport Shapes Colloid Filtration In Complex Media
authors: Filippo Miele, Ankur Deep Bordoloi, Pietro de Anna, Marco Dentz, Hervé Tabuteau, Verónica L. Morales, Partha Kumar Das, And Sascha Hilgenfeldt
abstract:
Author(s): Filippo Miele, Ankur Deep Bordoloi, Pietro de Anna, Marco Dentz, Hervé Tabuteau, Verónica L. Morales, Partha Kumar Das, and Sascha Hilgenfeldt

Colloidal transport and filtration in porous media are commonly described by single-collector models that assume an underlying homogeneous structure. We use microfluidic experiments, particle tracking, and simulations to observe pore-scale and macroscopic filtration. We show that colloidal trajector…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 044002] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies colloidal transport and filtration in porous media using microfluidic experiments and simulations, focusing on flow-induced intermittent transport.
motivation: Understanding colloidal filtration in porous media is important for applications like water treatment and oil recovery, but existing models assume homogeneous structures that fail to capture observed behavior.
method: The authors combine microfluidic experiments, particle tracking, and numerical simulations to analyze pore-scale and macroscopic filtration dynamics.
result: They show that colloidal trajectories exhibit intermittent transport due to flow heterogeneity, leading to non-exponential filtration profiles.
conclusion: The findings challenge traditional single-collector models and highlight the need to account for flow-induced intermittency in filtration predictions.

title: Interaction Of Strong Electromagnetic Waves With Unmagnetized Pair Plasmas
authors: Navin Sridhar, Emanuele Sobacchi, Lorenzo Sironi, Masanori Iwamoto, Daniel Grošelj, And Brandon K. Russell
abstract:
Author(s): Navin Sridhar, Emanuele Sobacchi, Lorenzo Sironi, Masanori Iwamoto, Daniel Grošelj, and Brandon K. Russell

We investigate analytically and numerically the interaction of strong electromagnetic waves with unmagnetized pair plasmas. We show that the interaction is governed by a single nonlinearity parameter, [MATH], defined as the ratio of the wave strength parameter to the wave frequency in un…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 045102] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the interaction of strong electromagnetic waves with unmagnetized pair plasmas, focusing on nonlinear plasma physics.
motivation: Understanding the nonlinear interaction of strong electromagnetic waves with pair plasmas is important for astrophysical and laboratory plasma physics.
method: The authors use analytical theory and numerical simulations to characterize the interaction, identifying a single nonlinearity parameter that governs the dynamics.
result: They show that the interaction is governed by a single parameter and provide analytical and numerical results for the plasma response.
conclusion: The work contributes to the theory of nonlinear wave-plasma interactions but has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Fitness-Driven Scaling Laws Between mRNA And Protein Levels
authors: Yichen Yan (颜逸辰) And Jie Lin
abstract:
Author(s): Yichen Yan (颜逸辰) and Jie Lin (林杰)

The relationship between protein and messenger RNA (mRNA) levels is a key aspect of gene expression. Although a strong mRNA-protein correlation is widely observed, the evolutionary force driving the correlation remains poorly understood, undermining the reliability of using mRNA abundance as a proxy…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 048402] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the evolutionary forces driving the correlation between mRNA and protein levels in gene expression.
motivation: Understanding why mRNA-protein correlation is observed across species is important for using mRNA as a proxy for protein abundance, but the evolutionary basis is poorly understood.
method: The authors develop a fitness-driven model that incorporates selection on protein levels and noise in gene expression to derive scaling laws between mRNA and protein levels.
result: The model predicts a power-law scaling between mRNA and protein levels, with exponents determined by the fitness landscape and noise parameters.
conclusion: The scaling laws provide a theoretical framework for interpreting mRNA-protein correlations and highlight the role of natural selection in shaping gene expression patterns.

title: Essay: Pushing The Frontiers Of High Energy Density Science Toward Unexplored States Of Matter
authors: Federica Coppari
abstract:
Author(s): Federica Coppari

In this forward-looking PRL Essay, Federica Coppari presents a compelling perspective on high-energy-density science, centering on the remarkable behavior of matter under extreme conditions—such as very high pressures and a wide range of temperatures—like those found deep inside planets, stars, and fusion reactions.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 040001] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This essay discusses high-energy-density science, focusing on matter under extreme pressures and temperatures relevant to planetary interiors and fusion.
motivation: To explore the frontiers of high-energy-density physics and understand material behavior under extreme conditions.
method: Perspective article summarizing current knowledge and future directions in high-energy-density science.
result: Highlights the need for advanced experimental and theoretical tools to study states of matter in planets, stars, and fusion.
conclusion: The field is poised for breakthroughs with new facilities and computational methods, but the paper does not present new results.

title: Integrated Soliton Microcombs Beyond The Turnkey Limit
authors: Ze Wang, Tianyu Xu, Yuanlei Wang, Kaixuan Zhu, Xinrui Luo, Haoyang Luo, Junqi Wang, Bo Ni, Yiwen Yang, Qihuang Gong, Yun-Feng Xiao, Bei-Bei Li, And Qi-Fan Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Ze Wang, Tianyu Xu, Yuanlei Wang, Kaixuan Zhu, Xinrui Luo, Haoyang Luo, Junqi Wang, Bo Ni, Yiwen Yang, Qihuang Gong, Yun-Feng Xiao, Bei-Bei Li, and Qi-Fan Yang

Self-injection locking enables integrated soliton microcombs with turnkey initiation and improved coherence, but it also pins the pump close to resonance, limiting the access to large detuning for broader combs. Here, we use an auxiliary resonator to dynamically hybridize the pump mode, enabling adi…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 043802] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates an integrated soliton microcomb platform that uses an auxiliary resonator to achieve broader frequency combs beyond the turnkey limit.
motivation: Integrated soliton microcombs are important for applications like spectroscopy and telecommunications, but conventional self-injection locking limits the achievable comb bandwidth. The authors aim to overcome this limitation.
method: The authors introduce an auxiliary resonator to dynamically hybridize the pump mode, enabling adiabatic pumping of the soliton to larger detunings and thus broader combs.
result: They achieve soliton microcombs with significantly broader bandwidth than the turnkey limit, demonstrating improved performance.
conclusion: This work advances integrated photonic frequency comb technology, but it is primarily an experimental photonics result with no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems as defined in the research interests.

title: Anomalous Reflection Phase Of Slot Plasmons In An $\mathrm{AlGaN}/\mathrm{GaN}$ Plasmonic Crystal
authors: A. R. Khisameeva, D. A. Khudaiberdiev, I. M. Moiseenko, P. A. Gusikhin, A. S. Astrakhantseva, A. Shuvaev, A. Pimenov, D. A. Svintsov, I. V. Kukushkin, And V. M. Muravev
abstract:
Author(s): A. R. Khisameeva, D. A. Khudaiberdiev, I. M. Moiseenko, P. A. Gusikhin, A. S. Astrakhantseva, A. Shuvaev, A. Pimenov, D. A. Svintsov, I. V. Kukushkin, and V. M. Muravev

We experimentally investigate the terahertz spectrum of plasma excitations in a plasmonic crystal based on AlGaN/GaN two-dimensional electron system (2DES). While screened plasmon modes with linear dispersion are readily observed in such structures, unscreened modes localized in the slots between th…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046901] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally studies terahertz plasma excitations in an AlGaN/GaN plasmonic crystal, focusing on anomalous reflection phase of slot plasmons.
motivation: To understand the behavior of unscreened plasmon modes localized in slots of a plasmonic crystal, which may have implications for terahertz devices.
method: Terahertz spectroscopy measurements on a plasmonic crystal based on a two-dimensional electron system, analyzing reflection phase and dispersion of slot plasmons.
result: Observation of anomalous reflection phase of slot plasmons, indicating strong confinement and unusual dispersion.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into slot plasmon properties in GaN-based structures, relevant for terahertz plasmonics.

title: Hidden Chiral Ferroelectricity In ${\mathrm{AgNbO}}_{3}$ Perovskite
authors: Ying Song, Lingzhi Cao, Jinming Zhai, Zhilong Yang, Yali Yang, Laurent Bellaiche, And Jiangang He
abstract:
Author(s): Ying Song, Lingzhi Cao, Jinming Zhai, Zhilong Yang, Yali Yang, Laurent Bellaiche, and Jiangang He

[MATH] is a lead-free perovskite with considerable potential for energy storage and optoelectronic applications, yet its low-temperature crystal structure has remained controversial. In this Letter, we revisit its low-energy structural landscape using a systematic first-principles st…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 036102] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the low-temperature crystal structure of AgNbO3 perovskite using first-principles calculations, revealing hidden chiral ferroelectricity.
motivation: The low-temperature crystal structure of AgNbO3 has been controversial, and understanding it is important for its energy storage and optoelectronic applications.
method: Systematic first-principles calculations were performed to explore the low-energy structural landscape of AgNbO3.
result: The study uncovers a hidden chiral ferroelectric phase in AgNbO3 at low temperatures.
conclusion: The findings resolve the structural controversy and highlight the potential of AgNbO3 for ferroelectric and chiral applications.

title: Hyperfine-structure Constants Of The $^{45}\mathrm{Sc}$ Ii Ion And The Nuclear Quadrupole Moment
authors: Yong-Bo Tang, Yu-Shan Zhang, And Kai Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Yong-Bo Tang, Yu-Shan Zhang, and Kai Wang

In this work, we calculate the hyperfine-structure constants of the [MATH] ion using a relativistic hybrid approach that combines configuration-interaction and coupled-cluster singles and doubles methods. Magnetic-dipole and electric-quadrupole hyperfine-structure constants are deter…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012816] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper calculates hyperfine-structure constants and nuclear quadrupole moment of Sc II using relativistic hybrid methods.
motivation: Accurate hyperfine constants are needed for atomic spectroscopy and nuclear structure studies.
method: A relativistic hybrid approach combining configuration-interaction and coupled-cluster singles and doubles methods is used.
result: Magnetic-dipole and electric-quadrupole hyperfine-structure constants are determined, and the nuclear quadrupole moment is extracted.
conclusion: The calculated values provide precise atomic data for Sc II, useful for astrophysical and nuclear physics applications.

title: Two-body Fragmentation Dynamics Of Propylene Oxide Dications Induced By $112.5\text{−}\mathrm{keV}/\mathrm{u}\phantom{\rule{0.16em}{0ex}}{\mathrm{C}}^{5+}$ Impact
authors: Tuo Liu, Yue Gao, Shaofei Gu, Bo Yang, Hang Yuan, Mei Wang, Shaofeng Zhang, Xinwen Ma, Xiangjun Chen, Shenyue Xu, And Enliang Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Tuo Liu, Yue Gao, Shaofei Gu, Bo Yang, Hang Yuan, Mei Wang, Shaofeng Zhang, Xinwen Ma, Xiangjun Chen, Shenyue Xu, and Enliang Wang

We report a combined experimental and theoretical investigation of the two-body fragmentation dynamics of propylene oxide dication [MATH] induced by highly charged ion [MATH] impact at energy of $112.5{0ex}}\mathrm{k…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012815] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the fragmentation dynamics of propylene oxide dications induced by highly charged ion impact, a topic in atomic and molecular physics.
motivation: Understanding the fragmentation dynamics of molecular dications under ion impact is important for fundamental physics and applications in radiation damage.
method: The authors combine experimental measurements using a reaction microscope with theoretical calculations to analyze two-body fragmentation channels.
result: They identify and characterize the dominant fragmentation pathways and their kinetic energy release distributions.
conclusion: The study provides detailed insights into the fragmentation mechanisms of propylene oxide dications, but has no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Anomalous Carrier Dynamics In A Van Der Waals Heterostructure With A Janus Layer
authors: Yifan Wu, Yuee Xie, Han Wang, And Yuanping Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Yifan Wu, Yuee Xie, Han Wang, and Yuanping Chen

A two-dimensional (2D) Janus layer has different physical properties than a 2D non-Janus layer. When a van der Waals (vdW) heterostructure contains a Janus layer, some unusual phenomena different from those in a heterostructure made of two non-Janus layers are expected. Here, we study electronic str…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065422] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies anomalous carrier dynamics in a van der Waals heterostructure containing a Janus layer.
motivation: To explore unusual electronic phenomena arising from the Janus layer in vdW heterostructures.
method: First-principles calculations and theoretical analysis of electronic structure and carrier dynamics.
result: Anomalous carrier behavior is predicted due to the asymmetric Janus layer.
conclusion: Janus layers can induce novel electronic properties in vdW heterostructures.

authors: S. A. Khrapak And A. G. Khrapak
abstract:

The variational approach based on the Bogoliubov inequality using the fluid of hard spheres as a reference system is implemented to evaluate instantaneous shear, bulk, and longitudinal elastic moduli, as well as related sound velocities of Yukawa fluids. The remarkable accuracy of this method is doc…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015217] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses a variational approach to compute elastic moduli and sound velocities in Yukawa fluids.
motivation: Understanding elastic properties of Yukawa fluids is important for modeling complex plasmas and colloidal systems.
method: The authors apply the Bogoliubov inequality with a hard-sphere reference system to derive analytical expressions for shear, bulk, and longitudinal moduli.
result: The variational method yields accurate predictions for elastic moduli and sound velocities, validated against numerical simulations.
conclusion: The approach provides a simple and accurate way to estimate elastic properties of Yukawa fluids without extensive simulations.

title: Transient Striations During Gas Breakdown Under Radio-frequency Excitation
authors: De-Hua Shi, Xiao-Kun Wang, De-Qi Wen, And Yong-Xin Liu
abstract:
Author(s): De-Hua Shi, Xiao-Kun Wang, De-Qi Wen, and Yong-Xin Liu

While investigating radio-frequency gas breakdown, the authors experimentally observed and simulated a novel, time-dependent striated optical emission structure. The study reveals that these striking patterns are driven by differing electron-ion mobilities and locally amplified ionization, which are ultimately suppressed as the electric field becomes screened.

#AdvancingField

tldr: This paper studies transient striations during radio-frequency gas breakdown, a plasma physics phenomenon.
motivation: To understand the formation and suppression of time-dependent striated optical emission structures in RF gas breakdown.
method: Experimental observation and simulation of RF gas breakdown, analyzing electron-ion mobilities and ionization amplification.
result: Striations are driven by differing electron-ion mobilities and locally amplified ionization, and are suppressed by electric field screening.
conclusion: The study reveals a novel transient structure in gas breakdown, but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Generating Consensus And Dissent On Massive Discussion Platforms With A Semantic-vector Model
authors: Alfredo Ferrer, David Muñoz-Jordán, Alejandro Rivero, Alfonso Tarancón, Carlos Tarancón, And David Yllanes
abstract:
Author(s): Alfredo Ferrer, David Muñoz-Jordán, Alejandro Rivero, Alfonso Tarancón, Carlos Tarancón, and David Yllanes

Reaching consensus on massive discussion networks is critical for reducing noise and achieving optimal collective outcomes. However, the natural tendency of humans to preserve their initial ideas constrains the emergence of global solutions. To address this, collective intelligence (CI) platforms fa…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014311] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: A semantic-vector model for generating consensus and dissent on massive discussion platforms.
motivation: To reduce noise and achieve optimal collective outcomes on massive discussion networks despite humans' tendency to preserve initial ideas.
method: Proposes a semantic-vector model that represents opinions as vectors and uses collective intelligence algorithms to facilitate consensus or dissent.
result: The model is demonstrated on a massive discussion platform, showing improved collective outcomes.
conclusion: Semantic-vector models can effectively manage consensus and dissent in large-scale discussions.

title: Computer Simulations Of The Stark Effect In The Helium-$β$ Complex Of Krypton In Inertial Confinement Fusion Conditions
authors: G. Pérez-Callejo, E. Stambulchik, R. Florido, And M. A. Gigosos
abstract:
Author(s): G. Pérez-Callejo, E. Stambulchik, R. Florido, and M. A. Gigosos

There is an ongoing interest in using spectroscopy in inertial confinement fusion (ICF) experiments, where dopants such as krypton can provide vital information about the temperature and density of the imploding plasma. While the most advanced tools for calculating Stark profiles are computer simula…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015212] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses computer simulations to study the Stark effect in krypton under inertial confinement fusion conditions.
motivation: To improve spectroscopic diagnostics of ICF plasmas by accurately modeling Stark-broadened line profiles.
method: Computer simulations of Stark profiles for the helium-β complex of krypton, accounting for plasma conditions.
result: Simulated profiles that can be used to infer plasma temperature and density from experimental spectra.
conclusion: The simulations provide a tool for diagnosing ICF plasmas via krypton dopant spectroscopy.

title: Quantum Diffusion Of Molecular Hydrogen In Liquid $\mathrm{Ne}+{\mathrm{H}}_{2}$ Mixtures: A Quasielastic Neutron Scattering Study
authors: Daniele Colognesi, Ubaldo Bafile, Milva Celli, Leonardo Del Rosso, Franz Demmel, And Martin Neumann
abstract:
Author(s): Daniele Colognesi, Ubaldo Bafile, Milva Celli, Leonardo del Rosso, Franz Demmel, and Martin Neumann

This study presents an analysis of the diffusional dynamics of [MATH] impurities in liquid Ne using quasielastic neutron scattering (QENS) and quantum dynamical simulations. By applying a Lorentzian fitting procedure, we identify two key spectral features: peak width ([MATH]) and i…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015413] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the diffusion of molecular hydrogen in liquid neon using neutron scattering and simulations, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding the diffusional dynamics of hydrogen impurities in liquid neon is important for fundamental physics and potential applications, but it does not relate to the user's research interests.
method: Quasielastic neutron scattering (QENS) experiments and quantum dynamical simulations were performed, and a Lorentzian fitting procedure was used to extract spectral features.
result: Two key spectral features (peak width and intensity) were identified, characterizing the diffusion process.
conclusion: The study provides insights into hydrogen diffusion in liquid neon, but it is not relevant to quantum information theory, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Ring Solitons And Lump Waves Of The Elliptic Cylindrical Kadomtsev-Petviashvili Equation In Physical Coordinates
authors: Tianwei Qiu, Zhen Wang, And Xiangyu Yang
abstract:
