The elliptic cylindrical Kadomtsev-Petviashvili (ecKP) equation is derived from the incompressible Euler equations governing surface gravity waves with nearly elliptic fronts. Using Hirota's bilinear method, this paper systematically investigates ring solitons, lump chains, and lump waves of the ecK…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014216] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies ring solitons and lump waves of the elliptic cylindrical Kadomtsev-Petviashvili equation, which is a model for surface gravity waves with nearly elliptic fronts.
motivation: To understand nonlinear wave phenomena in fluid dynamics, specifically ring solitons and lump waves in elliptic cylindrical coordinates.
method: Uses Hirota's bilinear method to derive analytic solutions for the ecKP equation.
result: Obtains ring solitons, lump chains, and lump wave solutions in physical coordinates.
conclusion: The ecKP equation admits rich soliton and lump wave structures that may be relevant to water wave experiments.

authors: Ilya Degtev, Daniel Jezierski, Adrián Gómez Pueyo, Luciana Di Gaspare, Monica de Seta, Paolo Barone, Giacomo Ghiringhelli, Pieter Glatzel, Zoran Mazej, Wojciech Grochala, Marco Moretti Sala, And José Lorenzana

[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033094] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses resonant inelastic x-ray scattering to study covalency in silver fluorides and cuprates, focusing on electronic structure rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand the electronic structure and covalency in silver fluorides compared to cuprates, which are relevant to high-temperature superconductivity.
method: X-ray absorption spectroscopy and resonant inelastic x-ray scattering at the Ag L3 edge, combined with density functional theory calculations.
result: The study reveals differences in covalency between silver fluorides and cuprates, providing insights into their electronic properties.
conclusion: The findings contribute to the understanding of electronic structure in these materials but have no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Efficient Associative Ionization Of Ultracold Lithium And The Long-lived ${\mathrm{Li}}_{2}^{+}$
authors: N. Joshi, Vaibhav Mahendrakar, M. Niranjan, Raghuveer Singh Yadav, E. Krishnakumar, A. Pandey, R. Vexiau, O. Dulieu, And S. A. Rangwala
abstract:

An 813 nm excitation of ultracold lithium atoms drives associative ionization with a giant collisional cross section, efficiently producing Li
[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032008] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies associative ionization of ultracold lithium atoms to form long-lived Li2+ molecular ions.
motivation: To understand and control the formation of molecular ions in ultracold atomic gases, which is relevant to cold chemistry and plasma physics.
method: Ultracold lithium atoms are excited with 813 nm light to drive associative ionization; the stability of the resulting molecular ions is investigated.
result: A giant collisional cross section for associative ionization is observed, and a subset of deeply bound Li2+ ions are found to be resistant to dissociation.
conclusion: Efficient production of long-lived molecular ions is demonstrated, with potential applications in cold ion chemistry and precision measurements.

title: Electronic Structure Of Compressively Strained Bilayer Nickelate Thin Film

tldr: This paper studies the electronic structure of compressively strained bilayer nickelate thin films using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy.
motivation: To understand the role of out-of-plane nickel orbital bands in superconductivity of bilayer nickelates.
method: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) measurements on thin films under compressive strain and doping.
result: The out-of-plane nickel orbital band shifts with strain and doping but is not required at the Fermi level for superconductivity.
conclusion: The electronic structure of bilayer nickelates is sensitive to strain and doping, but the out-of-plane band is not essential for superconductivity.

title: Are Neural Networks Collision Resistant?
authors: Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, And Riccardo Zecchina
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, and Riccardo Zecchina

A study of the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network shows that efficient algorithms fail to find collisions, a result of direct relevance for the definition of new cryptographic protocols based on machine-learning models.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021051] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network, showing that efficient algorithms fail to find collisions.
motivation: To explore whether neural networks can serve as collision-resistant hash functions for cryptographic protocols.
method: The authors analyze the computational complexity of collision finding in a one-layer neural network using theoretical and algorithmic approaches.
result: Efficient algorithms are shown to fail in finding collisions, suggesting that such neural networks may be collision resistant.
conclusion: The findings are relevant for defining new cryptographic protocols based on machine-learning models.

title: Elastic And Structural Anisotropy In Silica Thin Films For Gravitational-Wave Detectors
authors: Brenda Bracco, Michele Magnozzi, Stefano Colace, Maurizio Canepa, Giulio Favaro, Marco Bazzan, Massimo Granata, David Hofman, Alessandro Di Michele, Laura Silenzi, Gianpietro Cagnoli, Giovanni Carlotti, Paola Sassi, And Silvia Corezzi
abstract:
Author(s): Brenda Bracco, Michele Magnozzi, Stefano Colace, Maurizio Canepa, Giulio Favaro, Marco Bazzan, Massimo Granata, David Hofman, Alessandro Di Michele, Laura Silenzi, Gianpietro Cagnoli, Giovanni Carlotti, Paola Sassi, and Silvia Corezzi

Researchers find that silica films in mirror coatings of gravitational-wave detectors have hidden anisotropy that resists standard heat treatment. This discovery informs coating design and deposition and postprocessing strategies aimed at reducing thermal noise.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021036] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies elastic and structural anisotropy in silica thin films used in gravitational-wave detector mirror coatings, focusing on thermal noise reduction.
motivation: Thermal noise in mirror coatings limits the sensitivity of gravitational-wave detectors; understanding and mitigating anisotropy in silica films could improve performance.
method: The authors characterize the elastic and structural properties of silica thin films using experimental techniques to detect hidden anisotropy and evaluate the effectiveness of standard heat treatments.
result: Silica films exhibit hidden anisotropy that resists standard heat treatment, informing coating design and postprocessing strategies.
conclusion: The findings guide the development of coatings with reduced thermal noise for gravitational-wave detectors.

title: Pressure Effects On Metals, Alloys, And Compounds Of Transplutonium Elements
authors: Tyler W. Hines, Nicholas B. Beck, Kacy N. Mendoza, Joseph M. Sperling, And Thomas E. Albrecht
abstract:

Materials containing transplutonium elements (the actinides Am–Cm that come after Pu in the periodic table) are important for nuclear power, nuclear waste management, and long-term storage. They also have fascinating properties, with 5
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015004] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the physics and chemistry of transplutonium compounds under high pressure, focusing on their electronic structure and material properties.
motivation: Transplutonium elements are important for nuclear power and waste management, and their 5f electrons exhibit unique localized/itinerant behavior under pressure.
method: The paper is a review summarizing experimental and theoretical studies of transplutonium metals, alloys, and coordination complexes under high pressure.
result: It highlights the challenges and advances in understanding the behavior of these radioactive materials, including pressure-induced changes in electronic structure.
conclusion: The reviewed work expands our understanding of transplutonium materials but does not directly contribute to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Nobel Lecture: Physics Is A Point Of View
authors: John J. Hopfield
abstract:
Author(s): John J. Hopfield

The 2024 Nobel Prize for Physics was shared by John Hopfield and Geoffrey Hinton. This paper is the text of the address given in conjunction with the award.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 030501] Published Mon Aug 25, 2025.
tldr: Nobel lecture by John Hopfield reflecting on his scientific journey and the role of physics in understanding complex systems.
motivation: To share personal insights and perspectives on physics as a viewpoint for understanding the world, particularly in the context of neural networks and associative memory.
method: Narrative and reflective lecture, not a technical research paper.
result: No new technical results; the lecture provides historical context and philosophical reflections.
conclusion: Physics offers a unique and powerful perspective for tackling complex problems, exemplified by the development of neural network models.

title: Nobel Lecture: Boltzmann Machines
authors: Geoffrey Hinton
abstract:
Author(s): Geoffrey Hinton

The 2024 Nobel Prize for Physics was shared by John Hopfield and Geoffrey Hinton. This paper is the text of the address given in conjunction with the award.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 030502] Published Mon Aug 25, 2025.
tldr: This Nobel lecture describes Boltzmann machines, a class of stochastic neural networks, but does not address quantum information theory or thermodynamics.
motivation: The paper presents the historical development and key ideas behind Boltzmann machines as a contribution to machine learning and artificial intelligence.
method: The lecture explains the architecture, training algorithm (contrastive divergence), and relationship to statistical physics.
result: Boltzmann machines were influential in the development of deep learning, but the lecture does not present new results.
conclusion: The work is foundational for machine learning but falls outside the specified research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Codata Recommended Values Of The Fundamental Physical Constants: 2022
authors: Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, And Eite Tiesinga
abstract:
Author(s): Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, and Eite Tiesinga

This review contains the 2022 self-consistent set of values of the constants and conversion factors of physics and chemistry recommended by the Committee on Data for Science and Technology (CODATA). The CODATA values are based on a least-squares adjustment that takes into account all data available up to the end of 2022. Details of the data selection and methodology are described.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025002] Published Wed Apr 30, 2025.
tldr: This paper presents the 2022 CODATA recommended values of fundamental physical constants based on a least-squares adjustment of all available data.
motivation: Accurate and consistent values of fundamental constants are essential for science and technology, requiring periodic updates as new measurements become available.
method: A least-squares adjustment is performed on a global dataset of measurements, taking into account correlations and uncertainties to produce self-consistent constant values.
result: The 2022 set of recommended values for fundamental constants and conversion factors is provided, with improved precision over previous sets.
conclusion: The CODATA recommended values serve as the internationally accepted standard for fundamental constants, supporting research and applications across physics and chemistry.

title: Self-aligning Polar Active Matter
authors: Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, And Amir Shee
abstract:
Author(s): Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, and Amir Shee

What if active units could align–or even antialign–their orientation with their own velocity? This intriguing self-alignment property unlocks a spectrum of fascinating behaviors, from single self-propelled particles orbiting in harmonic traps to transformative collective phenomena like synchronized motion in dense or solid elastic assemblies. Unlike systems where units simply mimic their neighbors, self-alignment fundamentally reshapes how motion emerges, paving the way for groundbreaking discoveries in biology, smart materials, and robotics. This review uncovers the hidden power of self-alignment in active systems, introduces a unified mathematical and conceptual framework, explores existing models of self-alignment, and highlights its transformative impact on the study and real-world applications of active systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015007] Published Thu Mar 20, 2025.
tldr: A review of self-alignment in polar active matter, covering collective motion in biological and robotic systems.
motivation: To understand how self-alignment of active units with their velocity leads to novel collective behaviors.
method: Unified mathematical framework and review of existing models of self-alignment in active systems.
result: Self-alignment enables orbiting, synchronized motion, and emergent collective phenomena in dense assemblies.
conclusion: Self-alignment is a key mechanism for motion in active matter with applications in biology and robotics.

title: The Need For Optoacoustic Microscopy
authors: Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, And Vasilis Ntziachristos
abstract:
Author(s): Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, and Vasilis Ntziachristos

Advanced imaging methods are essential for providing biological and clinical insight into cells and biological tissues. Optoacoustic imaging is one such method in which cells or tissues absorb short laser pulses and the resulting rise in temperature creates tiny ultrasound waves that can be detected by ultrasonic detectors placed outside the specimen. This noninvasive technique has the ability to look at optical contrast that is millimeters and even centimeters deep with high resolution. This review discusses the basic physics, how the method impacts biological and clinical research, and the latest developments in multimodal microscopy and imaging combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015005] Published Tue Mar 04, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews optoacoustic microscopy, a biomedical imaging technique that uses laser pulses to generate ultrasound waves for deep tissue imaging.
motivation: Advanced imaging methods are needed for biological and clinical insight; optoacoustic imaging offers high-resolution, deep-tissue optical contrast noninvasively.
method: The review covers the basic physics of optoacoustic imaging, its impact on biological and clinical research, and recent developments in multimodal microscopy combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.
result: Optoacoustic microscopy enables imaging millimeters to centimeters deep with high resolution, providing optical contrast in biological tissues.
conclusion: Optoacoustic microscopy is a valuable tool for biological and clinical imaging, with ongoing developments in multimodal approaches.

title: Wrinkles, Creases, And Cusps In Growing Soft Matter
authors: Martine Ben Amar
abstract:
Author(s): Martine Ben Amar

The buckling of a material surface subject to compression or growth is a ubiquitous phenomenon, arising in materials science contexts such as the swelling of gels as well as in biological contexts such as morphogenesis and embryogenesis. A complete understanding of the creases and sharp cusps that commonly accompany buckling requires nonlinear elasticity theory. This review presents a modern treatment of the Biot instability, integrating many standard techniques of nonlinear physics and solid mechanics, such as bifurcation theory, conformal mapping, and
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015004] Published Mon Feb 24, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews nonlinear elasticity theory for buckling, creases, and cusps in growing soft matter, with applications in materials science and biology.
motivation: Understanding the formation of creases and cusps during buckling of soft materials is important for morphogenesis and gel swelling, but lacks a complete nonlinear theory.
method: The review integrates techniques from nonlinear physics and solid mechanics, including bifurcation theory, conformal mapping, and elliptic integrals, to analyze the Biot instability.
result: It provides a modern treatment of the Biot instability and explains how nonlinear elasticity leads to creases and sharp cusps.
conclusion: The paper consolidates standard nonlinear methods to describe buckling phenomena in soft matter, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

tldr: This paper proposes a method to generate zeptosecond gamma-ray pulses using FEL-driven microbunching and laser-Compton scattering.
motivation: The goal is to produce ultra-short, high-energy photon pulses for applications in ultrafast science and high-energy physics.
method: The approach synergistically exploits free-electron laser (FEL) microbunching and laser-Compton scattering to generate attosecond and zeptosecond pulse bursts.

authors: David Wright, Kalista Wayt, Jeffrey S. Hazboun, Xavier Siemens, Rutger van Haasteren, Levi Schult, And Stephen R. Taylor
abstract:

In 2023, after more than two decades of searching, pulsar timing array (PTA) collaborations around the world announced evidence for a stochastic gravitational wave background. It was quickly followed by work from the International Pulsar Timing Array (IPTA), demonstrating that the results of regiona…

tldr: This paper presents a new method for combining pulsar timing array data to detect a stochastic gravitational wave background.

authors: Ruirui Ma, Pengfei Liu, Liu Chen, Fulvio Zonca, And Zhiyong Qiu

motivation: Understanding radiation damage in tungsten is critical for fusion reactor design, as it is the primary plasma-facing material.

tldr: This paper studies velocity-independent dry friction on mica, realizing the ideal Amontons-Coulomb friction law.
motivation: Understanding the fundamental nature of friction, specifically whether the Amontons-Coulomb law holds exactly under certain conditions.

result: The frictional force is independent of sliding velocity, confirming the ideal Amontons-Coulomb behavior.
conclusion: The study provides a clean realization of velocity-independent friction, which is important for tribology but unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

tldr: This paper studies periodic gravitational lensing caused by oscillating boson stars, a topic in astrophysics.
motivation: To explore observable signatures of boson stars, which are hypothetical compact objects, through gravitational lensing.
method: The authors analyze the lensing properties of oscillating real-scalar boson stars, identifying an oscillating radial caustic and computing image-pair creation/annihilation.
result: They find that sources near the caustic produce periodic lensing events phase-locked to the boson star oscillation.
conclusion: Oscillating boson stars can generate unique periodic lensing signals that may be detectable in future observations.

result: The progenitor galaxy was identified, supporting the ejection scenario from a compact star-forming galaxy.

conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for turnkey generation of pure quartic solitons, which may enable practical microresonator-based frequency combs.

method: The study uses four-spacecraft Magnetospheric Multiscale (MMS) mission data to analyze in situ measurements of electron holes and their collisions.
result: Direct observations show that electron holes can either pass through each other or coalesce, depending on their relative velocities and amplitudes.

motivation: Understanding how eyeless mutants of Chlamydomonas can still exhibit phototaxis and sign reversal, which challenges the conventional role of the eyespot.

conclusion: Cell body lensing is sufficient to explain phototaxis in eyeless mutants, revealing an alternative mechanism for directional light sensing in algae.

result: The concept is proposed and described, but no experimental results are presented.
conclusion: The proposed source could facilitate future neutrino-mass experiments and precision spectroscopy.

title: Rheology Of Dense Vibrated Granular Flows: Nonmonotonic Response Controlled By Granular Temperature
authors: A. Plati, G. Petrillo, L. de Arcangelis, A. Gnoli, A. Puglisi, A. Sarracino, And E. Lippiello
abstract:
Author(s): A. Plati, G. Petrillo, L. de Arcangelis, A. Gnoli, A. Puglisi, A. Sarracino, and E. Lippiello

When subjected to vibrations, the effective viscosity of a granular medium depends heavily on both confining pressure and vibration parameters. In this work, experimentally calibrated discrete element simulations of a vane rheometer are used to provide a unified framework that reconciles experimental observations. The results show that confining pressure directly dictates the rheological response, while vibration effects are mediated by the granular temperature, which results from a balance between energy input and internal dissipation.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032010] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the rheology of dense vibrated granular flows, focusing on the nonmonotonic response controlled by granular temperature.
motivation: Understanding the effective viscosity of granular media under vibrations is important for industrial processes and geophysics, but experimental observations have been inconsistent.
method: The authors use experimentally calibrated discrete element simulations of a vane rheometer to model dense granular flows under vibration.
result: They find that confining pressure directly dictates the rheological response, while vibration effects are mediated by granular temperature, which arises from a balance between energy input and dissipation.
conclusion: The study provides a unified framework reconciling previous experimental observations on vibrated granular flows.

title: Constraints On The Thomson Optical Depth To The Cosmic Microwave Background From The Lyman-$α$ Forest
authors: Olga Garcia-Gallego, Vid Iršič, Martin G. Haehnelt, And James S. Bolton
abstract:
Author(s): Olga Garcia-Gallego, Vid Iršič, Martin G. Haehnelt, and James S. Bolton

The imprint of the thermal history of the intergalactic medium on the Lyman-alpha forest in the spectra of distant QSOs is used to constrain the Thomson optical depth to the cosmic microwave background (CMB). The analysis suggests a mild tension of high-resolution Lyman-alpha forest data with recently suggested large values of the optical depth to the CMB, in agreement with the direct measurements by the lanck satellite.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032009] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses Lyman-alpha forest data to constrain the Thomson optical depth to the CMB, a cosmological parameter.
motivation: The Thomson optical depth is a key cosmological parameter that affects CMB observations; recent measurements have shown tension, motivating independent constraints.
method: The authors analyze high-resolution Lyman-alpha forest spectra from distant QSOs to infer the thermal history of the intergalactic medium and thereby constrain the optical depth.
result: The analysis finds mild tension with large values of the optical depth, consistent with direct CMB measurements.
conclusion: Lyman-alpha forest data provide an independent constraint on the Thomson optical depth, supporting lower values.

title: Intermittency-driven Subcritical Fiber Breakage In Turbulence

Turbulence fragments slender fibers in oceans, process industries, and the atmosphere, shaping size spectra, transport, and impact. Mean-field estimates compare typical turbulent bending with a material failure threshold and predict a critical span below which fibers should be effectively unbreakabl…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033073] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies turbulence-induced fiber breakage in fluids, a problem in fluid dynamics and materials science.
motivation: Understanding how turbulence fragments slender fibers is important for predicting size spectra in oceans and industrial processes.
method: The author develops a theoretical model incorporating intermittency effects to estimate bending stresses and failure thresholds.
result: The model predicts a critical fiber span below which breakage is suppressed, revising mean-field estimates.
conclusion: Intermittency significantly influences fiber breakage, and the critical span is smaller than previously thought.

result: Detects first overtone and higher-order modes in the ringdown signal.

method: Combines quantitative experiments with theoretical modeling to study density-dependent reversal of migration direction.
result: Collective migration reversal is controlled by bacterial density and oxygen consumption dynamics.
conclusion: The feedback between metabolism and movement leads to unexpected collective behaviors in bacterial systems.

title: High-energy Emission From The Galactic Center
authors: Andrea Goldwurm, Maïca Clavel, Stefano Gabici, And Régis Terrier
abstract:
Author(s): Andrea Goldwurm, Maïca Clavel, Stefano Gabici, and Régis Terrier

In this review, the authors provide a comprehensive multiwavelength view of high-energy emission from the center of our Galaxy. This region contains the closest supermassive black hole to us, which offers the best studied galactic nucleus in the Universe, with its quiescent emission and accretion contrasted by flaring activity. The Galactic Center also hosts diverse compact sources, plasma bubbles, and x-ray chimneys, altogether forming a dense interacting molecular zone—a gigantic powerhouse in the Milky Way.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025006] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: A review of high-energy astrophysical emission from the Galactic Center, covering the supermassive black hole, compact sources, and plasma bubbles.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive multiwavelength view of the high-energy phenomena in the Galactic Center, which is the closest and best-studied galactic nucleus.
method: Review of observational data across multiple wavelengths, including X-ray, gamma-ray, and radio, summarizing key results from past and recent studies.
result: The Galactic Center exhibits a rich variety of high-energy emission processes, including quiescent and flaring accretion from Sgr A*, diffuse emission from plasma bubbles, and emission from compact sources.
conclusion: The Galactic Center is a unique laboratory for studying high-energy astrophysics, and future observations will further elucidate the underlying physical mechanisms.

title: Fundamentals Of Vacuum Breakdown In High-gradient Accelerator Structures
authors: Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, And Yinon Ashkenazy
abstract:
Author(s): Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, and Yinon Ashkenazy

Vacuum breakdown or arcing happens when a very strong electric field causes a metal surface in a vacuum to suddenly form plasma, allowing large electrical currents to flow. Breakdown can damage particle accelerators, fusion reactors, satellites, and x-ray devices, though it is useful in technologies like plasma thrusters. Scientists have studied this unpredictable and fast phenomenon for over a century. Recent advances in experiments and computer simulations now provide a coherent mechanistic picture: tiny surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles interact in complex ways to trigger breakdowns. These insights could improve high-power technologies and make advanced accelerators more reliable and efficient.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025004] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the physics of vacuum breakdown in high-gradient accelerator structures, focusing on the role of surface defects, electrical stress, and plasma formation.
motivation: Vacuum breakdown limits the performance of particle accelerators and other high-power devices; understanding its mechanism is crucial for improving reliability and efficiency.
method: The authors synthesize experimental observations and computer simulations to build a coherent mechanistic picture of the breakdown process.
result: They identify that tiny surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles interact in complex ways to trigger breakdowns.
conclusion: These insights can guide the design of more reliable high-power technologies and advanced accelerators.

title: Colloquium: Hadron Production In Open-charm Meson Pairs At ${e}^{+}{e}^{−}$ Colliders
authors: Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, And Yuanning Gao
abstract:
Author(s): Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, and Yuanning Gao

Hadron spectroscopy is a frontier of particle physics; searching for new hadrons is crucial for validating the theory of strong interaction (QCD). Investigating how charmonium, a bound state of charm and anticharm quarks, decays and searching for new charmoniumlike states yield valuable insights into strong interaction mechanisms, including quark confinement and gluon binding. Hadrons produced at e− collisions decaying to open-charm meson pairs are a primary source of experimental information for these investigations. This Colloquium reviews current progress from BARBAR, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII experiments. As BESIII accumulates high-precision data, it has emerged as the leading facility for measuring hadron production in charm-meson pair systems, and recent advances are highlighted.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021001] Published Fri Apr 03, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews hadron production in open-charm meson pairs at e+e- colliders, focusing on charmonium decays and new hadron searches.
motivation: Understanding strong interaction mechanisms such as quark confinement and gluon binding through charmonium decays and searches for new hadrons.
method: Review of experimental results from BaBar, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII on hadron production in e+e- collisions decaying to open-charm meson pairs.
result: Summarizes current progress and highlights recent advances from BESIII as the leading facility for such measurements.
conclusion: The study of open-charm meson pairs provides valuable insights into strong interaction mechanisms and hadron spectroscopy.

title: Colloquium: Planetary Radar At The Arecibo Observatory
authors: Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, And Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín
abstract:
Author(s): Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, and Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín

For more than two decades, the planetary radar installed at the Arecibo Telescope was the most sensitive instrument of its kind, harnessing the penetrating power of radio waves to perform observations of the (sub)surface of planets, moons, and asteroids in the Solar System—providing a unique perspective on those bodies that helped to drive in situ exploration. This Colloquium presents an overview of the scientific legacy of the Arecibo radar system, focusing on the period posterior to the Gregorian Update in the late 1990s until the unexpected demise of the telescope in 2020. After recalling the basics of planetary radar techniques, it reviews key Arecibo observations of Mercury, Venus, Mars, our Moon, and the Saturn system, and highlights its essential role in the characterization of a large sample of near-Earth asteroids and comets.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011003] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This colloquium reviews the scientific legacy of planetary radar observations at the Arecibo Observatory, focusing on Solar System bodies.
motivation: Planetary radar provides unique subsurface and surface information about planets, moons, and asteroids, complementing in situ exploration.
method: The paper summarizes radar techniques and reviews key Arecibo observations of Mercury, Venus, Mars, the Moon, Saturn system, and near-Earth asteroids.
result: Arecibo's radar system was the most sensitive of its kind, enabling detailed characterization of many Solar System objects.
conclusion: The Arecibo radar system made significant contributions to planetary science, and its loss is a major setback for the field.

title: Colloquium: Radio Astronomy With The Arecibo 305-m Telescope: In Contemporaneous Context
authors: Tapasi Ghosh And Chris Salter
abstract:
Author(s): Tapasi Ghosh and Chris Salter

The Arecibo Observatory, inaugurated in 1963 as the world’s largest single-dish radio telescope, remained at the forefront of astronomy and atmospheric science for more than five decades, until its catastrophic collapse in December 2020. This Colloquium focuses on Arecibo’s enduring legacy in radio astronomy, offering a historical perspective that emphasizes how successive major upgrades of the telescope continuously expanded its observational capabilities and scientific impact. It presents Arecibo’s most influential contributions in topics as diverse as pulsar studies, the mapping of neutral hydrogen (HI) in the Milky Way and other galaxies, the characterization of the interstellar medium, the imaging of extragalactic radio sources with very long baseline interferometry (VLBI), the search for extraterrestrial intelligence (SETI), and being a major contributor to the first-ever detection of a stochastic gravitational-wave background.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011004] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: A historical review of the Arecibo radio telescope's contributions to radio astronomy and atmospheric science.
motivation: To document the legacy of the Arecibo Observatory and its impact on various fields of astronomy.
method: Historical narrative and review of key scientific achievements enabled by successive upgrades of the telescope.
result: Arecibo made influential contributions to pulsar studies, HI mapping, VLBI, SETI, and gravitational-wave detection.
conclusion: The Arecibo telescope was a transformative instrument whose legacy continues to influence radio astronomy.

title: Colloquium: Geospace Pathfinder Science At Arecibo Observatory
authors: J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, And Shikha Raizada
abstract:
Author(s): J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, and Shikha Raizada

The Arecibo Observatory housed the largest single-aperture radio telescope for approximately 50 years. A major scientific focus was studying the upper atmosphere; its highly sensitive radar facility, combined with lidars, optical sensors, and satellite-based systems, enabled unprecedented studies of ionospheric physics based on incoherent scattering of radio waves off free electrons. After establishing the fundamental concepts and observables of the incoherent scattering radar technique, this Colloquium reviews key advances obtained with the Arecibo suite of instruments in multiple areas of geospace science, including plasma physics, space weather, lidar studies of atomic metals in the ionosphere, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011005] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews geospace science advances using the Arecibo Observatory's radar and lidar instruments, focusing on ionospheric physics and space weather.
motivation: The Arecibo Observatory's unique capabilities for studying the upper atmosphere are highlighted, aiming to summarize key scientific contributions over its lifetime.
method: The paper is a colloquium-style review, synthesizing results from incoherent scatter radar, lidar, and optical measurements at Arecibo.
result: Key advances in plasma physics, space weather, metal layers in the ionosphere, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling are presented.
conclusion: The Arecibo Observatory has been instrumental in geospace science, and its legacy continues through ongoing data analysis and future collaborations.

title: Colloquium: Multimessenger Astronomy With Continuous Gravitational Waves And Future Detectors
authors: Benjamin J. Owen
abstract:
Author(s): Benjamin J. Owen

The search for continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars represents a key frontier of gravitational-wave astrophysics, with strong connections to electromagnetic astronomy, nuclear astrophysics, and condensed matter physics. This Colloquium discusses the detection prospects for these long-lived yet elusive signals in the upcoming generation of gravitational-wave detectors, emphasizing the importance of simultaneous electromagnetic observations. It also surveys the potential implications of such multimessenger observations for our understanding of the physical and astrophysical processes taking place in the extremely dense environments of their sources.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011002] Published Tue Mar 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper discusses the prospects for detecting continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars and the implications for multimessenger astronomy.
motivation: Continuous gravitational waves are a key frontier in gravitational-wave astrophysics, with connections to electromagnetic astronomy, nuclear astrophysics, and condensed matter physics.
method: The paper reviews detection prospects for upcoming gravitational-wave detectors and emphasizes the importance of simultaneous electromagnetic observations.
result: It surveys potential implications for understanding physical and astrophysical processes in dense environments.
conclusion: Multimessenger observations combining gravitational and electromagnetic data will enhance our understanding of neutron star interiors and related physics.

title: Colloquium: Convection-cloud Chambers: Experiment And Theory
authors: Steven Krueger And Raymond A. Shaw
abstract:
Author(s): Steven Krueger and Raymond A. Shaw

In warm clouds, drops grow into raindrops through both condensation and collision coalescence, but the observed rapid transition between these mechanisms remains difficult to theoretically explain. The convection-cloud chamber, which reproduces key phenomena such as turbulent fluctuations in droplet concentrations and supersaturation under controlled laboratory conditions, offers a promising approach to addressing this long-standing bottleneck in understanding in cloud physics. This Colloquium reviews the physics underlying the precipitation bottleneck, examines how convection-cloud chambers capture the essential processes, and synthesizes insights from experiments, theory, and computational models that bridge laboratory and atmospheric scales.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011001] Published Wed Feb 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews convection-cloud chambers as a laboratory tool to study the precipitation bottleneck in warm clouds.
motivation: Understanding the rapid transition from condensation to collision-coalescence in warm clouds is a long-standing problem in cloud physics.
method: The authors review experimental, theoretical, and computational studies using convection-cloud chambers that reproduce key cloud phenomena under controlled conditions.
result: Convection-cloud chambers can capture turbulent fluctuations in droplet concentrations and supersaturation, providing insights into the precipitation bottleneck.
conclusion: The convection-cloud chamber is a promising approach to bridge laboratory and atmospheric scales for understanding warm rain formation.

title: Colloquium: Gravitational Waves From Neutrino-driven Core Collapse Supernovae
authors: A. Mezzacappa And M. Zanolin
abstract:
Author(s): A. Mezzacappa and M. Zanolin

The observation of a core collapse supernova explosion of (near-)Galactic origin would constitute a landmark, once-in-a-century event for multimessenger astronomy, eagerly awaited by observers and modelers alike. The detection of gravitational waves, along with photons and neutrinos, from such an event would provide unique insights into the supernova central engine and the physics of the newly forming neutron star. This Colloquium presents the latest progress in core collapse supernova modeling and the associated gravitational wave signal predictions. It also provides an overview of the specific methods of detection and physical parameter estimation that can be implemented for such signals in ground-based laser interferometers, in the context of multimessenger research strategies.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041002] Published Tue Dec 30, 2025.
tldr: This colloquium reviews gravitational wave signals from core collapse supernovae and their detection.
motivation: Observing a Galactic core collapse supernova would be a landmark event for multimessenger astronomy, providing insights into the supernova engine and neutron star physics.
method: The paper summarizes latest progress in supernova modeling and gravitational wave signal predictions, and discusses detection methods and parameter estimation for ground-based laser interferometers.
result: The review presents current understanding of gravitational wave signatures from core collapse supernovae and the status of detection strategies.
conclusion: Gravitational wave detection from a nearby supernova, combined with photons and neutrinos, will offer unique multimessenger insights.

title: Colloquium: The Cosmic Dipole Anomaly
authors: Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, And Subir Sarkar
abstract:
Author(s): Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, and Subir Sarkar

The cosmological principle, which states that the Universe must be statistically isotropic and homogeneous on large scales, is a foundational principle of the standard model of cosmology, known as lambda cold dark matter (ΛCDM). The validity of this principle can be tested by assessing the compatibility of a dipole anisotropy in the large-scale distribution of matter with the dipole observed in the cosmic microwave background, interpreted in the ΛCDM model as due to our local peculiar motion. This Colloquium describes the methodology for such a test and presents its outcome based on the analysis of recent large catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars, revealing a significant inconsistency between the two dipoles. The authors review these recent findings, as well as potential biases, systematic issues, and alternate interpretations, and discuss how this anomaly could challenge the standard description of our Universe based on the ΛCDM model.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041001] Published Thu Dec 11, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the cosmic dipole anomaly, testing the cosmological principle by comparing the dipole in the large-scale matter distribution with the CMB dipole.
motivation: The cosmological principle is a foundational assumption of the standard ΛCDM model, and its validity can be tested by comparing the dipole anisotropy in galaxy catalogs with the CMB dipole.
method: The authors analyze recent large catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars to measure the dipole in the matter distribution and compare it with the CMB dipole, accounting for potential biases and systematic effects.
result: A significant inconsistency is found between the two dipoles, challenging the standard interpretation that the CMB dipole is due to our local peculiar motion.
conclusion: The cosmic dipole anomaly may indicate a violation of the cosmological principle or require modifications to the standard ΛCDM model.

title: Astrophysical Tests Of Dark Matter Self-interactions
authors: Susmita Adhikari, Arka Banerjee, Kimberly K. Boddy, Francis-Yan Cyr-Racine, Harry Desmond, Cora Dvorkin, Bhuvnesh Jain, Felix Kahlhoefer, Manoj Kaplinghat, Anna Nierenberg, Annika H. G. Peter, Andrew Robertson, Jeremy Sakstein, And Jesús Zavala
abstract:
Author(s): Susmita Adhikari, Arka Banerjee, Kimberly K. Boddy, Francis-Yan Cyr-Racine, Harry Desmond, Cora Dvorkin, Bhuvnesh Jain, Felix Kahlhoefer, Manoj Kaplinghat, Anna Nierenberg, Annika H. G. Peter, Andrew Robertson, Jeremy Sakstein, and Jesús Zavala

Dark sectors, involving new particles that couple very weakly to the standard model ones, play an important role in current model-building efforts in particle physics, as they allow, for example, for new dark matter production and interaction mechanisms. This review focuses on self-interacting dark matter scenarios, their implications on the dynamics and distribution of dark matter halos in the Universe, and the related astrophysical tests and observations, from galaxies to large-scale structures. It is embedded in the framework of the Novel Probes Project, a forum connecting observers and theorists involved in the study of astrophysical tests of dark-sector interactions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045004] Published Mon Dec 08, 2025.
tldr: A review of astrophysical tests of self-interacting dark matter, focusing on dark matter halo dynamics and large-scale structure.
motivation: To understand the implications of self-interacting dark matter scenarios on cosmic structure formation and to summarize observational tests.
method: Review of theoretical models and observational data from galaxies to large-scale structures, within the Novel Probes Project framework.
result: Summarizes current constraints on dark matter self-interaction cross-sections from astrophysical observations.
conclusion: Self-interacting dark matter remains a viable candidate, with ongoing and future observations expected to provide tighter constraints.

title: Prospects For Supersymmetry At High-Luminosity Lhc
authors: Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, And Kairui Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, and Kairui Zhang

Supersymmetry remains one of the leading candidates for physics beyond the standard model, offering a compelling framework to address the hierarchy of scales. Its theoretical appeal has inspired decades of intensive model building and experimental searches. Recent results have placed stringent bounds on the supersymmetric parameter space, sharpening the focus on the remaining viable models. This review surveys the current status and outlook for supersymmetry in light of experimental constraints and recent theoretical developments, and presents projections for the discovery potential of the High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider across multiple search channels and a variety of well-motivated scenarios.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045001] Published Fri Oct 17, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the prospects for supersymmetry at the High-Luminosity LHC, focusing on experimental searches and model constraints.
motivation: Supersymmetry is a leading candidate for physics beyond the Standard Model, but recent experimental results have constrained its parameter space. The paper aims to survey the current status and future discovery potential.
method: The authors review theoretical developments and experimental constraints, and project discovery potential across multiple search channels at the HL-LHC.
result: The paper provides an overview of viable supersymmetric models and their expected signatures at the HL-LHC.
conclusion: Supersymmetry remains a compelling framework, and the HL-LHC offers significant discovery potential for well-motivated scenarios.

title: Solar Fusion Iii: New Data And Theory For Hydrogen-burning Stars
authors: B. Acharya et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): B. Acharya et al.

Approximately 90% of the stars in the Milky Way are on the main sequence, fusing hydrogen into helium through a network of nuclear reactions. This includes the nearest star, our Sun. A precise understanding of hydrogen burning is crucial to predicting its luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology. This review describes the theoretical and experimental work of the last decade that has advanced our understanding of the nuclear physics of hydrogen burning. It describes the plasma and atomic physics that influences the solar environment in which the nuclear reactions take place, as well as the diagnostics probes—including solar neutrinos and helioseismology—that allow us to test our resulting model of the solar interior.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035002] Published Thu Sep 04, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews nuclear physics of hydrogen burning in stars, focusing on solar fusion and neutrino production.
motivation: Understanding hydrogen burning is crucial for predicting stellar luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology.
method: The review summarizes theoretical and experimental advances in nuclear reaction rates, plasma physics, and solar modeling.
result: Updated nuclear reaction rates and improved solar models are presented, with implications for neutrino fluxes and helioseismology.
conclusion: The paper provides a comprehensive update on hydrogen-burning nuclear physics, but does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Gas Bubble Dynamics
authors: Dominique Legendre And Roberto Zenit
abstract:
Author(s): Dominique Legendre and Roberto Zenit

The motion of gas bubbles in liquids plays a vital role in numerous natural, industrial, and everyday phenomena. Unlike solid particles, gas bubbles are nearly weightless and highly responsive to forces from the surrounding fluid. Their dynamics are affected by added mass acceleration and deformable surfaces, and also by interactions with turbulent flows, other bubbles, and walls, with liquid rheology and surfactants further influencing their behavior. This review examines the intricate behavior of noncondensable gas bubbles, highlighting key advances over the past 20 years. Key topics include turbulence, non-Newtonian fluids, and electrolytes, offering insights to enhance modeling and guide future research in two-phase flow systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025001] Published Thu Apr 17, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the dynamics of gas bubbles in liquids, covering turbulence, non-Newtonian fluids, and electrolytes.
motivation: Understanding gas bubble dynamics is crucial for many natural and industrial processes, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The review synthesizes advances over the past 20 years, focusing on key topics like turbulence and non-Newtonian effects.
result: Key insights include the influence of added mass, deformable surfaces, and interactions with turbulence and surfactants.
conclusion: The review provides a comprehensive overview to enhance modeling and guide future research in two-phase flow systems.
